rules.atomic_rule: Every person has a right to inspect any public record; the right to request/inspect is not limited to residents, citizens, or an enumerated class of requesters.
rules.source_language: Public records are open to inspection at all times during the office hours of a state or local agency and every person has a right to inspect any public record, except as otherwise provided.
rules.trigger: Any person makes a records request
rules.legal_concept: Public right of access to public records
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. Source Type: Statute. Reinforced by § 7922.530(a) ('shall make the records promptly available to any person').
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by Stats. 2024, Ch. 80 (SB 1525), eff. Jan 1, 2025)

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not condition or limit access to an otherwise-disclosable public record based on the purpose for which the record is requested; requesters need not state a reason.
rules.source_language: This division does not allow limitations on access to a public record based upon the purpose for which the record is being requested, if the record is otherwise subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.legal_concept: Purpose-neutral access
rules.notes: Universal-access fact per shared key. Purpose may still be VOLUNTARILY stated to aid identification (§ 7922.600(a)(1)), but cannot be required. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Records must be made available to any person; there is no residency, citizenship, or in-state requirement to request records.
rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Any person requests a copy of records
rules.legal_concept: Any-person access, no residency limitation
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared key even though 'no residency' is expressed by the absence of any residency clause and the 'any person' language. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The CPRA applies to a 'local agency,' which includes a county; a city (general law or chartered); a city and county; a school district; a municipal corporation; a district; a political subdivision; any board/commission/agency of the foregoing; and other local public agencies.
rules.source_language: As used in this division, "local agency" includes any of the following: (a) A county. (b) A city, whether general law or chartered. (c) A city and county. (d) A school district. (e) A municipal corporation. (f) A district. (g) A political subdivision. (h) Any board, commission, or agency of the foregoing. (i) Another local public agency. (j) An entity that is a legislative body of a local agency pursuant to subdivision (c) or (d) of Section 54952.
rules.trigger: Request directed to a local public body
rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'local agency' (coverage scope)
rules.notes: Software branches on this to confirm the receiving body is CPRA-covered. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A 'public record' is any writing containing information relating to the conduct of the public's business prepared, owned, used, or retained by any state or local agency, regardless of physical form or characteristics.
rules.source_language: As used in this division, "public records" includes any writing containing information relating to the conduct of the public's business prepared, owned, used, or retained by any state or local agency regardless of physical form or characteristics.
rules.trigger: Determining whether requested material is a record
rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public records'
rules.notes: Software branches on this to classify whether the request seeks a covered record. Subdivision (b) adds a date floor for Governor's-office records (not municipal). Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A copy request must reasonably describe an identifiable record or records before the duty to produce attaches.
rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Request received; agency assesses whether it identifies records
rules.legal_concept: Reasonably-describes-identifiable-record threshold
rules.notes: 'Reasonably describes an identifiable record' is a soft standard; a request failing it triggers the agency assistance/clarification duty (CA-0007) rather than immediate denial. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: To assist the requester in making a focused, effective request, the agency shall (to the extent reasonable) help identify responsive records, describe the information technology and physical location where records exist, and suggest ways to overcome any practical basis for denying access.
rules.source_language: When a member of the public requests to inspect a public record or obtain a copy of a public record, the public agency, in order to assist the member of the public make a focused and effective request that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall do all of the following, to the extent reasonable under the circumstances: (1) Assist the member of the public to identify records and information that are responsive to the request or to the purpose of the request, if stated. (2) Describe the information technology and physical location in which the records exist. (3) Provide suggestions for overcoming any practical basis for denying access to the records or information sought.
rules.trigger: Request is unclear or does not identify records
rules.legal_concept: Agency duty to assist requester
rules.notes: Structural clarification stage. No statutory tolling of the 10-day clock is attached to clarification. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The agency's duty to help identify responsive records is deemed satisfied if it cannot identify the requested information after making a reasonable effort to elicit additional clarifying information from the requester.
rules.source_language: The requirements of paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) shall be deemed to have been satisfied if the public agency is unable to identify the requested information after making a reasonable effort to elicit additional clarifying information from the requester that will help identify the record or records.
rules.trigger: Agency makes reasonable effort to elicit clarification but cannot identify records
rules.legal_concept: Safe-harbor for unmet clarification
rules.notes: Not a formal abandonment/closure trigger; it discharges the assistance duty in subd. (a)(1) only. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 days of receiving a copy request, the agency must determine whether it seeks disclosable public records in its possession and promptly notify the requester of the determination and the reasons.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 10 days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Each agency, upon a request for a copy of records, shall, within 10 days from receipt of the request, determine whether the request, in whole or in part, seeks copies of disclosable public records in the possession of the agency and shall promptly notify the person making the request of the determination and the reasons therefor.
rules.trigger: Agency receives a copy request
rules.legal_concept: 10-day determination deadline
rules.notes: State fixes the value at 10 days (config_home=parameter, constraint_basis=fixed — city does not choose the number). Counted in calendar days; interacts with holiday/weekend rollover under general time-computation rules. This is a DETERMINATION deadline, not a deadline to produce records. Source Type: Statute.
rules.effective_status: Current (amended by AB 370, Stats. 2025, Ch. 34, eff. Jan 1, 2026)

rules.atomic_rule: The agency must promptly notify the requester of its determination and the reasons therefor.
rules.source_language: Each agency, upon a request for a copy of records, shall, within 10 days from receipt of the request, determine whether the request, in whole or in part, seeks copies of disclosable public records in the possession of the agency and shall promptly notify the person making the request of the determination and the reasons therefor.
rules.trigger: Agency completes its 10-day determination
rules.legal_concept: Determination notice
rules.notes: Structural notice tied to the CA-0009 deadline. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: If the agency determines the request seeks disclosable public records, it must also state the estimated date and time when the records will be made available.
rules.source_language: If the agency determines that the request seeks disclosable public records, the agency shall also state the estimated date and time when the records will be made available.
rules.trigger: Determination is that records are disclosable
rules.legal_concept: Estimated-availability-date notice
rules.notes: The estimated date/time is set by the agency per-request (not a statute-fixed number), so it is a structural commitment the engine records, not a parameter. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: In unusual circumstances the determination time limit may be extended by written notice, but not by more than 14 days.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 14 additional days beyond the 10-day determination deadline; requires written extension notice
rules.source_language: In unusual circumstances, the time limit prescribed in this article and Article 1 (commencing with Section 7922.500) may be extended by written notice from the head of the agency or a designee to the person making the request, setting forth the reasons for the extension and the date on which a determination is expected to be dispatched. The notice shall not specify a date that would result in an extension for more than 14 days.
rules.trigger: 'Unusual circumstances' (defined in § 7922.535(c)) exist
rules.legal_concept: 14-day extension of the determination deadline
rules.notes: Ceiling: statute caps the extension at 14 days; the actual extension date is chosen per-request by the agency within that cap. 'Unusual circumstances' are exhaustively defined in subd. (c) (field-facility search; voluminous records; interagency/intra-agency consultation; data compilation/programming; cyberattack access loss; gubernatorial-emergency staffing/closure). Source Type: Statute.
rules.effective_status: Current (unusual-circumstances list expanded by AB 370, eff. Jan 1, 2026)

rules.atomic_rule: An extension of the determination deadline is valid only if made by written notice from the agency head or designee, setting forth the reasons for the extension and the date a determination is expected to be dispatched.
rules.source_language: In unusual circumstances, the time limit prescribed in this article and Article 1 (commencing with Section 7922.500) may be extended by written notice from the head of the agency or a designee to the person making the request, setting forth the reasons for the extension and the date on which a determination is expected to be dispatched. The notice shall not specify a date that would result in an extension for more than 14 days.
rules.trigger: Agency invokes an unusual-circumstances extension
rules.legal_concept: Written extension notice
rules.notes: Structural notice that must accompany any CA-0012 extension. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Once a disclosable copy request is made, the agency must make the records promptly available (a soft-standard production deadline distinct from the 10-day determination).
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt / upon payment of duplication fees
rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Disclosable copy request received and fees paid
rules.legal_concept: Prompt production of copies
rules.notes: 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard — config_home=structural, no invented day-count. Distinct from the CA-0009 10-day DETERMINATION clock: the 10 days is to decide, production may take longer per the CA-0011 estimated date. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Public records are open to inspection at all times during the office hours of the agency.
rules.source_language: Public records are open to inspection at all times during the office hours of a state or local agency and every person has a right to inspect any public record, except as otherwise provided.
rules.trigger: Person seeks to inspect during office hours
rules.legal_concept: Inspection during office hours
rules.notes: Inspection (as opposed to copies) is not subject to the duplication-cost fee, which by its terms attaches only to copies (§ 7922.530(a)). Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A requester inspecting disclosable records on agency premises may use their own equipment to photograph or copy records without physical contact, unless doing so would damage the record or gain unauthorized access to agency systems; the agency may set reasonable equipment-use limits.
rules.source_language: A requester inspecting disclosable records on agency premises may use their own equipment to photograph or copy records in a manner that does not require the equipment to make physical contact with the record, unless doing so would damage the record or result in unauthorized access to the agency's computer systems or secured networks.
rules.trigger: Requester inspects records on premises and wishes to self-copy
rules.legal_concept: Requester self-copying with own device
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the WebFetch returned subd. (b)-(c) partly in summary form; the (b)(2) 'unauthorized access' clause and the subd. (c) reasonable-limits language should be re-verified verbatim before reliance. Operationally: agency must permit no-contact self-copying subject to reasonable protective limits. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: If information constituting a non-exempt identifiable public record is held in an electronic format, the agency must make it available in an electronic format when requested by any person.
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise prohibited by law, any agency that has information that constitutes an identifiable public record not exempt from disclosure pursuant to this division that is in an electronic format shall make that information available in an electronic format when requested by any person.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for electronic-format record that agency holds electronically
rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format availability
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The agency must make the information available in any electronic format in which it holds the information, and must provide a copy in the requested format if that format is one the agency has used to create copies for its own use or for other agencies.
rules.source_language: (1) The agency shall make the information available in any electronic format in which it holds the information. (2) The agency shall provide a copy of an electronic record in the format requested if the requested format is one that the agency has used to create copies for its own use or for provision to other agencies.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies an electronic format
rules.legal_concept: Format-of-production choice
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy a records-posting/production obligation by maintaining the record on its website and directing the requester there, but must promptly provide a copy if the requester cannot access or reproduce the record from the website.
rules.source_language: [Subd. (a)] a public agency may comply by posting the record on its internet website and directing the member of the public to the location on the website; [Subd. (b)] if the requester is unable to access or reproduce the record from the website, the agency shall promptly provide a copy of the public record pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 7922.530.
rules.trigger: Requested record is available on the agency website
rules.legal_concept: Website-posting production alternative
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: WebFetch returned this section in summary form; re-verify verbatim before reliance. Operational fork: website-redirect path vs. direct-copy fallback. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record must be made available after deletion of the portions that are exempt by law.
rules.source_language: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record shall be available for inspection by any person requesting the record after deletion of the portions that are exempted by law.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and non-exempt content
rules.legal_concept: Segregability / redact-and-release
rules.notes: Structural redaction step preventing whole-record withholding when segregation is reasonable. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies of records are limited to fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies.
rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks copies (not mere inspection)
rules.legal_concept: Direct-cost-of-duplication fee limit
rules.notes: Ceiling: the state caps fees at 'direct costs of duplication' (or a separately-authorized statutory fee); the city sets the actual per-copy amount under that ceiling — do not split fixed vs. ceiling into separate concepts. No statewide cents-per-page number exists. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The cost of duplicating an electronic record is limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of the record in an electronic format.
rules.source_language: The cost of duplication of an electronic record pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 7922.570 shall be limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of a record in an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks an electronic-format copy
rules.legal_concept: Direct-cost limit for electronic copies
rules.notes: Ceiling: city sets the actual electronic-duplication charge under the 'direct cost' cap. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: The requester bears the cost of producing a copy (including the cost to construct a record and the cost of programming and computer services) when the electronic record is produced only at regularly scheduled intervals, or when the request requires data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding subdivision (a), the requester shall bear the cost of producing a copy of the record, including the cost to construct a record, and the cost of programming and computer services necessary to produce a copy of the record when either of the following applies: (1) In order to comply with subdivisions (a) and (b) of Section 7922.570, the public agency would be required to produce a copy of an electronic record and the record is one that is produced only at otherwise regularly scheduled intervals. (2) The request would require data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
rules.trigger: Electronic record is produced only at scheduled intervals, OR request requires data compilation/extraction/programming
rules.legal_concept: Cost-shift for constructed/extracted electronic records
rules.notes: A conditional branch, not a city-set value, so config_home=structural. This is the narrow exception to the direct-cost ceiling in CA-0022. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: For ordinary production of electronic records, an agency may not charge for the ancillary staff time of searching for and redacting/reviewing records; such time is chargeable only within the narrow data-extraction cost-shift of Section 7922.575(b) (i.e., where extraction/programming or interval-only production applies).
rules.source_language: Under section 6253.9, subdivision (b) [now § 7922.575(b)], the cost of 'data compilation, extraction, or programming' recoverable from a requester does not include the ancillary tasks of searching for, or redacting, otherwise-disclosable electronic records; those tasks must be borne by the agency except in the two circumstances the statute specifies.
rules.source_authority: National Lawyers Guild, S.F. Bay Area Chapter v. City of Hayward (2020) 9 Cal.5th 488 (Appellate/Supreme Court Decision)
rules.trigger: Request for electronic records requiring redaction or search time
rules.legal_concept: Scope of recoverable electronic-production costs
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true and REQUIRES MANUAL LEGAL REVIEW: holding stated from memory of the California Supreme Court opinion; the operative holding language was not opened this pass. Included because it changes fee behavior (bars charging redaction/search time as 'extraction'). Interprets § 7922.575(b) (former § 6253.9(b)). Source Type: Appellate Decision.
rules.effective_status: Current (requires manual verification of quoted holding)

rules.atomic_rule: The agency's duty is to make copies available upon payment of the duplication fees, permitting the agency to condition release of copies on payment.
rules.source_language: ...shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
rules.trigger: Copies are ready and a duplication fee is owed
rules.legal_concept: Payment as condition of copy release
rules.notes: 'Upon payment' gates release of copies (structural precondition); statute does not authorize an advance-deposit/estimate scheme for ordinary requests. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A response to a written request that includes a determination denying the request, in whole or in part, must be in writing.
rules.source_language: A response to a written request for inspection or copies of public records that includes a determination that the request is denied, in whole or in part, shall be in writing.
rules.trigger: Written request is denied in whole or in part
rules.legal_concept: Written denial requirement
rules.notes: Written-response duty attaches to WRITTEN requests. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: A notification of denial must set forth the names and titles or positions of each person responsible for the denial.
rules.source_language: The notification of denial shall set forth the names and titles or positions of each person responsible for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency issues a denial notification
rules.legal_concept: Responsible-person disclosure in denial
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency must justify withholding any record by demonstrating that it is exempt under an express provision of the CPRA, or that on the facts of the particular case the public interest served by nondisclosure clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure.
rules.source_language: An agency shall justify withholding any record by demonstrating that the record in question is exempt under express provisions of this division, or that on the facts of the particular case the public interest served by not disclosing the record clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure of the record.
rules.trigger: Agency withholds a record or portion
rules.legal_concept: Withholding justification standard (express exemption or public-interest balancing)
rules.notes: The public-interest 'catch-all' balancing test requires human legal review; do not automate the balancing. § 7922.540(c) cross-references this section as the justification each denial must meet. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Any person may institute a proceeding for injunctive or declaratory relief, or a writ of mandate, in any court of competent jurisdiction, to enforce the right to inspect or receive a copy of public records.
rules.source_language: Any person may institute a proceeding for injunctive or declarative relief, or for a writ of mandate, in any court of competent jurisdiction, to enforce that person's right under this division to inspect or receive a copy of any public record or class of public records.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to enforce access rights after denial or non-response
rules.legal_concept: Judicial enforcement (mandate / injunctive / declaratory relief)
rules.notes: California provides ONLY a judicial enforcement path — namespaced appeal.judicial.*. There is NO statutory administrative appeal or AG-review stage (see material negatives). Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Nothing in the CPRA may be construed to permit an agency to delay or obstruct the inspection or copying of public records.
rules.source_language: Nothing in this division shall be construed to permit an agency to delay or obstruct the inspection or copying of public records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.legal_concept: No-delay / no-obstruction mandate
rules.notes: Operative anti-delay standard underpinning the promptness duties; the engine must not encode workflow states that stall access. Source Type: Statute.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not allow another party to control the disclosure of information that is otherwise subject to disclosure under the CPRA.
rules.source_language: A state or local agency may not allow another party to control the disclosure of information that is otherwise subject to disclosure pursuant to this division.
rules.trigger: A third party (e.g., contractor or record submitter) asserts control over disclosure
rules.legal_concept: No third-party control over disclosure
rules.notes: Affects routing/decisioning: the agency cannot defer the disclosure decision to a third party. Source Type: Statute.

structural_branches.description: Mandatory 10-day determination stage: agency issues a notice stating whether the request seeks disclosable records and the reasons (§ 7922.535(a)).
When records are disclosable, the agency commits to a per-request 'estimated date and time' of availability — a stored commitment the engine tracks, not a fixed value (§ 7922.535(a)).
Optional unusual-circumstances extension branch: written notice from agency head/designee stating reasons and the expected determination date, capped at +14 days (§ 7922.535(b)).
Soft-standard production deadline ('promptly') distinct from the determination clock — engine applies a standard, not a city-entered number (§ 7922.530(a)).
Website-posting production alternative with a direct-copy fallback when the requester cannot access/reproduce from the site (§ 7922.545).
On-premises inspection branch permitting requester no-contact self-copying with their own equipment, subject to reasonable agency limits (§ 7922.530(b)-(c)).
Redact-and-release step: reasonably segregable non-exempt portions must be produced after deleting exempt portions (§ 7922.525(b)).
Conditional fee-shift branch where interval-only production or data compilation/extraction/programming moves construction/programming costs to the requester (§ 7922.575(b)).
Withholding-justification decision requiring either an express exemption or a case-specific public-interest balancing test (the latter needs human legal review) (§ 7922.000).
California's sole review path is judicial: writ of mandate / injunctive / declaratory relief in court — there is no administrative appeal stage (§ 7923.000).

material_negatives.note: No statutory administrative appeal or AG-review stage exists in the CPRA. Enforcement is exclusively judicial (§ 7923.000). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists in local ordinance, but the state statute provides none.

No explicit statutory 'deemed denial' / constructive-denial clock (e.g., 'silence for N days = denial'). Failure to meet the 10-day determination duty exposes the agency to judicial enforcement but the statute does not convert silence into an automatic denial with a terminal clock.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. The statute caps fees at 'direct costs of duplication' (§ 7922.530(a)); the city supplies the actual value under that ceiling. (Some jurisdictions and courts treat ~$0.10-0.25/page as within direct cost, but that is not a statewide statutory number.)

No statutory required request form, and no requirement that a request be in writing to trigger the access right (inspection may be requested orally). A WRITTEN request is what triggers the written-denial duties of § 7922.540 — but writing is not a precondition to access itself.
No separate mandatory acknowledgment deadline distinct from the 10-day determination. The 10-day determination under § 7922.535(a) is the only intake-side statutory clock.

No statutory advance-deposit or fee-estimate-and-hold scheme for ordinary requests; the statute conditions copy release on 'payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication' (§ 7922.530(a)) but does not authorize a deposit process.

No explicit statutory tolling or pausing of the 10-day determination clock while the agency seeks clarification. The assistance duty (§ 7922.600) exists but carries no attached toll of the § 7922.535 deadline.

No numeric statutory deadline for actual PRODUCTION of records; production is governed by the soft 'promptly' standard (§ 7922.530(a)) and the agency's self-set 'estimated date' (§ 7922.535(a)), not a fixed day-count.

rules.legal_concept: Right of access on application by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may apply to the officer for public information and the officer shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both.
rules.trigger: A person applies to the officer for public information.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared-key mandate.

rules.legal_concept: No inquiry into purpose
rules.atomic_rule: The governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which the requested information will be used.
rules.trigger: A request is received (may accompany a permitted clarification).
rules.source_language: If a large amount of information has been requested, the governmental body may discuss with the requestor how the scope of a request might be narrowed, but the governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which information will be used.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as rule with shared key.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency requirement; the right to request runs to 'any person' regardless of residence.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer.
rules.notes: No residency condition appears in the Act; inference from the 'any person' grant. Emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry, not as a material negative.

rules.legal_concept: Request from or about certain incarcerated individuals
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body is not required to accept or comply with a request from an incarcerated/confined individual or that individual's agent (other than the individual's attorney seeking disclosable information).
rules.trigger: Requestor is imprisoned/confined in a correctional facility, or is that individual's agent.
rules.source_language: A governmental body is not required to accept or comply with a request for information from: (1) an individual who is imprisoned or confined in a correctional facility; or (2) an agent of that individual, other than that individual's attorney when the attorney is requesting information that is subject to disclosure under this chapter.
rules.notes: Structural branch: engine must be able to decline/route these requests. 'Correctional facility' defined in § 552.028(c).

rules.legal_concept: Written request; permitted delivery methods
rules.atomic_rule: A request must be in writing and delivered by U.S. mail, e-mail, hand delivery, or another method the governmental body has approved (e.g., fax, submission through its website).
rules.trigger: A person seeks to invoke the Act.
rules.source_language: A person may make a written request for public information under this chapter only by delivering the request by one of the following methods to the applicable officer for public information or a person designated by that officer: (1) United States mail; (2) electronic mail; (3) hand delivery; or (4) any other appropriate method approved by the governmental body, including: (A) facsimile transmission; and (B) electronic submission through the governmental body's Internet website.
rules.notes: Approved method under (a)(4) is effective only if advertised on the § 552.205 sign or the body's website (§ 552.234(b)).

rules.legal_concept: Designated addresses for receiving requests
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body may designate one mailing address and one e-mail address for requests; if it posts/prints them, it need not respond to a request unless received at a designated address, by hand delivery, or by an approved (a)(4) method.
rules.trigger: Body designates and publishes addresses.
rules.source_language: A governmental body may designate one mailing address and one electronic mail address for receiving written requests for public information. The governmental body shall provide the designated mailing address and electronic mailing address to any person on request.
rules.notes: Drives routing/misdirected-request handling. Full (d) lists the three receipt channels that still bind the body.

rules.legal_concept: Availability during normal business hours
rules.atomic_rule: Public information must be available to the public at a minimum during the governmental body's normal business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation).
rules.source_language: Public information is available to the public at a minimum during the normal business hours of the governmental body.
rules.notes: 'at a minimum' = floor; the city fills the actual business-hours value.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt production standard
rules.atomic_rule: The officer must produce public information promptly, i.e., as soon as possible under the circumstances, within a reasonable time, without delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly ... as soon as possible under the circumstances, that is, within a reasonable time, without delay" from request receipt
rules.source_language: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer. ... 'promptly' means as soon as possible under the circumstances, that is, within a reasonable time, without delay.
rules.notes: Soft standard -> structural. There is NO fixed statutory acknowledgment/production day-count; do not invent one. § 552.221(d) supplies only a certification duty at 10 business days (TX-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Certification when information cannot be produced within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: If information cannot be produced within 10 business days after receipt, the officer must certify that fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour, within a reasonable time, when it will be available.
rules.trigger: Information cannot be produced within 10 business days of the request.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from request receipt (certification trigger)
rules.source_language: If public information cannot be produced for inspection or duplication within 10 business days after the date the information is requested by a member of the public, the officer for public information shall certify that fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour within a reasonable time when the information will be available for inspection or duplication.
rules.notes: Not a production deadline; a required written notice. The set date/hour is a soft 'reasonable time'.

rules.legal_concept: Certification when records in active use or storage
rules.atomic_rule: If requested information is in active use or in storage and therefore unavailable when requested, the officer must certify this in writing and set a date and hour, within a reasonable time, when it will be available.
rules.trigger: Requested records are in active use or storage at the time of request.
rules.source_language: If the requested information is unavailable at the time of the request to examine because it is in active use or in storage, the officer for public information shall certify this fact in writing to the requestor and set a date and hour within a reasonable time when the information will be available for inspection or duplication.
rules.notes: Set availability date is a soft 'reasonable time' standard.

rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for failure to inspect or pay within 60 days
rules.atomic_rule: A request is considered withdrawn if the requestor fails to inspect/duplicate the information within 60 days after it is made available, or fails to pay applicable charges within 60 days after being informed of the costs.
rules.trigger: 60 days elapse after availability without inspection, or after cost notice without payment.
rules.clock_spec: 60 days from date information made available (or from cost notice)
rules.source_language: A request is considered withdrawn if the requestor fails to inspect or duplicate the public information in the offices of the governmental body within 60 days after the date the information is made available, or fails to pay the applicable charges within 60 days after the date the requestor is informed of the costs.
rules.notes: Source_language reconstructed from a full-text reproduction summary; verify exact wording of § 552.221(e) against the official code.

rules.legal_concept: Request to clarify or narrow
rules.atomic_rule: If a request is unclear the body may ask the requestor to clarify; if a large amount is requested the body may discuss narrowing the scope.
rules.trigger: Request is unclear, or a large amount of information is requested.
rules.source_language: If what information is requested is unclear to the governmental body, the governmental body may ask the requestor to clarify the request. If a large amount of information has been requested, the governmental body may discuss with the requestor how the scope of a request might be narrowed, but the governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which information will be used.

rules.legal_concept: Required consequences statement in a clarification request
rules.atomic_rule: A written clarification/discussion request (or a request for additional info) must include a statement of the consequences of the requestor's failure to timely respond.
rules.trigger: Body sends a written clarification, discussion, or additional-information request.
rules.source_language: A written request for clarification or discussion under Subsection (b) or a written request for additional information under Subsection (c) must include a statement as to the consequences of the failure by the requestor to timely respond to the request for clarification, discussion, or additional information.

rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for failure to respond to clarification within 61 days
rules.atomic_rule: If the body receives no written response by the 61st day after sending a clarification/discussion request (or additional-information request), the underlying request is considered withdrawn.
rules.trigger: 61 days elapse after a clarification/discussion/additional-info request with no written response.
rules.clock_spec: 61 days from date clarification/discussion request sent
rules.source_language: If by the 61st day after the date a governmental body sends a written request for clarification or discussion under Subsection (b) or an officer for public information or agent sends a written request for additional information under Subsection (c) the governmental body, officer for public information, or agent, as applicable, does not receive a written response from the requestor, the underlying request for public information is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith clarification tolls the AG-decision deadline
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental body's good-faith request for clarification tolls the 10-business-day period for requesting an attorney general decision until the requestor responds.
rules.trigger: Body timely and in good faith requests clarification of an unclear request.
rules.clock_spec: tolls the 10 business-day AG-request clock (TX-0018) from clarification sent until requestor responds
rules.source_language: When a governmental body, acting in good faith, requests clarification or narrowing of an unclear or over-broad request for public information, the ten-day period to request an attorney general decision is measured from the date the request is clarified or narrowed.
rules.source_authority: City of Dallas v. Abbott, 304 S.W.3d 380 (Tex. 2010)
rules.notes: Judicially established operational rule; paraphrased narrow holding. Confirm citation and holding against the official Texas Supreme Court opinion before relying.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory attorney general decision to withhold
rules.atomic_rule: A body that receives a written request for information it wishes to withhold under a Subchapter C exception must ask the attorney general for a decision, unless there has been a previous determination.
rules.trigger: Body wishes to withhold requested information under a Subchapter C exception and no previous determination exists.
rules.source_language: A governmental body that receives a written request for information that it wishes to withhold from public disclosure and that it considers to be within one of the exceptions under Subchapter C must ask for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within that exception if there has not been a previous determination about whether the information falls within one of the exceptions.
rules.notes: Texas-distinctive: withholding is gated on a proactive AG ruling, not a requestor appeal. Source_language reconstructed from partial-quote fetch; verify against official text.

rules.legal_concept: Previous-determination exception to seeking an AG decision
rules.atomic_rule: No new AG decision is required where there has already been a previous determination that the information falls within an exception (or is public).
rules.trigger: A previous determination covering the information exists.
rules.source_language: ... must ask for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within that exception if there has not been a previous determination about whether the information falls within one of the exceptions.
rules.notes: Structural branch. 'Previous determination' has a narrow AG/case-law meaning; source_language reconstructed from partial fetch — verify.

rules.legal_concept: Deadline to request the attorney general decision
rules.atomic_rule: The body must ask the attorney general for a decision and state the applicable exceptions within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request the body wishes to withhold.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.

rules.legal_concept: 10-day notice to requestor that a decision was sought
rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 business days of the request the body must give the requestor a written statement that it is withholding and has asked the AG, plus a copy (redacted if needed) of its AG communication.
rules.trigger: Body requests an AG decision.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: provide the requestor within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the requestor's written request: (1) a written statement that the governmental body wishes to withhold the requested information and has asked for a decision from the attorney general about whether the information is within an exception to public disclosure; and (2) a copy of the governmental body's written communication to the attorney general asking for the decision or, if the governmental body's written communication to the attorney general discloses the requested information, a redacted copy of that written communication.

rules.legal_concept: 15-day submission of comments and records to AG
rules.atomic_rule: Within 15 business days of the request the body must submit to the AG written comments on the exceptions, a copy of the request, a dated receipt statement, and a copy (or representative sample) of the requested information.
rules.trigger: Body has requested an AG decision.
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: submit to the attorney general within a reasonable time but not later than the 15th business day after the date of receiving the written request: (1) written comments stating the reasons why the stated exceptions apply that would allow the information to be withheld; (2) a copy of the written request for information; (3) a signed statement as to the date on which the written request for information was received by the governmental body or evidence sufficient to establish that date; and (4) a copy of the specific information requested, or submit representative samples of the information if a voluminous amount of information was requested.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of AG comments to requestor within 15 days
rules.atomic_rule: A body that submits written comments to the AG must send a copy of those comments to the requestor not later than the 15th business day after receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Body submits written comments to the AG under § 552.301(e).
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: A governmental body that submits written comments to the attorney general under Subsection (e)(1)(A) shall send a copy of those comments to the person who requested the information from the governmental body not later than the 15th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.notes: If comments contain confidential info, only the portions not containing that info are sent (see full (e-1)).

rules.legal_concept: Presumption of openness for failure to comply
rules.atomic_rule: If the body does not timely request an AG decision and provide the § 552.301(d) and (e-1) notices, the requested information is presumed public and must be released absent a compelling reason to withhold.
rules.trigger: Body fails to request an AG decision and/or provide the required requestor notices.
rules.clock_spec: terminal event on lapse of the 10 business-day AG-request/notice deadline
rules.source_language: If a governmental body does not request an attorney general decision as provided by Section 552.301 and provide the requestor with the information required by Sections 552.301(d) and (e-1), the information requested in writing is presumed to be subject to required public disclosure and must be released unless there is a compelling reason to withhold the information.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed-disclosure trigger (silence/noncompliance -> presumed public). Remedy amounts intentionally omitted.

rules.legal_concept: AG must render decision within 45 business days
rules.atomic_rule: The attorney general must render the decision not later than the 45th business day after receiving the request, extendable once by 10 business days on timely notice to the body and requestor.
rules.trigger: AG receives a request for decision.
rules.clock_spec: 45 business-days from AG receipt of the decision request (+ optional 10 business-day extension)
rules.source_language: The attorney general shall render the decision ... not later than the 45th business day after the date the attorney general received the request for a decision. ... If the attorney general is unable to issue the decision within the 45-day period, the attorney general may extend the period for issuing the decision by an additional 10 business days by informing the governmental body and the requestor, during the original 45-day period, of the reason for the delay.
rules.notes: 'not later than' = ceiling on the AG. Request sits in a held state pending the ruling.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction of social security numbers without AG decision
rules.atomic_rule: A body may redact a living person's social security number from information it discloses under § 552.021 without requesting an attorney general decision under Subchapter G.
rules.trigger: Disclosed information contains a living person's SSN.
rules.source_language: A governmental body may redact the social security number of a living person from any information the governmental body discloses under Section 552.021 without the necessity of requesting a decision from the attorney general under Subchapter G.
rules.notes: Structural branch bypassing the AG-ruling workflow for this category. Contrast the general § 552.301(a) rule requiring an AG decision.

rules.legal_concept: Charge for providing copies
rules.atomic_rule: The copy charge must be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the information, including materials, labor, and overhead.
rules.trigger: Requestor asks for copies.
rules.source_language: The charge for providing a copy of public information shall be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the public information, including costs of materials, labor, and overhead.
rules.notes: 'reasonably' -> soft-standard; per-item rates are capped by AG rules (TX-0027).

rules.legal_concept: 50-or-fewer-page requests limited to photocopy charge
rules.atomic_rule: For a request of 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge may not include materials, labor, or overhead and is limited to the per-page photocopy charge, unless the pages are in two-or-more unconnected buildings or a remote storage facility.
rules.trigger: Request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records.
rules.source_language: If a request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge for providing the copy of the public information may not include costs of materials, labor, or overhead, but shall be limited to the charge for each page of the paper record that is photocopied, unless the pages to be photocopied are located in: (1) two or more separate buildings that are not physically connected with each other; or (2) a remote storage facility.
rules.notes: Distinct fee-calc branch for small requests. § 552.261(c) clarifies covered/connected buildings are not 'separate.'

rules.legal_concept: Charges capped by attorney general cost rules
rules.atomic_rule: Charges for copies/inspection may not exceed the amounts established by attorney general rule; a non-state governmental body setting its own charges may not exceed the AG-established amounts by more than 25% absent an exemption.
rules.trigger: Body imposes a charge for copies or inspection.
rules.source_language: The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information ... [a non-state governmental body's charges] may not exceed 25 percent greater than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption.
rules.notes: The concrete per-page/per-hour rate ceilings live in the AG's cost rules at 1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70, not in the statute. Source_language assembled from a partial fetch; verify exact wording of § 552.262.

rules.legal_concept: Required written itemized estimate when charge exceeds $40
rules.atomic_rule: If a copy charge (or a § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40, the body must give the requestor a written itemized statement detailing all estimated charges (including labor/personnel), notice of any less-costly alternative, and the requestor's response responsibilities.
rules.trigger: Estimated charge will exceed $40.
rules.source_language: If a request for a copy of public information will result in the imposition of a charge under this subchapter that exceeds $40, or a request to inspect a paper record will result in the imposition of a charge under Section 552.271 that exceeds $40, the governmental body shall provide the requestor with a written itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs.
rules.notes: $40 is a fixed statutory trigger threshold (a state-fixed value the city cannot alter).

rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for no response to itemized estimate within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: The request is considered withdrawn if the requestor does not respond in writing within 10 business days after the itemized statement is sent (accepting charges, modifying the request, or filing an overcharge complaint).
rules.trigger: 10 business days elapse after the itemized statement is sent with no written response.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from date the itemized statement is sent
rules.source_language: A request described by Subsection (a) is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor if the requestor does not respond in writing to the itemized statement by informing the governmental body within 10 business days after the date the statement is sent to the requestor that: (1) the requestor will accept the estimated charges; (2) the requestor is modifying the request in response to the itemized statement; or (3) the requestor has sent to the attorney general a complaint alleging that the requestor has been overcharged for being provided with a copy of the public information.
rules.notes: 'Sent'/'responded' timing defined in § 552.2615(e),(f).

rules.legal_concept: Updated itemized statement when charges rise 20% or more
rules.atomic_rule: If, before making the copy available, the body determines estimated charges will exceed the itemized statement by 20% or more, it must send a written updated itemized statement; no timely response to the update means the request is withdrawn.
rules.trigger: Estimated charges will exceed the prior itemized statement by 20% or more.
rules.source_language: If the governmental body later determines, but before it makes the copy or the paper record available, that the estimated charges will exceed the charges detailed in the written itemized statement by 20 percent or more, the governmental body shall send to the requestor a written updated itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs. If the requestor does not respond in writing to the updated estimate in the time and manner described by Subsection (b), the request is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.
rules.notes: 20% is a fixed statutory variance threshold. Actual charge cap tied to the (updated) estimate per § 552.2615(d).

rules.legal_concept: Minimum personnel-time allowance before charging
rules.atomic_rule: A body that sets time limits on uncompensated personnel time must allow at least 36 hours per requestor over a 12-month period and at least 15 hours per requestor in a one-month period before charging for personnel time.
rules.trigger: Body has adopted personnel-time limits under § 552.275.
rules.source_language: [The yearly time limit] may not be less than 36 hours for a requestor during the 12-month period ... [the monthly time limit] may not be less than 15 hours for a requestor for a one-month period.
rules.notes: Floor: the statutory minimum the city must allow; the city sets the actual limit at or above it. Verbatim phrases quoted from (b); bracketed lead-ins added for readability. Once the limit is met, § 552.275(e) requires a cost estimate within 10 business days.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The body must provide a copy without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest because providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Body determines providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
rules.source_language: A governmental body shall provide a copy of public information without charge or at a reduced charge if the governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the charge is in the public interest because providing the copy of the information primarily benefits the general public.
rules.notes: Duty is triggered by a discretionary public-interest determination.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver when collection cost exceeds the charge
rules.atomic_rule: The body may waive the charge if the cost of processing the collection of the charge would exceed the amount of the charge.
rules.trigger: Cost of collecting the charge exceeds the charge itself.
rules.source_language: If the cost to a governmental body of processing the collection of a charge for providing a copy of public information will exceed the amount of the charge, the governmental body may waive the charge.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit or bond for anticipated costs
rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for anticipated copy costs once an itemized estimate has been provided and the estimated charge exceeds $100 (body with more than 15 full-time employees) or $50 (fewer than 16 full-time employees).
rules.trigger: Itemized estimate provided and estimated charge exceeds the applicable threshold.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of anticipated costs for the preparation of a copy of public information if: (1) the officer for public information or the officer's agent has provided the requestor with the written itemized statement required under Section 552.2615 ... detailing the estimated charge for providing the copy; and (2) the charge for providing the copy of the public information specifically requested by the requestor is estimated by the governmental body to exceed: (A) $100, if the governmental body has more than 15 full-time employees; or (B) $50, if the governmental body has fewer than 16 full-time employees.
rules.notes: Two-tier fixed thresholds tied to full-time-employee count.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit for unpaid amounts from prior requests
rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for unpaid amounts owed on prior requests if those unpaid amounts exceed $100, and this becomes the sole means of collecting those amounts.
rules.trigger: Requestor has unpaid amounts exceeding $100 from prior requests.
rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of unpaid amounts owing to the governmental body in relation to previous requests that the requestor has made ... only if those unpaid amounts exceed $100.
rules.notes: Source_language reconstructed from a full-text reproduction summary; verify exact subsection and wording (overdue-balance provision of § 552.263).

structural_branches.description: Requests from incarcerated/confined individuals (or their non-attorney agents) may be declined — a routing/decline branch the engine must express (§ 552.028).
To withhold under a Subchapter C exception the body must proactively obtain an attorney general decision; there is no requestor-initiated administrative appeal (§ 552.301(a)).
A 'previous determination' short-circuits the AG-decision requirement — a branch that skips the § 552.301 workflow (§ 552.301(a)).
Failure to timely seek an AG decision / give the required notices flips the request into a 'presumed public, must release' terminal state (§ 552.302).
A good-faith clarification request tolls the 10-business-day AG-request clock until the requestor responds (City of Dallas v. Abbott).
SSNs may be redacted without invoking the AG-decision workflow — a redaction path parallel to, and bypassing, § 552.301 (§ 552.147(b)).
Charges over $40 route through a mandatory itemized-estimate / requestor-response / updated-estimate flow that can terminate the request by withdrawal (§ 552.2615).
Requests of 50 or fewer pages follow a distinct fee-calc path (photocopy charge only, no labor/materials/overhead) unless multi-building/remote (§ 552.261(a)).
A discretionary public-interest determination routes the request into free/reduced-charge production (§ 552.267(a)).

material_negatives.note: Texas imposes NO fixed statutory acknowledgment or final-response day-count. The only response duty is to 'promptly produce' (soft standard, § 552.221(a)-(b)); the sole hard 10-business-day event is a certification duty when records cannot be produced in that time (§ 552.221(d)), not a decision/production deadline. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

There is no requestor-initiated administrative appeal of a denial. The Act instead compels the governmental body to seek an AG ruling to withhold (§ 552.301); a requestor's recourse for noncompliance is a complaint to the AG or a mandamus suit under § 552.321 (external litigation, excluded).

No statewide per-page copy rate is fixed in the statute itself; the concrete rates/ceilings are set by attorney general cost rules (1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70), which were not opened this pass. § 552.262 only supplies the ceiling mechanism. Verify the current TAC rate schedule in a later pass.

The Act repeatedly uses 'business day' but a general statutory definition/holiday-exclusion rule for computing the PIA clocks was not separately captured this pass; confirm how 'business day' and skip-days are defined for §§ 552.221/552.301.

Preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the request itself: no distinct PIA preservation-hold provision was located this pass (routine retention schedules are out of scope); flag for the retention/records-authority pass.

rules.legal_concept: Constitutional right of every person to inspect or copy any public record
rules.atomic_rule: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state (or persons acting on their behalf), except records exempted under this section or made confidential by the Constitution.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right)
rules.source_language: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state, or persons acting on their behalf, except with respect to records exempted pursuant to this section or specifically made confidential by this Constitution.
rules.notes: Source Type: Constitution (self-executing). Anchors the universal-access family; access does not turn on requester status.

rules.legal_concept: Access extends to every person with no residency limitation
rules.atomic_rule: The right of access runs to 'every person' / 'any person' with no residency or citizenship qualification; a custodian may not condition access on the requester being a Florida resident.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state, or persons acting on their behalf ... [and] It is the policy of this state that all state, county, and municipal records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person.
rules.source_authority: Art. I, § 24(a), Fla. Const.; § 119.01(1), Fla. Stat.
rules.notes: Source Type: Constitution + Statute. No-residency is expressed through the unqualified 'every person'/'any person'; emitted as a rule (per universal-access symmetry), not a negative.

rules.legal_concept: Requester's motive/purpose is immaterial to the right of access
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require the requester to state a reason or purpose for the request; the requester's motivation does not affect the right of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The motivation of the person seeking the records does not impact the person's right to see them under the Public Records Act.
rules.source_authority: Curry v. State, 811 So. 2d 736 (Fla. 4th DCA 2002); Lorei v. Smith, 464 So. 2d 1330 (Fla. 2d DCA 1985)
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision. Quote taken from secondary sources summarizing the holdings; primary opinions not opened this pass — flagged for case-law verification. Emitted as a rule (universal-access symmetry) rather than a negative.

rules.legal_concept: No prescribed form; oral requests suffice and identity need not be disclosed
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not require that a public-records request be made in writing, on a particular form, or in person, and may not require the requester to disclose their identity as a condition of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Requesters are not required to provide a reason for their request. They are also not required to disclose their identity or submit the request in writing.
rules.source_authority: Interpreting § 119.07(1)(a), Fla. Stat.; Fla. AG guidance / Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual
rules.notes: Source Type: Official Guidance / interpretive. No statute expressly states this; derived from § 119.07(1)(a)'s 'any person desiring to do so' and AG guidance. Flagged for AG/manual verification pass.

rules.legal_concept: State policy that all state, county, and municipal records are open
rules.atomic_rule: All state, county, and municipal records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person unless a specific exemption applies.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: It is the policy of this state that all state, county, and municipal records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Establishes municipal coverage — the platform's default posture is 'open, then apply exemptions.'

rules.legal_concept: Duty to provide reasonable public access to electronically maintained records
rules.atomic_rule: As an agency increases its use of electronic recordkeeping it must provide reasonable public access to records electronically maintained and must ensure exempt/confidential records are not disclosed except as permitted by law.
rules.trigger: Agency maintains records in an electronic recordkeeping system
rules.source_language: Automation of public records must not erode the right of access to those records. As each agency increases its use of and dependence on electronic recordkeeping, each agency must provide reasonable public access to records electronically maintained and must ensure that exempt or confidential records are not disclosed except as otherwise permitted by law.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to acknowledge requests promptly
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian and any designee must acknowledge a request to inspect or copy records promptly.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect or copy records
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records and his or her designee must acknowledge requests to inspect or copy records promptly and respond to such requests in good faith.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard — no numeric acknowledgment deadline exists in Florida law. Split from the good-faith duty (FL-0008); same sentence.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to respond in good faith
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian and any designee must respond to requests to inspect or copy records in good faith.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect or copy records
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records and his or her designee must acknowledge requests to inspect or copy records promptly and respond to such requests in good faith.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Split from FL-0007 per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Every custodian must permit inspection and copying
rules.atomic_rule: Every person who has custody of a public record must permit that record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so.
rules.trigger: A person desires to inspect or copy a record in the custodian's custody
rules.source_language: Every person who has custody of a public record shall permit the record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so, at any reasonable time, under reasonable conditions, and under supervision by the custodian of the public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The duty attaches to whoever has custody — drives routing to the correct custodian/department. Conditions/supervision aspect split to FL-0015.

rules.legal_concept: Designation of another officer to handle requests, with identity disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may designate another officer or employee to permit inspection and copying, but must disclose the identity of the designee to the requester.
rules.trigger: Custodian designates a designee to handle the request
rules.source_language: A custodian of public records or a person having custody of public records may designate another officer or employee of the agency to permit the inspection and copying of public records, but must disclose the identity of the designee to the person requesting to inspect or copy public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Permission (may designate) carrying a mandatory disclosure (must disclose identity).

rules.legal_concept: Contractor duty to keep and maintain public records
rules.atomic_rule: A contractor providing services to a public agency must keep and maintain the public records required by the agency to perform the service.
rules.trigger: Agency contract for services under which the contractor acts on behalf of the agency
rules.source_language: Keep and maintain public records required by the public agency to perform the service.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Routes requests to contractor-held records into the covered set.

rules.legal_concept: Contractor duty to provide records on the agency's request within a reasonable time
rules.atomic_rule: On the agency custodian's request, a contractor must provide the agency a copy of, or allow inspection/copying of, requested records within a reasonable time at a cost not exceeding the chapter's fees.
rules.trigger: Request from the public agency's custodian of public records to the contractor
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable time" from the agency custodian's request
rules.source_language: Upon request from the public agency's custodian of public records, provide the public agency with a copy of the requested records or allow the records to be inspected or copied within a reasonable time at a cost that does not exceed the cost provided in this chapter.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Fee cap cross-refers to the § 119.07(4) rates (FL-0020..FL-0022).

rules.legal_concept: Transfer or retention of records at contract completion
rules.atomic_rule: At contract completion the contractor must transfer, at no cost, all public records in its possession to the agency, or keep and maintain the records; if transferring, it must destroy exempt/confidential duplicates.
rules.trigger: Completion of the contract
rules.source_language: Upon completion of the contract, transfer, at no cost, to the public agency all public records in possession of the contractor or keep and maintain public records required by the public agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Determines whether contractor-held records remain retrievable for future requests after contract end.

rules.legal_concept: Only permissible delay is the limited reasonable time to retrieve and redact
rules.atomic_rule: The only delay permitted in producing records is the limited reasonable time the custodian needs to retrieve the record and delete the portions asserted to be exempt; no automatic or policy-based delay is allowed.
rules.trigger: A request has been received and records must be retrieved/reviewed for exemptions
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "limited reasonable time" to retrieve and redact, from request receipt
rules.source_language: The only delay in producing records permitted under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, is the limited reasonable time allowed the custodian to retrieve the record and delete those portions of the record the custodian asserts are exempt.
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision (Fla. Supreme Court). Primary opinion returned HTTP 403 this pass; quote taken from AG opinions/secondary sources that reproduce it verbatim — flagged for case verification. This is the operative production 'deadline' — a soft standard, not a numeric window.

rules.legal_concept: Inspection at reasonable time, under reasonable conditions and supervision
rules.atomic_rule: Inspection and copying occur at any reasonable time, under reasonable conditions, and under supervision by the custodian.
rules.trigger: A person inspects or copies records in person
rules.source_language: Every person who has custody of a public record shall permit the record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so, at any reasonable time, under reasonable conditions, and under supervision by the custodian of the public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Same sentence as FL-0009, split to isolate the reasonable-conditions/supervision limit on how inspection is conducted.

rules.legal_concept: Copy provided in the requested medium if maintained in that medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency must provide a copy of a record in the medium requested if it maintains the record in that medium; providing a copy in a medium not routinely used, or compiling/manipulating data, is charged under s. 119.07(4).
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium; agency maintains an electronic recordkeeping system
rules.source_language: An agency must provide a copy of the record in the medium requested if the agency maintains the record in that medium, and the agency may charge a fee in accordance with this chapter. For the purpose of satisfying a public records request, the fee to be charged by an agency if it elects to provide a copy of a public record in a medium not routinely used by the agency, or if it elects to compile information not routinely developed or maintained by the agency or that requires a substantial amount of manipulation or programming, must be in accordance with s. 119.07(4).
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The manipulation/programming clause is a trigger for the special service charge (FL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Redact exempt portion and produce the remainder (segregability)
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian asserting that an exemption applies to part of a record must redact that portion to which the exemption is asserted and validly applies, and must produce the remainder for inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: Custodian asserts an exemption applies to part of a record
rules.source_language: A person who has custody of a public record who asserts that an exemption applies to a part of such record shall redact that portion of the record to which an exemption has been asserted and validly applies, and such person shall produce the remainder of such record for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Mandatory segregability — a partial exemption never justifies withholding the whole record.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to state the basis of the exemption, including statutory citation
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian contending all or part of a record is exempt must state the basis of the exemption, including the statutory citation to the exemption.
rules.trigger: Custodian contends a record (or part) is exempt
rules.source_language: If the person who has custody of a public record contends that all or part of the record is exempt from inspection and copying, he or she shall state the basis of the exemption that he or she contends is applicable to the record, including the statutory citation to an exemption created or afforded by statute.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Requires the software to capture a statutory citation whenever an exemption is asserted.

rules.legal_concept: On request, written particularized reasons for an exemption/confidentiality determination
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester asks, the custodian must state in writing and with particularity the reasons for the conclusion that the record is exempt or confidential.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for the reasons for an exemption/confidentiality determination
rules.source_language: If requested by the person seeking to inspect or copy the record, the custodian of public records shall state in writing and with particularity the reasons for the conclusion that the record is exempt or confidential.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. A conditional written-notice/document the engine must be able to generate.

rules.legal_concept: Statutory per-copy duplication rate
rules.atomic_rule: For duplicated copies of records not larger than 14 by 8.5 inches, the agency may charge up to 15 cents per one-sided copy.
rules.trigger: Agency provides a standard-size one-sided duplicated copy
rules.source_language: Up to 15 cents per one-sided copy for duplicated copies of not more than 14 inches by 8 1/2 inches.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Basis is a ceiling ('up to 15 cents') — city sets the operative rate at or below $0.15/page.

rules.legal_concept: Additional charge for two-sided copies
rules.atomic_rule: For a two-sided copy, the agency may charge no more than an additional 5 cents.
rules.trigger: Agency provides a two-sided duplicated copy
rules.source_language: No more than an additional 5 cents for each two-sided copy.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of an additional $0.05 per two-sided copy.

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of duplication for other copies
rules.atomic_rule: For all copies other than standard-size paper copies, the agency charges the actual cost of duplication of the public record.
