rules.trigger: Agency provides a copy that is not a standard-size paper copy
rules.source_language: For all other copies, the actual cost of duplication of the public record.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Actual cost of duplication' is bounded by the statutory definition in FL-0023.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'actual cost of duplication'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Actual cost of duplication' means the cost of the material and supplies used to duplicate the record, and does not include labor cost or overhead cost associated with such duplication.
rules.trigger: Charging 'actual cost of duplication' under s. 119.07(4)(a)3.
rules.source_language: "Actual cost of duplication" means the cost of the material and supplies used to duplicate the public record, but does not include labor cost or overhead cost associated with such duplication.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Definition the fee engine branches on — labor/overhead are excluded from the base copy charge (they belong only to the special service charge, FL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Charge for certified copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge up to $1 per copy for a certified copy of a public record.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified copy
rules.source_language: An agency may charge up to $1 per copy for a certified copy of a public record.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of $1.00 per certified copy.

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extensive IT or clerical/supervisory assistance
rules.atomic_rule: If the nature or volume of records requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service charge based on the cost actually incurred.
rules.trigger: Nature or volume of records requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance (or both)
rules.source_language: If the nature or volume of public records requested to be inspected or copied pursuant to this subsection is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or both, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor cost of the personnel providing the service that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the clerical and supervisory assistance required, or both.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. 'Reasonable' with no fixed number = soft-standard; city sets a rate methodology under the reasonableness constraint. Applies to inspection as well as copying. Trigger term 'extensive' is undefined.

rules.legal_concept: Supervision charge when requester photographs records
rules.atomic_rule: When a person photographs public records, the custodian may charge for supervision services at a rate agreed upon by the parties; if they cannot agree, the custodian determines the charge.
rules.trigger: A person elects to photograph public records rather than obtain agency copies
rules.source_language: The custodian of public records may charge the person making the photographs for supervision services at a rate of compensation to be agreed upon by the person desiring to make the photographs and the custodian of public records. If they fail to agree as to the appropriate charge, the charge shall be determined by the custodian of public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. No fixed number — negotiated/custodian-set = soft-standard.

rules.legal_concept: Requester pays expense of a separate room/place to photograph records
rules.atomic_rule: Where another room or place is necessary to photograph public records, the expense of providing it is paid by the person desiring to photograph the records.
rules.trigger: Photographing records requires provision of another room or place
rules.source_language: Where provision of another room or place is necessary to photograph public records, the expense of providing the same shall be paid by the person desiring to photograph the public records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Charge equals the actual expense incurred (fixed to cost).

rules.legal_concept: Unjustified delay or refusal as a constructive/unlawful denial
rules.atomic_rule: Delay beyond the limited reasonable time needed to retrieve and redact, or a policy-based/automatic delay, constitutes an unlawful (constructive) denial of access.
rules.trigger: Custodian delays production beyond the limited reasonable time, or imposes an automatic/policy delay
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: constructive denial arises once delay exceeds the "limited reasonable time" (no fixed day-count)
rules.source_language: The only delay in producing records permitted under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, is the limited reasonable time allowed the custodian to retrieve the record and delete those portions of the record the custodian asserts are exempt.
rules.notes: Source Type: Appellate Decision. Keeper-sliver #3 (constructive-denial trigger): Florida sets NO numeric silence-equals-denial period; the trigger is the soft 'reasonable time' standard. Remedy amounts (attorney fees under § 119.12) deliberately excluded. Primary opinion not opened (403) — flagged.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory in camera inspection for specified asserted exemptions in a civil action
rules.atomic_rule: In a civil action where an exemption under specified provisions (s. 119.071(1)(d) or (f), (2)(d),(e),(f), or (4)(c)) is asserted, the record must be submitted to the court for in camera inspection.
rules.trigger: Civil action in which one of the enumerated exemptions is asserted
rules.source_language: In any civil action in which an exemption to this section is asserted, if the exemption is alleged to exist under or by virtue of s. 119.071(1)(d) or (f), (2)(d), (e), or (f), or (4)(c), the public record or part thereof in question shall be submitted to the court for an inspection in camera.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Judicial-review path (namespaced appeal.judicial per pilot #1). Florida's enforcement is by court action, not an internal administrative appeal stage.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day no-disposal hold when custodian disputes that a requested record is public
rules.atomic_rule: Even if the custodian asserts a requested record is not a public record subject to inspection, the record must not be disposed of for 30 days after a written request to inspect or copy it was served on or made to the custodian.
rules.trigger: A written request is served/made and the custodian asserts the record is not a public record subject to inspection
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from the date the written request to inspect or copy was served on or made to the custodian
rules.source_language: Even if an assertion is made by the custodian of public records that a requested record is not a public record subject to public inspection or copying under this subsection, the requested record shall, nevertheless, not be disposed of for a period of 30 days after the date on which a written request to inspect or copy the record was served on or otherwise made to the custodian of public records by the person seeking access to the record.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #2 (preservation hold triggered by the request itself) — a state the request enters, with a hard 30-day retention clock. Requires the request to be written to trigger the hold.

structural_branches.description: FL-0029: Florida's exemption dispute path is judicial — a civil action with mandatory in camera inspection for enumerated exemptions. There is NO statutory internal/administrative appeal stage; the engine must express a court-review fork rather than an appeal.administrative.* stage.
FL-0030: a distinct state the request enters — a 30-day no-disposal hold on the record whenever a written request is made and the custodian disputes the record's public status.
FL-0014: production timing is a soft 'limited reasonable time' standard the engine applies, not a city-filled numeric window — a structural deadline path distinct from a parameter value.
FL-0007: acknowledgment is governed by the soft standard 'promptly' — a structural deadline the engine applies, with no numeric value to configure.
FL-0028: the request can transition to a constructive-denial (unlawful refusal) state once delay exceeds the reasonable time — a terminal branch triggered by a soft standard, not a fixed clock.

FL-0011..FL-0013: when a contractor holds agency records, a distinct routing/production sub-path applies (maintain, provide within reasonable time at chapter cost, transfer/keep at contract completion).
FL-0017..FL-0019: mandatory segregability path — assert exemption with statutory citation, redact, produce remainder, and generate written particularized reasons on request.

material_negatives.note: Florida sets NO fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline. The only standards are 'promptly'/'good faith' (§ 119.07(1)(c)) and the 'limited reasonable time' of Tribune Co. v. Cannella. Captured as soft-standard rules FL-0007 and FL-0014, not numeric parameters. Absence of a day-count is itself the finding.

Chapter 119 contains NO explicit statutory deposit/advance-payment provision. AG opinions and practice permit requiring payment of estimated fees before producing copies, but no codified clock or threshold was found. Deferred to an AG-opinion pass; not emitted as a rule to avoid asserting a statute that does not exist.

No statute imposes a mandatory clarification stage or a nonresponse-abandonment clock. Case law recognizes that overbroad requests may be met with a request to narrow, but no explicit statutory clarification clock or deemed-abandonment trigger was located. Deferred to case-law/AG pass.

Florida provides NO internal administrative appeal stage and no statewide AG administrative-review adjudication for records denials. Enforcement is judicial (civil action / mandamus). Emitted affirmatively as the judicial path FL-0029; the absence of an administrative appeal is a structural fact, not a gap to fill with a value.
No statutory requirement that agencies assign or track a request number, log requests, or report request metrics for an individual municipal request. Nothing for the software to enforce here.
No statutory free-copy allowance or de minimis waiver threshold was found; the fee schedule (§ 119.07(4)) applies from the first copy. Absence noted; cities may adopt their own waiver policy.

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access (Freedom of Information Law)
rules.atomic_rule: Any member of the public may request access to the records of government; access is a public right exercisable by any person.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional public right)
rules.source_language: The legislature therefore declares that government is the public's business and that the public, individually and collectively and represented by a free press, should have access to the records of government in accordance with the provisions of this article.
rules.notes: Affirmative right; § 89(3)(a) runs the response duty to 'the person requesting it.' Shared universal-access key.

rules.legal_concept: No showing of need, good faith or purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason, need, good faith, or legitimate purpose to obtain accessible records.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: New York's Court of Appeals and the Committee on Open Government hold that FOIL does not require the party requesting records to make any showing of need, good faith or legitimate purpose as a condition to access.
rules.source_authority: Matter of M. Farbman & Sons v. N.Y.C. Health & Hosps. Corp., 62 N.Y.2d 75 (1984); Committee on Open Government advisory opinions
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry (never a material negative). Paraphrase: statutory text imposes no purpose condition; principle stated in case law and COOG opinions. Verify exact holding language.

rules.legal_concept: Equal availability irrespective of requester status/residency
rules.atomic_rule: Accessible records are equally available to any person regardless of residency, citizenship, or status; an agency may not condition access on proof of residency or identity.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: When records are accessible under the Freedom of Information Law, they must be made equally available to any person, irrespective of the status, residence, interest or intended use of the person making the request.
rules.source_authority: Committee on Open Government advisory opinions (construing N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6)
rules.notes: Emitted as rule per universal-access symmetry. No statutory residency condition exists; COOG consistently so construes. Verify verbatim opinion text.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers statutory duty
rules.atomic_rule: The agency's five-business-day response duty is triggered by receipt of a written request for a record.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request
rules.source_language: Each entity subject to the provisions of this article, within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it, deny such request in writing or furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request...
rules.notes: Written form is the trigger; § 89(3)(b) additionally requires accepting email requests where reasonable means exist.

rules.legal_concept: Record must be reasonably described
rules.atomic_rule: The response duty attaches only where the requested record is reasonably described.
rules.trigger: Written request received
rules.source_language: ...within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it...
rules.notes: 'Reasonably described' is the statutory adequacy standard; FOIL provides no explicit clarification-cure clock (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Acceptance of and response to email requests
rules.atomic_rule: An entity with reasonable means available shall accept requests submitted by email and respond by email, unless the request seeks a response in another form.
rules.trigger: Email request received; entity has reasonable means
rules.source_language: All entities shall, provided such entity has reasonable means available, accept requests for records submitted in the form of electronic mail and shall respond to such requests by electronic mail, using forms, to the extent practicable, consistent with the form or forms developed by the committee on open government pursuant to subdivision one of this section and provided that the written requests do not seek a response in some other form.
rules.notes: Applies to all entities (municipal included). § 89(3)(c) online-submission duty is limited to STATE agencies.

rules.legal_concept: Standard request form on the internet
rules.atomic_rule: The Committee on Open Government develops a request form, made available on the internet, that the public may use to request a record.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The committee shall: ... v. develop a form, which shall be made available on the internet, that may be used by the public to request a record;
rules.notes: Form use is permissive for the requester; agencies respond 'using forms, to the extent practicable.'

rules.legal_concept: Presumption of openness; enumerated exemptions
rules.atomic_rule: Each agency shall make all records available for inspection and copying except records or portions that fall within the enumerated exceptions.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: Each agency shall, in accordance with its published rules, make available for public inspection and copying all records, except that such agency may deny access to records or portions thereof that: (a) are specifically exempted from disclosure by state or federal statute; (b) if disclosed would constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy...
rules.notes: Default is disclosure; exemptions are the enumerated (a)-(w) categories (see special records). Disclosure is discretionary ('may deny'), not mandatory withholding.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day initial response
rules.atomic_rule: Within five business days of receipt of a written request, the agency shall grant access, deny the request in writing, or furnish a written acknowledgement of receipt with an approximate date.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request reasonably describing a record
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of written request
rules.source_language: Each entity subject to the provisions of this article, within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person requesting it, deny such request in writing or furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request and a statement of the approximate date, which shall be reasonable under the circumstances of the request, when such request will be granted or denied...
rules.notes: Three-way branch (grant / written denial / acknowledgement). 5 business days is fixed by statute; municipalities cannot lengthen it.

rules.legal_concept: Approximate-date standard in acknowledgement
rules.atomic_rule: A written acknowledgement must state an approximate date, reasonable under the circumstances, when the request will be granted or denied.
rules.trigger: Agency issues an acknowledgement instead of granting/denying within 5 business days
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable under the circumstances" from date of acknowledgement
rules.source_language: ...furnish a written acknowledgement of the receipt of such request and a statement of the approximate date, which shall be reasonable under the circumstances of the request, when such request will be granted or denied...
rules.notes: Soft standard — do not encode a fixed day count; the engine applies a reasonableness standard.

rules.legal_concept: Twenty-business-day disclosure checkpoint
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency grants a request but circumstances prevent disclosure within twenty business days from the acknowledgement, it must act (state reasons and a date certain).
rules.trigger: Request granted in whole or part; disclosure not achievable within 20 business days of acknowledgement
rules.clock_spec: 20 business-days from date of acknowledgement
rules.source_language: If an agency determines to grant a request in whole or in part, and if circumstances prevent disclosure to the person requesting the record or records within twenty business days from the date of the acknowledgement of the receipt of the request, the agency shall state, in writing, both the reason for the inability to grant the request within twenty business days and a date certain within a reasonable period, depending on the circumstances, when the request will be granted in whole or in part.
rules.notes: 20 business days is a checkpoint, not a hard production deadline; failing it triggers the delay-notice duty (NY-0012), not automatic denial.

rules.legal_concept: Delay notice with reason and date certain
rules.atomic_rule: When disclosure cannot occur within twenty business days, the agency must state in writing both the reason for the inability and a date certain, within a reasonable period, when the request will be granted.
rules.trigger: Disclosure not achievable within 20 business days of acknowledgement
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "date certain within a reasonable period" from the delay notice
rules.source_language: ...the agency shall state, in writing, both the reason for the inability to grant the request within twenty business days and a date certain within a reasonable period, depending on the circumstances, when the request will be granted in whole or in part.
rules.notes: The 'date certain' is agency-set and reasonableness-bounded (soft), so Config Home is structural.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive denial for non-conformance
rules.atomic_rule: An agency's failure to conform to the subdivision-three response provisions constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Agency fails to meet the § 89(3) response obligations
rules.clock_spec: on lapse of the § 89(3) response obligations
rules.source_language: Failure by an agency to conform to the provisions of subdivision three of this section shall constitute a denial.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial trigger (keeper sliver): silence/non-conformance = denial, which opens the administrative appeal right.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create records
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to prepare any record it does not possess or maintain (except the statutorily specified subject-matter/vote records).
rules.trigger: Request seeks a record not possessed or maintained
rules.source_language: Nothing in this article shall be construed to require any entity to prepare any record not possessed or maintained by such entity except the records specified in subdivision three of section eighty-seven and subdivision three of section eighty-eight of this article.
rules.notes: Distinguish from electronic retrieval/extraction, which IS required (NY-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Duty to retrieve/extract from computer storage
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency can retrieve or extract a record or data from a computer storage system with reasonable effort, it shall do so.
rules.trigger: Requested record/data is in a computer storage system and retrievable with reasonable effort
rules.source_language: When an agency has the ability to retrieve or extract a record or data maintained in a computer storage system with reasonable effort, it shall be required to do so.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable effort' is a soft standard on the duty's scope.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic retrieval preferred when it takes less time
rules.atomic_rule: Where electronic retrieval/extraction requires less employee time than manual retrieval or redaction from non-electronic records, the agency shall retrieve or extract the record electronically.
rules.trigger: Electronic retrieval requires less employee time than manual
rules.source_language: When doing so requires less employee time than engaging in manual retrieval or redactions from non-electronic records, the agency shall be required to retrieve or extract such record or data electronically.
rules.notes: Affects fee (labor time) as well as method.

rules.legal_concept: Programming to retrieve is not record creation
rules.atomic_rule: Programming necessary to retrieve a record from computer storage and transfer it to the requested medium is not the preparation or creation of a new record.
rules.trigger: Retrieval/transfer requires programming
rules.source_language: Any programming necessary to retrieve a record maintained in a computer storage system and to transfer that record to the medium requested by a person or to allow the transferred record to be read or printed shall not be deemed to be the preparation or creation of a new record.
rules.notes: Rebuts a 'no-duty-to-create' defense for database extractions; programming labor may still be recoverable as fee.

rules.legal_concept: No refusal for volume/burden where outside service available
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not deny a request as voluminous or burdensome due to insufficient staffing (or any basis) if it may engage an outside professional service to provide copying, programming, or other services, the cost of which it may recover.
rules.trigger: Request is voluminous/burdensome and an outside professional service could perform the work
rules.source_language: An agency shall not deny a request on the basis that the request is voluminous or that locating or reviewing the requested records or providing the requested copies is burdensome because the agency lacks sufficient staffing or on any other basis if the agency may engage an outside professional service to provide copying, programming or other services required to provide the copy, the costs of which the agency may recover pursuant to paragraph (c) of subdivision one of section eighty-seven of this article.
rules.notes: Cost of the outside service is recoverable under § 87(1)(c) (see NY-0030).

rules.legal_concept: Copy provided on payment/offer to pay; certification
rules.atomic_rule: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the prescribed fee, the entity shall provide a copy of the record and, if requested, certify its correctness.
rules.trigger: Requester pays or offers to pay the prescribed fee
rules.source_language: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the fee prescribed therefor, the entity shall provide a copy of such record and certify to the correctness of such copy if so requested, or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
rules.notes: An OFFER to pay suffices to trigger the duty — production is gated on payment/offer, not on completed prepayment of the full charge.

rules.legal_concept: Certification of non-possession after diligent search
rules.atomic_rule: Where applicable, the entity shall certify that it does not possess the record or that the record cannot be found after a diligent search.
rules.trigger: Record not in possession or not found after diligent search
rules.source_language: ...or as the case may be, shall certify that it does not have possession of such record or that such record cannot be found after diligent search.
rules.notes: Split from NY-0019 (same sentence): a distinct terminal outcome — certified no-record response.

rules.legal_concept: Records in the medium requested
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall provide records in the medium requested if it can reasonably make the copy or have it made by engaging an outside professional service.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium and the copy can reasonably be made
rules.source_language: An agency shall provide records on the medium requested by a person, if the agency can reasonably make such copy or have such copy made by engaging an outside professional service.
rules.notes: Applies to electronic/computer formats.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-format records not encrypted
rules.atomic_rule: Records provided in a computer format shall not be encrypted.
rules.trigger: Records provided in computer format
rules.source_language: Records provided in a computer format shall not be encrypted.
rules.notes: Constrains the delivery format of electronic production.

rules.legal_concept: Inspection and copying of records
rules.atomic_rule: Each agency shall, per its published rules, make available for public inspection and copying all records except those (or portions) that may be withheld under the exemptions.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: Each agency shall, in accordance with its published rules, make available for public inspection and copying all records, except those records or portions thereof that may be withheld pursuant to the exceptions of rights of access appearing in this subdivision.
rules.notes: Inspection is an access mode distinct from copying (no copy fee for pure inspection).

rules.legal_concept: Paper copy fee ceiling (25 cents/page)
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for paper copies shall not exceed 25 cents per photocopy not exceeding 9 by 14 inches, unless a different fee is prescribed by statute.
rules.trigger: Paper photocopy up to 9x14 inches provided
rules.source_language: except when a different fee is otherwise prescribed by statute: (1) the fees for paper copies of records shall not exceed twenty-five cents per photocopy not in excess of nine inches by fourteen inches, or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
rules.notes: Ceiling, not a fixed rate: the city sets its actual per-page fee up to $0.25. A statute-specified different fee overrides this ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of reproduction for other records
rules.atomic_rule: For records other than 9x14 paper photocopies, the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction determined under § 87(1)(c).
rules.trigger: Reproduction of a record that is not a 9x14 paper photocopy
rules.source_language: ...or the actual cost of reproducing any other record in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c) of this subdivision.
rules.notes: 'Actual cost' is capped and its composition is fixed by § 87(1)(c) (NY-0027 through NY-0030).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for recently prepared identical electronic record
rules.atomic_rule: Where an identical record was prepared for a prior request within the past six months and an electronic copy is available, the agency shall charge no fee except the actual cost of a storage device/media if provided.
rules.trigger: Identical record prepared within past 6 months and electronic copy available
rules.source_language: In the case where an identical record has been prepared for a previous request within the past 6 months and an electronic copy is available, an agency shall not charge a fee for the reproduction of such record, except for the actual cost of a storage device or media if one is provided to the requester in complying with such request.
rules.notes: Fee fixed at $0 (plus media cost); 6-month lookback is the trigger condition.

rules.legal_concept: Preparation labor billed at lowest-paid qualified employee's rate
rules.atomic_rule: Actual reproduction cost may include only the hourly salary attributed to the lowest-paid agency employee who has the necessary skill to prepare the copy.
rules.trigger: Copy preparation requires employee labor (subject to the 2-hour threshold)
rules.source_language: In determining the actual cost of reproducing a record, an agency may include only: i. an amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to the lowest paid agency employee who has the necessary skill required to prepare a copy of the requested record;
rules.notes: Basis is fixed by statute (lowest-paid qualified employee); the city supplies the actual wage figure as the operative value.

rules.legal_concept: Two-hour preparation threshold for any labor fee
rules.atomic_rule: No preparation fee may be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare the copy.
rules.trigger: Copy preparation requires agency employee time
rules.source_language: ...no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
rules.notes: Two-hour floor gates the labor fee entirely; fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Search time and administrative costs excluded from fee
rules.atomic_rule: Preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs; these may not be charged to the requester.
rules.trigger: Fee calculation for copy preparation
rules.source_language: ...preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs, and no fee shall be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare a copy of the record requested.
rules.notes: Constrains the fee calculation — the recoverable labor is copy-preparation time only, not search/admin.

rules.legal_concept: Outside professional service cost only when IT equipment inadequate
rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of engaging an outside professional service to prepare a copy may be included only when the agency's information technology equipment is inadequate to prepare the copy and the service is used.
rules.trigger: Agency IT equipment inadequate; outside service used to prepare copy
rules.source_language: iii. the actual cost to the agency of engaging an outside professional service to prepare a copy of a record, but only when an agency's information technology equipment is inadequate to prepare a copy, if such service is used to prepare the copy;
rules.notes: Branch condition on recovering outside-service cost; ties to the no-burden-refusal rule (NY-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Estimated cost notice
rules.atomic_rule: The requester shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing the copy if more than two hours of employee time is needed or if an outside professional service would be retained.
rules.trigger: Preparation needs more than 2 hours of employee time, or an outside service is to be retained
rules.source_language: A person requesting a record shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing a copy of the record if more than two hours of an agency employee's time is needed, or if an outside professional service would be retained to prepare a copy of the record.
rules.notes: Cost-estimate notice is a required communication before charging preparation fees.

rules.legal_concept: Deletion of identifying details
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may delete identifying details when it makes records available to prevent an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
rules.trigger: Record contains identifying details whose disclosure would invade privacy
rules.source_language: In the absence of such guidelines, an agency may delete identifying details when it makes records available.
rules.notes: Redaction to enable partial release rather than wholesale denial; privacy categories enumerated in § 89(2)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation and retrieval for maximum access
rules.atomic_rule: Where electronic records mix accessible and withholdable items, the agency shall, whenever practicable and reasonable, design retrieval to permit segregation and retrieval of the accessible items to provide maximum public access.
rules.trigger: Electronically maintained records contain both available and withholdable items
rules.source_language: When records maintained electronically include items of information that would be available under this article, as well as items of information that may be withheld, an agency in designing its information retrieval methods, whenever practicable and reasonable, shall do so in a manner that permits the segregation and retrieval of available items in order to provide maximum public access.
rules.notes: Segregability principle — withholdable portions do not justify denying the whole record.

rules.legal_concept: Particularized and specific justification for denial
rules.atomic_rule: A denial of access is valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies access to a record or portion
rules.source_language: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of such record and shall be valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for such denial.
rules.notes: Governs the content/validity of a denial notice.

rules.legal_concept: No denial based solely on record category
rules.atomic_rule: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of the record.
rules.trigger: Agency denies access
rules.source_language: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of such record and shall be valid only when there is a particularized and specific justification for such denial.
rules.notes: Split from NY-0034 (same sentence): a distinct prohibition on blanket category-based withholding.

rules.legal_concept: Internal FOIL appeal to agency head
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access to a record may appeal in writing to the head, chief executive, or governing body of the entity (or its designee).
rules.trigger: Access denied (including constructive denial)
rules.source_language: Except as provided in subdivision five of this section, any person denied access to a record may within thirty days appeal in writing such denial to the head, chief executive or governing body of the entity, or the person therefor designated by such head, chief executive, or governing body...
rules.notes: Mandatory internal appeal stage; prerequisite to judicial (Article 78) review.

rules.legal_concept: Thirty-day window to file administrative appeal
rules.atomic_rule: The requester must file the written administrative appeal within thirty days of the denial.
rules.trigger: Denial of access
rules.clock_spec: 30 days from denial (requester's filing window)
rules.source_language: ...any person denied access to a record may within thirty days appeal in writing such denial to the head, chief executive or governing body of the entity...
rules.notes: Statute says 'within thirty days' (day-type not specified as business days). Fixed statutory window.

rules.legal_concept: Ten-business-day appeal determination
rules.atomic_rule: Within ten business days of receiving the appeal, the appeal authority shall fully explain in writing the reasons for further denial or provide access to the record.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written administrative appeal
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of appeal
rules.source_language: ...who shall within ten business days of the receipt of such appeal fully explain in writing to the person requesting the record the reasons for further denial, or provide access to the record sought.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory window; failing it is a constructive denial (NY-0040).

rules.legal_concept: Forward appeal and determination to Committee on Open Government
rules.atomic_rule: Each agency shall immediately forward to the Committee on Open Government a copy of the appeal when received and the ensuing determination.
rules.trigger: Agency receives an appeal / issues an appeal determination
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "immediately" from receipt of appeal / determination
rules.source_language: In addition, each agency shall immediately forward to the committee on open government a copy of such appeal when received by the agency and the ensuing determination thereon.
rules.notes: Notice obligation to the state oversight body; 'immediately' is a soft timing standard.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to determine appeal constitutes denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency's failure to conform to the appeal provisions of paragraph (a) constitutes a denial (opening judicial review).
rules.trigger: Agency fails to timely/properly determine the administrative appeal
rules.clock_spec: on lapse of the § 89(4)(a) 10-business-day appeal determination
rules.source_language: Failure by an agency to conform to the provisions of paragraph (a) of this subdivision shall constitute a denial.
rules.notes: Second deemed-denial trigger, at the appeal stage; enables Article 78 review.

rules.legal_concept: Article 78 judicial review of appeal denial
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access in an administrative appeal determination may bring a proceeding to review that denial under CPLR Article 78; the agency bears the burden of proving the record falls within an exemption.
rules.trigger: Denial in an administrative appeal determination (or constructive denial of the appeal)
rules.source_language: Except as provided in subdivision five of this section, a person denied access to a record in an appeal determination under the provisions of paragraph (a) of this subdivision may bring a proceeding for review of such denial pursuant to article seventy-eight of the civil practice law and rules. In the event that access to any record is denied pursuant to the provisions of subdivision two of section eighty-seven of this article, the agency involved shall have the burden of proving that such record falls within the provisions of such subdivision two.
rules.notes: Judicial path (namespaced appeal.judicial). Exhaustion of the internal appeal is a prerequisite. CPLR 4-month limitation applies but is not stated in Art. 6 — not encoded here.

structural_branches.description: Within 5 business days the agency takes ONE of three paths: (a) grant/make available, (b) written denial, or (c) written acknowledgement stating a reasonable approximate date. The acknowledgement path opens the 20-business-day checkpoint and the delay-notice/date-certain obligations (§ 89(3)(a)).

Mandatory internal FOIL appeal stage: initial determination -> written appeal to head/CEO/governing body within 30 days -> 10-business-day written appeal determination -> immediate forwarding of appeal+determination to the Committee on Open Government. Exhaustion is a prerequisite to Article 78 (§ 89(4)(a)-(b)).

Composed actual-cost fee engine for non-standard reproduction: labor at the lowest-paid qualified employee's hourly rate, only above a 2-hour preparation threshold; plus actual storage-device/media cost; plus outside-professional-service cost only when agency IT equipment is inadequate; excluding search time and administrative costs (§ 87(1)(c)).

STATE-AGENCY-ONLY pre-submission exception path (§ 89(5); 'agency' there = state department/board/office and gubernatorially-appointed public corporations — NOT ordinary municipalities): submitter requests exception at submission; info maintained apart until 15 days after entitlement finally determined; on a later request, agency notifies submitter, who has 10 business days to submit a written statement; agency issues a written determination within 7 business days; a denial may be appealed within 7 business days and is determined within 10 business days; Article 78 review must be commenced within 15 days. Flag: largely inapplicable to municipal requests.

Law-enforcement disciplinary records path (§ 86(6), § 89(2-b) mandatory and § 89(2-c) permissive redactions): before disclosure, a law-enforcement agency must redact enumerated items (officer medical history, home/personal contact info, SSNs, EAP/mental-health/substance-abuse use) and may redact technical-infraction records. Creates a record-type-specific redaction workflow and an employee-notification policy duty (§ 89 subd. relating to notification / § 87(6)).

material_negatives.note: No explicit statutory clarification/cure clock. FOIL's only intake-adequacy standard is that a record be 'reasonably described' (§ 89(3)(a)); there is no statutory deadline for a requester to narrow or clarify a request. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists (COOG guidance encourages agencies to assist).

No statutory abandonment/closure trigger for requester non-response (e.g., failure to pay or clarify). Statute conditions production on 'payment of, or offer to pay' (§ 89(3)(a)) but sets no time limit after which a request is deemed abandoned.

No statutory advance-deposit percentage or dollar threshold in Article 6. Production is gated on 'payment of, or offer to pay' the prescribed fee (§ 89(3)(a)); no formula (e.g., '50% deposit if over $X') is provided by statute.

No fixed numeric outer deadline for actual production. After the 5-business-day response and the 20-business-day checkpoint, the operative standard is a 'date certain within a reasonable period' (§ 89(3)(a)) — a soft standard, not a hard statewide cap.

There is no fixed statewide per-page fee. The 25 cents/page figure is a CEILING (§ 87(1)(b)(iii)); municipalities set their own per-page fee up to that cap, and no statutory floor exists. (Captured affirmatively as NY-0024.)

No statutory requirement or prohibition governing rolling/installment production of voluminous requests; the statute addresses timing via the acknowledgement/date-certain mechanism rather than mandated installments.

Article 6 uses 'business days' for the 5-, 20-, and 10-day windows but 'days' (unqualified) for the 30-day appeal-filing window (§ 89(4)(a)); the article does not itself define how business days are counted (e.g., holidays).

EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(c) attorney's fees and litigation costs ('may assess' / 'shall assess' where petitioner 'substantially prevailed' and agency 'had no reasonable basis'): a Remedy on the Remove list. The linked constructive-denial trigger it references is captured at NY-0013/NY-0040.
EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(d) and § 89(5)(d) appellate procedure (preference, 60-day abandonment, CPLR 5513 appeals): litigation procedure, not request-handling behavior.

EXCLUDED — § 89(4)(b) / § 89(5)(f) burden of proof in an Article 78 proceeding (agency must prove exemption): litigation burden; the operational duty to give particularized justification is captured at NY-0034.

EXCLUDED — § 87(3)(a)-(b) duty to maintain a final-vote record and an employee name/title/salary roster, and § 87(3)(c) annually-updated subject-matter list: general recordkeeping obligations (Remove list), not per-request processing.
EXCLUDED — § 89(8) criminal violation for willful concealment/destruction of a record: a penalty provision (Remove list).

EXCLUDED — § 89(7) non-disclosure of home addresses of officers/employees/retirees/applicants: an exemption (special record content), not a processing step; belongs to the exemption catalog rather than the workflow.

SCOPE FLAG (not excluded, but municipally inapplicable) — § 89(3)(c) online-submission duty and § 87(3)(c)/§ 87(4)(c) website-posting duties apply to 'state agency' only, so they do not bind ordinary municipalities. Municipal platforms should treat these as state-agency configuration.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to any person
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must make all public records available to any person for inspection or copying, except records exempt under Sections 7 and 8.5.
rules.trigger: None stated (any person may request)
rules.source_language: Each public body shall make available to any person for inspection or copying all public records, except as otherwise provided in Sections 7 and 8.5 of this Act.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key. Sections 7 (exemptions) and 8.5 (mandatory-disclosure carve-outs) are the exception surfaces; not inventoried here.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not require a requester to state the purpose of a request, except to determine commercial-purpose status or to rule on a fee-waiver request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form or require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver.
rules.notes: Two carve-outs: commercial-purpose determination drives fee basis; fee-waiver determination drives fee reduction. Same sentence also supports IL-0004.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may request public records; the Act imposes no residency or citizenship condition on the right of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Each public body shall make available to any person for inspection or copying all public records, except as otherwise provided in Sections 7 and 8.5 of this Act.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key emitted as a rule per discovery discipline #2. Source language is the verbatim any-person clause; the absence of any residency limitation is inferred from that clause and from the broad Section 2 definition of Person. Not a separate operative sentence.

rules.legal_concept: No mandatory request form
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A public body may not require that a request be submitted on a standard form or require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver.
rules.notes: Section 3(c) also requires that requests be made in writing for the 5-day clock to run, but permits oral requests to be honored (IL-0005).

rules.legal_concept: Oral requests may be honored
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may honor oral requests for inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: Requester makes an oral request
rules.source_language: A public body may honor oral requests for inspection or copying.
rules.notes: Permissive (may). The statutory response clock in Section 3(d) attaches to a written request; oral requests are discretionary.

rules.legal_concept: Freedom of Information officer designation
rules.atomic_rule: Each public body must designate one or more officials or employees to act as its Freedom of Information officer(s).
rules.trigger: None stated (standing duty)
rules.source_language: Each public body shall designate one or more officials or employees to act as its Freedom of Information officer or officers.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver (who-must-respond / routing). Drives routing of an incoming request to a designated FOIA officer.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA officer notes receipt date and computes due date
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receiving a request, the FOIA officer must note the date the public body received the written request and compute and record the date the response period expires.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: start event = date written request received; due-date computed per Section 3(d)/(e)
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a request for a public record, the Freedom of Information officer shall: (1) note the date the public body receives the written request; (2) compute the day on which the period for response will expire and make a notation of that date on the written request...
rules.notes: Establishes the clock-start mechanic that IL-0010 depends on. Verbatim captured for paragraphs (1)-(2); later paragraphs of 3.5(b) continue the officer's duties.

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that records are open
rules.atomic_rule: All records in the custody or possession of a public body are presumed open to inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: None stated (default state)
rules.source_language: All records in the custody or possession of a public body are presumed to be open to inspection or copying.
rules.notes: Default classification the engine starts from; overcome only by an asserted exemption carrying the IL-0009 burden.

rules.legal_concept: Burden of proving exemption
rules.atomic_rule: A public body asserting a record is exempt bears the burden of proving the exemption by clear and convincing evidence.
rules.trigger: Public body asserts a record is exempt
rules.source_language: Any public body that asserts that a record is exempt from disclosure has the burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence that it is exempt.
rules.notes: Same evidentiary standard is restated in Section 11 for judicial review; one concept, cited to both.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must comply with or deny a written request within 5 business days after receipt, unless the time is properly extended.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Each public body shall, promptly, either comply with or deny a request for public records within 5 business days after its receipt of the request, unless the time for response is properly extended under subsection (e) of this Section.
rules.notes: Statute also imposes a co-standard: response must be prompt (the word promptly modifies the 5-day cap). Commercial (IL-0017), recurrent (IL-0020), and voluminous (IL-0024) requests run on different windows.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may extend the response time by not more than 5 business days beyond the original due date for any of seven enumerated reasons.
rules.trigger: One of seven enumerated conditions (records off-site; substantial collection; categorical/extensive search; records not yet located; exemption review; undue operational burden; need for consultation)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 5 business-days beyond original due date
rules.source_language: The time for response under this Section may be extended by the public body for not more than 5 business days from the original due date for any of the following reasons: (i) the requested records are stored in whole or in part at other locations than the office having charge of the requested records; (ii) the request requires the collection of a substantial number of specified records; (iii) the request is couched in categorical terms and requires an extensive search for the records responsive to it; (iv) the requested records have not been located in the course of routine search and additional efforts are being made to locate them; (v) the requested records require examination and evaluation by personnel having the necessary competence and discretion to determine if they are exempt from disclosure under Section 7 of this Act or should be revealed only with appropriate deletions; (vi) the request for records cannot be complied with by the public body within the time limits prescribed by subsection (d) of this Section without unduly burdening or interfering with the operations of the public body; (vii) there is a need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another public body or among 2 or more components of a public body having a substantial interest in the determination or in the subject matter of the request.
rules.notes: Ceiling of 5 business days is fixed by statute; the enumerated reasons are the gating conditions. Extension is optional (may).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of extension
rules.atomic_rule: When it extends, the public body must, within 5 business days after receipt, notify the requester of the reasons for the extension and the date the response will be forthcoming.
rules.trigger: Public body invokes an extension under Section 3(e)
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: When additional time is required for any of the above reasons, the public body shall, within 5 business days after receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of the reasons for the extension and the date by which the response will be forthcoming.
rules.notes: Required notice (structural) with a fixed timing; failure to give it defaults back to the 5-day denial trigger (IL-0014).

rules.legal_concept: Extension by written agreement
rules.atomic_rule: The requester and the public body may agree in writing to extend the time for compliance for a period determined by the parties.
rules.trigger: Written agreement between requester and public body
rules.clock_spec: period agreed in writing by the parties (no statutory cap)
rules.source_language: The person making a request and the public body may agree in writing to extend the time for compliance for a period to be determined by the parties.
rules.notes: An agreed extension has no statutory day-count; the parties set it. Distinct from the 5-day unilateral extension (IL-0011).

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond is a denial
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to comply with, extend the time for, or deny a written request within 5 business days after receipt is treated as a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: 5 business days elapse with no compliance, extension, or denial
rules.clock_spec: denial deemed at expiry of 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Failure to comply with a written request, extend the time for response, or deny a request within 5 business days after its receipt shall be considered a denial of the request.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3 (constructive denial). A deemed denial opens the PAC-review and judicial-review paths (final denial for review purposes).

rules.legal_concept: Unduly burdensome categorical request
rules.atomic_rule: A request for all records within a category may be denied only if compliance would be unduly burdensome, there is no way to narrow it, and the burden outweighs the public interest in the information.
rules.trigger: Categorical request whose compliance is unduly burdensome with no way to narrow
rules.source_language: Requests calling for all records falling within a category shall be complied with unless compliance with the request would be unduly burdensome for the complying public body and there is no way to narrow the request and the burden on the public body outweighs the public interest in the information.
rules.notes: Conjunctive three-part test kept in one row (not fragmented). Gated by the mandatory confer step in IL-0016.

rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to confer
rules.atomic_rule: Before denying a categorical request as unduly burdensome, the public body must give the requester an opportunity to confer to reduce the request to manageable proportions.
rules.trigger: Public body intends to invoke the unduly-burdensome exemption
rules.source_language: Before invoking this exemption, the public body shall extend to the person making the request an opportunity to confer with it in an attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions.
rules.notes: Mandatory precondition to the IL-0015 denial path.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial-purpose request response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a request for records to be used for a commercial purpose within 21 working days after receipt.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose
rules.clock_spec: 21 working-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: A public body shall respond to a request for records to be used for a commercial purpose within 21 working days after receipt.
rules.notes: Source term is working days (distinct from business days used elsewhere). Commercial-purpose is a Section 2 defined classification branch.

rules.legal_concept: Required content of commercial-request response
rules.atomic_rule: The commercial-request response must do one of four things: give a time-and-fee estimate, deny under an exemption, notify the request is unduly burdensome with an opportunity to narrow, or provide the records.
rules.trigger: Public body responds to a commercial-purpose request
rules.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested.
rules.notes: Four-branch response menu specific to commercial requests. Prepayment permission split out as IL-0019.

rules.legal_concept: Full prepayment before copying
rules.atomic_rule: When it gives a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request, the public body may require the requester to pay the fees in full before copying the requested documents.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request
rules.source_language: provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents
rules.notes: Payment gate. Identical prepayment language appears in Section 3.2(a) for recurrent requesters; one concept cited to both.

rules.legal_concept: Recurrent-requester response time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a request from a recurrent requester within 21 business days after receipt.
rules.trigger: Requester meets the recurrent-requester definition
rules.clock_spec: 21 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a public body shall respond to a request from a recurrent requester...within 21 business days after receipt
rules.notes: Source term is business days (vs working days for commercial, IL-0017). Elided text in the quote is the intervening statutory clause naming the recurrent requester; captured operative window verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Five-day recurrent-requester notice
rules.atomic_rule: Within 5 business days after receiving a request from a recurrent requester, the public body must notify the requester that it is being treated under the recurrent-requester provisions.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a request from a recurrent requester
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Within 5 business days after receiving a request from a recurrent requester...the public body shall notify the requester
rules.notes: Required notice with a fixed 5-business-day timing. Elided text names the recurrent-requester status the notice addresses.

rules.legal_concept: Recurrent requester
rules.atomic_rule: A requester is a recurrent requester if, in the prior 12 months, it submitted to the same public body at least 50 requests, or at least 15 within a 30-day period, or at least 7 within a 7-day period.
rules.trigger: Request-volume thresholds met against the same public body
rules.source_language: "Recurrent requester", as used in Section 3.2 of this Act, means a person that, in the 12 months immediately preceding the request, has submitted to the same public body (i) a minimum of 50 requests for records, (ii) a minimum of 15 requests for records within a 30-day period, or (iii) a minimum of 7 requests for records within a 7-day period.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (drives the recurrent-requester workflow). Thresholds are state-fixed; the city cannot change them, so treated as a structural classification fork rather than a city parameter.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request
rules.atomic_rule: A request is voluminous if it includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records within 20 business days, or requires compiling more than 500 letter/legal-sized pages (unless a single record exceeds 500 pages).
rules.trigger: Category-count or page-volume thresholds met
rules.source_language: "Voluminous request" means a request that: (i) includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records or a combination of individual requests that total requests for more than 5 different categories of records in a period of 20 business days; or (ii) requires the compilation of more than 500 letter or legal-sized pages of public records unless a single requested record exceeds 500 pages.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on (drives the voluminous-request workflow and its fee tiers). Full statutory definition (including the exclusions for requests from news media, non-profits, etc.) may carry further carve-outs; captured core thresholds verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request initial response
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must respond to a voluminous request within 5 business days after receipt (notifying the requester it is being treated as voluminous).
rules.trigger: Request meets the voluminous-request definition
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: a public body shall respond to a voluminous request within 5 business days after receipt.
rules.notes: This initial response notifies the requester the request is voluminous and triggers the requester-response window (IL-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Requester response to voluminous notice
rules.atomic_rule: After the public body's voluminous-request response, the requester must respond within 10 business days; if the requester does not respond (or the request remains voluminous), the public body responds and assesses any fees.
rules.trigger: Public body sends its voluminous-request response
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from the public body's response being sent
rules.source_language: the requester must respond to the public body within 10 business days after the public body's response was sent
rules.notes: Statute does not state that non-response withdraws the request; if the requester does not respond within 10 business days the public body proceeds to respond and assess fees. Requester-facing deadline, so config_home structural.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous request final response
rules.atomic_rule: The public body must give its final voluminous-request response within the earlier of 5 business days after receiving the requester's response or 5 business days after the final day for the requester to respond.
rules.trigger: Requester responds, or the requester-response window closes
rules.clock_spec: earlier of 5 business-days from requester's response OR 5 business-days from final day for requester to respond
rules.source_language: the public body shall respond within the earlier of 5 business days after it receives the response from the requester or 5 business days after the final day for the requester to respond
rules.notes: Two-branch earlier-of calculation kept in one row.

rules.legal_concept: First 50 pages free
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the first 50 pages of black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies requested.
rules.trigger: Requester requests black-and-white letter/legal copies
rules.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
rules.notes: Fixed 50-page free threshold set by state; the city cannot lower it.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page copy fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies (after the free 50) may not exceed 15 cents per page.
rules.trigger: Copies beyond the first 50 black-and-white letter/legal pages
rules.source_language: The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page.
rules.notes: Ceiling of 15 cents; the city sets the operative rate at or below it. Same concept whether a city charges a fixed 10 cents or the full 15 cents.

rules.legal_concept: Color/non-standard copy cost
rules.atomic_rule: For copies in color or in a size other than letter/legal, a public body may not charge more than its actual cost of reproduction.
rules.trigger: Copies in color or a non-letter/legal size
rules.source_language: If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual cost (no fixed number).

rules.legal_concept: Certification fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: The cost for certifying a record may not exceed $1.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified record
rules.source_language: The cost for certifying a record shall not exceed $1.
rules.notes: Ceiling of $1 per certification.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic recording-medium cost
rules.atomic_rule: For records provided in electronic format, a public body may charge the requester only the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium.
rules.trigger: Records furnished in electronic format on a recording medium
rules.source_language: A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual medium cost. Voluminous electronic requests have their own tiered caps (IL-0038).

rules.legal_concept: No search/review fee (non-commercial)
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge the requester for the cost of any search for and review of the records.
rules.trigger: Any non-commercial request
rules.source_language: a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records.
rules.notes: General prohibition on search/review charges; the only exception is the commercial-request hourly fee in Section 6(f) (IL-0035).

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: Documents must be furnished without charge or at reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the requester states a specific purpose and the waiver is in the public interest (principally to disseminate information on public health/safety/welfare or legal rights, not for personal/commercial benefit).
rules.trigger: Requester states a specific purpose and asserts the waiver is in the public interest
rules.source_language: Documents shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the person requesting the documents states the specific purpose for the request and indicates that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest. Waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest if the principal purpose of the request is to access and disseminate information regarding the health, safety and welfare or the legal rights of the general public and is not for the principal purpose of personal or commercial benefit.
rules.notes: Soft public-interest standard the engine applies (a discretionary waiver path), so config_home structural. The public-interest test is one of the two allowed purpose inquiries (see IL-0002).

rules.legal_concept: Furnish in requested electronic format
rules.atomic_rule: When a person requests a copy of a record maintained in electronic format, the public body must furnish it in the electronic format the requester specifies, if feasible.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies an electronic format for an electronically-maintained record
rules.source_language: When a person requests a copy of a record maintained in an electronic format, the public body shall furnish it in the electronic format specified by the requester, if feasible.
rules.notes: Duty qualified by an if-feasible standard the engine applies; kept as one row.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial-request search/redaction hourly fee
rules.atomic_rule: For a commercial request, a public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel searching for, retrieving, or examining the record for necessary redactions.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose
rules.source_language: A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions.
rules.notes: Ceiling of $10/hour; applies only to commercial requests. This is the sole exception to the no-search-fee rule (IL-0032).

rules.legal_concept: First 8 search hours free (commercial)
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel searching for or retrieving a requested record on a commercial request.
rules.trigger: Commercial request incurring personnel search/retrieval time
rules.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record.
rules.notes: Fixed 8-hour free floor before the IL-0035 hourly fee applies. Applies only to commercial requests.

rules.legal_concept: Accounting of commercial-request fees
rules.atomic_rule: If it imposes a Section 6(f) fee, the public body must provide the requester an accounting of all fees, costs, and personnel hours connected with the request.
rules.trigger: Public body imposes a commercial-request fee under Section 6(f)
rules.source_language: If a public body imposes a fee pursuant to this subsection (f), it must provide the requester with an accounting of all fees, costs, and personnel hours in connection with the request for public records.
rules.notes: Required document tied to commercial fees only.

rules.legal_concept: Voluminous electronic-data fee tiers
rules.atomic_rule: For a voluminous request for electronic records, a public body may charge tiered caps by data size: for non-PDF data up to $20 (<=2 MB), $40 (2-4 MB), or $100 (>4 MB); for PDF data up to $20 (<=80 MB), $40 (80-160 MB), or $100 (>160 MB).
rules.trigger: Voluminous request for electronic records
rules.source_language: If a voluminous request is for electronic records and those records are not in a portable document format (PDF), the public body may charge up to $20 for not more than 2 megabytes of data, up to $40 for more than 2 but not more than 4 megabytes of data, and up to $100 for more than 4 megabytes of data. [For PDF:] up to $20 for not more than 80 megabytes of data, up to $40 for more than 80 megabytes but not more than 160 megabytes of data, and up to $100 for more than 160 megabytes of data.
rules.notes: One concept (voluminous electronic-data cap) with two format bases (PDF vs non-PDF) kept in one row per the do-not-split guidance. All tiers are ceilings.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of denial
rules.atomic_rule: A public body denying a request must notify the requester in writing of the decision to deny.
rules.trigger: Public body denies a request (in whole or part)
rules.source_language: Each public body denying a request for public records shall notify the requester in writing of the decision to deny the request.
rules.notes: Required denial document; the required contents are IL-0040 through IL-0042.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of denial notice
rules.atomic_rule: The denial notice must specify the exemption claimed and the specific reasons for the denial, including a detailed factual basis and a citation to supporting legal authority.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial
rules.source_language: the notice of denial shall specify the exemption claimed to authorize the denial and the specific reasons for the denial, including a detailed factual basis and a citation to supporting legal authority.
rules.notes: Mandatory content of the denial notice.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of right to PAC review
rules.atomic_rule: Each denial notice must inform the requester of the right to review by the Public Access Counselor and provide the PAC's address and phone number.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial
rules.source_language: Each notice of denial shall also inform such person of the right to review by the Public Access Counselor and provide the address and phone number for the Public Access Counselor.
rules.notes: Connects the denial to the administrative-review path (IL-0043).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of right to judicial review
rules.atomic_rule: Each denial notice must inform the requester of the right to judicial review.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial
rules.source_language: Each notice of denial shall inform such person of his right to judicial review under Section 11 of this Act.
rules.notes: Connects the denial to the judicial-review path (IL-0047).

rules.legal_concept: Request for review with Public Access Counselor
rules.atomic_rule: A person whose request is denied may file a request for review with the Public Access Counselor (except against the General Assembly and its committees/commissions/agencies).
rules.trigger: Public body denies a request
rules.source_language: A person whose request to inspect or copy a public record is denied by a public body, except the General Assembly and committees, commissions, and agencies thereof, may file a request for review with the Public Access Counselor established in the Office of the Attorney General not later than 60 days after the date of the final denial.
rules.notes: Administrative-review fork (namespaced appeal.administrative). Filing deadline split as IL-0044.

rules.legal_concept: PAC review filing deadline
rules.atomic_rule: A request for review with the PAC must be filed not later than 60 days after the date of the final denial.
rules.trigger: Final denial of the request
rules.clock_spec: 60 days from date of final denial
rules.source_language: ...may file a request for review with the Public Access Counselor established in the Office of the Attorney General not later than 60 days after the date of the final denial.
rules.notes: Requester-facing filing deadline; state-fixed 60-day window.

rules.legal_concept: Public body cooperation with PAC
rules.atomic_rule: Within 7 business days after receiving the request for review, the public body must provide copies of the requested records to the PAC and otherwise fully cooperate.
rules.trigger: Public body receives the PAC request for review
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from receipt of request for review
rules.source_language: Within 7 business days after receipt of the request for review, the public body shall provide copies of records requested and shall otherwise fully cooperate with the Public Access Counselor.
rules.notes: Public-body-facing deadline within the administrative-review path.

rules.legal_concept: Binding PAC opinion
rules.atomic_rule: The Attorney General must examine the issues and records, make findings of fact and conclusions of law, and issue a binding opinion within 60 days after receipt of the request for review.
rules.trigger: PAC proceeds to a binding opinion on the request for review
rules.clock_spec: 60 days from receipt of request for review
rules.source_language: the Attorney General shall examine the issues and the records, shall make findings of fact and conclusions of law, and shall issue to the requester and the public body an opinion in response to the request for review within 60 days after its receipt. The opinion shall be binding upon both the requester and the public body.
rules.notes: The 60-day period may be extended by up to 21 business days under the statute (extension clause not captured verbatim here). Binding opinion is itself reviewable in the Appellate Court under the Administrative Review Law.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial review in circuit court
rules.atomic_rule: Any person denied access to inspect or copy a public record may file suit for injunctive or declaratory relief in circuit court.
rules.trigger: Person is denied access to records
rules.source_language: Any person denied access to inspect or copy any public record by a public body may file suit for injunctive or declaratory relief.
rules.notes: Judicial-review fork (namespaced appeal.judicial), distinct from the administrative PAC path. A requester may go to court without first seeking PAC review.

rules.legal_concept: Venue for FOIA suit
rules.atomic_rule: Suit against a State public body may be filed in the circuit court for the county where the public body has its principal office or where the person denied access resides.
rules.trigger: Person files a FOIA suit against a State public body
rules.source_language: Where the denial is from a public body of the State, suit may be filed in the circuit court for the county where the public body has its principal office or where the person denied access resides.
rules.notes: Venue rule for the judicial path.

structural_branches.description: Commercial-purpose path: a request classified as commercial runs on a 21-working-day window with a four-branch response menu (estimate/deny/burden-notice/produce) and its own $10/hour search fee — a distinct pipeline from ordinary requests.
Recurrent-requester path: a requester meeting the 50/12mo, 15/30d, or 7/7d thresholds is routed to a 21-business-day window with a mandatory 5-business-day notice and prepayment option.

Voluminous-request path: a request meeting the category-count or 500-page thresholds enters a multi-step handshake (5-day initial response, 10-business-day requester response, earlier-of final response) with tiered electronic-data fees.
Unduly-burdensome denial path: a categorical request can exit via a three-part burden test, but only after a mandatory confer-to-narrow step.
