Agreed-extension path: requester and public body can extend the compliance deadline by written agreement for a party-determined period with no statutory cap.
Fee-waiver path: a discretionary branch applying a soft public-interest standard (health/safety/welfare/legal-rights dissemination, not personal/commercial benefit) to waive or reduce fees.

Administrative-review path: a denial (including a deemed denial) can be taken to the Public Access Counselor within 60 days, triggering a 7-business-day public-body cooperation deadline and a 60-day binding opinion.

Judicial-review path: a denied requester may sue for injunctive/declaratory relief in circuit court, with venue rules and a clear-and-convincing burden on the public body — available independently of PAC review.

material_negatives.note: No separate acknowledgment-of-receipt deadline distinct from the substantive response. Illinois folds acknowledgment into the 5-business-day comply-or-deny window (Section 3(d)); there is no statutory duty to send a bare receipt confirmation on a shorter clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No general clarification clock that tolls or restarts the response deadline when a request is ambiguous. The only statutory clarification mechanism is the confer-to-narrow duty for an unduly-burdensome categorical request (IL-0016), which does not itself pause the clock.

No statutory requirement that municipalities maintain or publish a public request-tracking log. Section 3.5 requires the FOIA officer to note the receipt date and compute the due date internally, but this is an internal notation, not a mandated tracking system.
No filing fee is imposed for a request for review to the Public Access Counselor; the administrative-review path is free to the requester. Stated as an absence of any fee provision in Section 9.5.
No explicit statutory translation or language-access requirement for processing a request within FOIA (5 ILCS 140). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No general statutory deposit threshold (e.g., prepay when estimate exceeds $X) for ordinary requests. Full-prepayment-before-copying is permitted only on commercial (Section 3.1) and recurrent-requester (Section 3.2) estimates (IL-0019); no analogous deposit rule was found for standard requests.

rules.legal_concept: Records open to citizens of the Commonwealth and in-state media
rules.atomic_rule: Public records are open only to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of newspapers/magazines with circulation in, and radio/TV stations broadcasting in or into, the Commonwealth; the engine may restrict standing to these requester classes.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise specifically provided by law, all public records shall be open to citizens of the Commonwealth, representatives of newspapers and magazines with circulation in the Commonwealth, and representatives of radio and television stations broadcasting in or into the Commonwealth during the regular office hours of the custodian of such records.
rules.notes: Virginia is one of the few states with a requester-residency limitation (upheld in McBurney v. Young, 569 U.S. 221 (2013)). Do NOT map to eligibility.any_person or eligibility.no_residency_requirement — VFOIA affirmatively restricts standing.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to obtain public records; the custodian may require only the requester's name and legal address.
rules.trigger: Any records request
rules.source_language: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry. is_paraphrase=true because 'no purpose required' is an inference from the enumerated permission (name + legal address only); VFOIA states no purpose condition affirmatively.

rules.legal_concept: Access by inspection or copies at requester's option
rules.atomic_rule: Access is provided by inspection or by providing copies of the requested records, at the option of the requester.
rules.trigger: Access is provided
rules.source_language: Access to such records shall be provided by the custodian in accordance with this chapter by inspection or by providing copies of the requested records, at the option of the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may require name and legal address
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.
rules.trigger: Request received
rules.source_language: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.

rules.legal_concept: Request must identify records with reasonable specificity
rules.atomic_rule: A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable specificity' is an undefined soft standard the engine applies at intake; not a numeric threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Request need not reference the chapter
rules.atomic_rule: A request need not reference VFOIA to invoke the chapter's provisions or to impose the response time limits on the public body.
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: The request need not make reference to this chapter in order to invoke the provisions of this chapter or to impose the time limits for response by a public body.

rules.legal_concept: Five-working-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall, promptly but in all cases within five working days of receiving a request, provide the records or make one of four written responses.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 5 working days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Any public body that is subject to this chapter and that is the custodian of the requested records shall promptly, but in all cases within five working days of receiving a request, provide the requested records to the requester or make one of the following responses in writing:

rules.legal_concept: Additional seven work days when response not practically possible
rules.atomic_rule: If, within the five-work-day period, the body responds in writing that it is not practically possible to provide the records or determine availability and specifies the conditions making a response impossible, it gets an additional seven work days to make one of the four responses.
rules.trigger: Body determines it is not practically possible to respond within 5 working days and says so in writing within that period
rules.clock_spec: fixed: additional 7 work days from the original 5-working-day response
rules.source_language: It is not practically possible to provide the requested records or to determine whether they are available within the five-work-day period. Such response shall specify the conditions that make a response impossible. If the response is made within five working days, the public body shall have an additional seven work days ... in which to provide one of the four preceding responses.

rules.legal_concept: Sixty work days for criminal investigative files
rules.atomic_rule: For a request for criminal investigative files under § 2.2-3706.1, the additional extension when a response is not practically possible is 60 work days rather than seven.
rules.trigger: Not-practically-possible response to a request for criminal investigative files under § 2.2-3706.1
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 60 work days (in lieu of 7) from the original 5-working-day response
rules.source_language: the public body shall have an additional seven work days or, in the case of a request for criminal investigative files pursuant to § 2.2-3706.1, 60 work days in which to provide one of the four preceding responses.

rules.legal_concept: Petition court for additional time — extraordinary volume/search
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search that would prevent it from meeting operational responsibilities, but must first make reasonable efforts to reach agreement with the requester.
rules.trigger: Request for extraordinary volume or requiring extraordinarily lengthy search
rules.source_language: Any public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond to a request for records when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search, and a response by the public body within the time required by this chapter will prevent the public body from meeting its operational responsibilities. Before proceeding with the petition, however, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to reach an agreement with the requester concerning the production of the records requested.
rules.notes: Structural fork: an external court-extension path with an antecedent duty to attempt agreement; no fixed day-count set.

rules.legal_concept: Entire-withholding response requirements
rules.atomic_rule: A response withholding records entirely shall identify with reasonable particularity the volume and subject matter of withheld records and cite, as to each category, the specific Code section authorizing the withholding.
rules.trigger: Records withheld in their entirety
rules.source_language: The requested records are being entirely withheld. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the volume and subject matter of withheld records, and cite, as to each category of withheld records, the specific Code section that authorizes the withholding of the records.

rules.legal_concept: Partial provide/withhold response requirements
rules.atomic_rule: A response providing records in part and withholding in part shall identify with reasonable particularity the subject matter of withheld portions and cite, as to each category, the specific Code section authorizing the withholding.
rules.trigger: Records provided in part and withheld in part
rules.source_language: The requested records are being provided in part and are being withheld in part. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the subject matter of withheld portions, and cite, as to each category of withheld records, the specific Code section that authorizes the withholding of the records.

rules.legal_concept: Records could not be found or do not exist — referral
rules.atomic_rule: If records could not be found or do not exist, the response says so; and if the receiving body knows another public body has the records, the response shall include contact information for that other public body.
rules.trigger: Records not found or nonexistent; receiving body knows another body holds them
rules.source_language: The requested records could not be found or do not exist. However, if the public body that received the request knows that another public body has the requested records, the response shall include contact information for the other public body.
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver: obligates a referral hand-off to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: No public body is required to create a new record that does not already exist, but it may abstract or summarize information under terms agreed with the requester.
rules.trigger: Requested record does not already exist
rules.source_language: Subject to the provisions of subsection G, no public body shall be required to create a new record if the record does not already exist. However, a public body may abstract or summarize information under such terms and conditions as agreed between the requester and the public body.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond is a deemed denial and violation
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond to a request within the statutory period is deemed a denial of the request and constitutes a violation of the chapter.
rules.trigger: No response made within the applicable response deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal: expiry of the 5-working-day (or extended) response window with no response = deemed denial
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to a request for records shall be deemed a denial of the request and shall constitute a violation of this chapter.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial keeper-sliver: the terminal trigger only; the remedy/penalty amount is excluded.

rules.legal_concept: Access to records in an electronic database
rules.atomic_rule: Records maintained in an electronic data processing system or database shall be made available at a reasonable cost not exceeding actual cost; where databases combine exempt and nonexempt records, the body shall provide access to the nonexempt records.
rules.trigger: Requested records held in an electronic database or structured data collection
rules.source_language: Public records maintained by a public body in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or any other structured collection of data shall be made available to a requester at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F. When electronic or other databases are combined or contain exempt and nonexempt records, the public body may provide access to the exempt records if not otherwise prohibited by law, but shall provide access to the nonexempt records as provided by this chapter.

rules.legal_concept: Excision or format conversion is not creation of a new record
rules.atomic_rule: Excising exempt fields from a database, or converting data from one available format to another, is not deemed the creation, preparation, or compilation of a new public record.
rules.trigger: Redaction of database fields or format conversion during production
rules.source_language: The excision of exempt fields of information from a database or the conversion of data from one available format to another shall not be deemed the creation, preparation, or compilation of a new public record.

rules.legal_concept: Production in any tangible medium identified by requester
rules.atomic_rule: The body shall produce nonexempt database records in any tangible medium identified by the requester — including, where it has the capability, posting on a website or delivery to a requester-provided email address — if that medium is used in the regular course of business.
rules.trigger: Requester identifies a tangible medium for production
rules.source_language: Public bodies shall produce nonexempt records maintained in an electronic database in any tangible medium identified by the requester, including, where the public body has the capability, the option of posting the records on a website or delivering the records through an electronic mail address provided by the requester, if that medium is used by the public body in the regular course of business.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to produce in a format not regularly used
rules.atomic_rule: No public body is required to produce records from an electronic database in a format not regularly used by it, but it shall make reasonable efforts to provide records in any format under terms agreed with the requester, including payment of reasonable costs.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a format the body does not regularly use
rules.source_language: No public body shall be required to produce records from an electronic database in a format not regularly used by the public body. However, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to provide records in any format under such terms and conditions as agreed between the requester and public body, including the payment of reasonable costs.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to redact and disclose nonexempt portions
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not withhold an entire record because some portion is excluded; a record may be withheld in full only where an exclusion applies to its entire content, otherwise only the excluded portions are withheld and all nonexcluded portions shall be disclosed.
rules.trigger: Record contains both excluded and nonexcluded information
rules.source_language: No provision of this chapter is intended, nor shall it be construed or applied, to authorize a public body to withhold a public record in its entirety on the grounds that some portion of the public record is excluded from disclosure by this chapter or by any other provision of law. A public record may be withheld from disclosure in its entirety only to the extent that an exclusion from disclosure under this chapter or other provision of law applies to the entire content of the public record. Otherwise, only those portions of the public record containing information subject to an exclusion under this chapter or other provision of law may be withheld, and all portions of the public record that are not so excluded shall be disclosed.

rules.legal_concept: Charges not to exceed actual cost incurred
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records.
rules.trigger: Body incurs cost in responding
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost incurred in accessing/duplicating/supplying/searching
rules.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
rules.notes: State sets a ceiling (actual cost); the city sets its actual per-request charge under it. No statewide fixed per-page rate exists.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to supply at lowest possible cost
rules.atomic_rule: The body shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
rules.trigger: Body sets charges for a request
rules.clock_spec: soft-standard: 'lowest possible cost'
rules.source_language: and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.

rules.legal_concept: No extraneous/intermediary/surplus fees
rules.atomic_rule: No public body shall impose extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs of creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.
rules.trigger: Body assesses charges
rules.source_language: No public body shall impose any extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs associated with creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.

rules.legal_concept: Duplicating fee not to exceed actual cost of duplication
rules.atomic_rule: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.
rules.trigger: Body charges a duplicating fee
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of duplication
rules.source_language: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.

rules.legal_concept: Pre-search written notice of possible charges
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to conducting a search for records, the body shall notify the requester in writing that it may make reasonable charges not to exceed actual cost and inquire whether the requester would like a cost estimate in advance.
rules.trigger: Before conducting a search for records
rules.source_language: Prior to conducting a search for records, the public body shall notify the requester in writing that the public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for requested records and inquire of the requester whether he would like to request a cost estimate in advance of the supplying of the requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate provided on request
rules.atomic_rule: The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a cost estimate
rules.source_language: The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.

rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled pending requester's estimate response
rules.atomic_rule: The response period is tolled for the amount of time that elapses between the public body's notice of the cost estimate and the requester's response.
rules.trigger: Cost estimate sent; awaiting requester's response
rules.clock_spec: tolls: from notice of cost estimate until requester responds
rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the cost estimate and the response of the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Request deemed withdrawn after 30 days' silence on cost estimate
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request is deemed withdrawn.
rules.trigger: No requester response within 30 days of the cost estimate being sent
rules.clock_spec: fixed terminal: 30 days from sending the cost estimate = deemed withdrawn
rules.source_language: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn.

rules.legal_concept: Estimating cost credited toward overall charges
rules.atomic_rule: Any costs incurred by the public body in estimating the cost of supplying the records shall be applied toward the overall charges to be paid by the requester.
rules.trigger: Body incurs cost preparing a cost estimate
rules.source_language: Any costs incurred by the public body in estimating the cost of supplying the requested records shall be applied toward the overall charges to be paid by the requester for the supplying of such requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Local body may offer an electronic method of payment
rules.atomic_rule: Any local public body that charges for producing records may provide an electronic method of payment (noncash, non-paper-check — credit/debit cards, direct deposit/debit, electronic checks, telephonic payment).
rules.trigger: Local public body charges for record production
rules.source_language: Any local public body that charges for the production of records pursuant to this section may provide an electronic method of payment through which all payments for the production of such records to such locality may be made.

rules.legal_concept: Advance deposit when charges likely to exceed $200
rules.atomic_rule: Where a public body determines in advance that charges are likely to exceed $200, it may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
rules.trigger: Advance determination that charges are likely to exceed $200
rules.clock_spec: fixed threshold: $200; deposit ceiling = the advance-determination amount
rules.source_language: In any case where a public body determines in advance that charges for producing the requested records are likely to exceed $200, the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
rules.notes: $200 is a state-fixed trigger threshold; the deposit itself is capped at the body's advance determination (a ceiling).

rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled pending advance-determination response
rules.atomic_rule: The response period is tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the requester's response.
rules.trigger: Advance determination (deposit demand) sent; awaiting requester's response
rules.clock_spec: tolls: from notice of advance determination until requester responds
rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the response of the requester.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for FERPA scholastic records to parent/guardian/eligible student
rules.atomic_rule: The reasonable-charge fee provisions do not apply to scholastic records that must be made available under FERPA when requested by a parent or legal guardian of a minor student or by a student who is 18 or older.
rules.trigger: Request for scholastic records under § 2.2-3705.4(A)(1) by parent/guardian or student 18+
rules.source_language: Except with regard to scholastic records requested pursuant to subdivision A 1 of § 2.2-3705.4 that must be made available for inspection pursuant to the federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (20 U.S.C. § 1232g) and such requests for scholastic records by a parent or legal guardian of a minor student or by a student who is 18 years of age or older, a public body may make reasonable charges ...
rules.notes: Special-record fee treatment: carves this class out of the § 2.2-3704(F) charge regime.

rules.legal_concept: Charge for GIS records to non-owner; topo map pro rata
rules.atomic_rule: A body may make a reasonable charge, not exceeding actual cost, for records produced from a geographic information system at the request of anyone other than the owner of the subject land, except that it may charge on a pro rata per-acre basis for topographical maps it developed that encompass a contiguous area greater than 50 acres.
rules.trigger: Request for GIS-produced records by a non-owner of the subject land
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost; exception — pro rata per-acre for body-developed topo maps over 50 contiguous acres
rules.source_language: The public body may also make a reasonable charge for the cost incurred in supplying records produced from a geographic information system at the request of anyone other than the owner of the land that is the subject of the request. However, such charges shall not exceed the actual cost to the public body in supplying such records, except that the public body may charge, on a pro rata per acre basis, for the cost of creating topographical maps developed by the public body, for such maps or portions thereof, which encompass a contiguous area greater than 50 acres.
rules.notes: Special-record fee treatment (GIS/topo).

rules.legal_concept: Designation of a FOIA officer as point of contact
rules.atomic_rule: All state, local, and regional public bodies subject to the chapter shall designate and publicly identify one or more FOIA officers to serve as the point of contact for records requests and to coordinate the body's FOIA compliance.
rules.trigger: Body is subject to VFOIA
rules.source_language: All state public bodies, including state authorities, that are subject to the provisions of this chapter and all local public bodies and regional public bodies that are subject to the provisions of this chapter shall designate and publicly identify one or more Freedom of Information Act officers (FOIA officer) whose responsibility is to serve as a point of contact for members of the public in requesting public records and to coordinate the public body's compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: Custodian-designation keeper-sliver: anchors intake routing to the designated FOIA officer.

rules.legal_concept: Petition for mandamus or injunction to enforce VFOIA
rules.atomic_rule: An aggrieved requester may file a petition for mandamus or injunction in the appropriate court (venue keyed to the type of public body) to enforce the chapter's records-access rights.
rules.trigger: Denial or alleged VFOIA violation
rules.source_language: Venue for a petition against a local public body lies in the court of the county or city from which the public body has been elected or appointed to serve; for a regional body, where its principal business office is located; and for a state agency or institution of higher education, in the court of the residence of the aggrieved party or of the City of Richmond.
rules.notes: Judicial enforcement path (no internal administrative appeal exists under VFOIA). Venue clause paraphrased from the summarized fetch — flag for verbatim re-pull.

rules.legal_concept: Enforcement petition heard within seven days
rules.atomic_rule: The petition for mandamus or injunction shall be heard within seven days of the date it is made, provided the defendant receives at least three working days' notice (notice waived for open-meetings violations).
rules.trigger: Enforcement petition filed
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 7 days from date petition is made; ≥3 working days' notice to defendant
rules.source_language: The petition for mandamus or injunction shall be heard within seven days of the date when the same is made

rules.legal_concept: Public body bears burden; procedural failure presumed a violation
rules.atomic_rule: In an enforcement proceeding the public body bears the burden of proving an exclusion by a preponderance of the evidence, and any failure by the body to follow the chapter's procedures is presumed to be a violation.
rules.trigger: Enforcement proceeding on the record
rules.source_language: The public body shall bear the burden of proof to establish an exclusion by a preponderance of the evidence. ... any failure by a public body to follow the procedures established by this chapter shall be presumed to be a violation.

rules.legal_concept: Enforcement proceeding given docket precedence
rules.atomic_rule: The enforcement proceeding shall be given precedence on the court's docket over all cases not otherwise given precedence by law.
rules.trigger: Enforcement petition on the docket
rules.source_language: shall be given precedence on the docket of such court over all cases that are not otherwise given precedence by law.

material_negatives.note: VFOIA has no acknowledgment step distinct from the substantive response. The five-working-day response IS the first required communication (§ 2.2-3704(B)); there is no separate 'we received your request' clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

VFOIA provides NO internal administrative appeal and no binding agency/AG review of a denial. The only formal remedy is the judicial mandamus/injunction petition (§ 2.2-3713). The Virginia FOIA Advisory Council (§ 30-179) issues only nonbinding advisory opinions. Emit no appeal.administrative.* rule for Virginia.
No statewide fixed or ceiling per-page copy rate. Fees are bounded only by the 'actual cost' ceiling (VA-0021, VA-0024); the per-page amount, if any, is set by each locality under that ceiling.

VFOIA draws no commercial-vs-noncommercial requester distinction and authorizes no commercial-purpose fee surcharge; 'commercial purpose' is not a defined term in § 2.2-3701. Charges turn on actual cost regardless of requester purpose.

Deliberately NOT emitted as a rule: Virginia does not grant universal any-person access. Standing is restricted to citizens of the Commonwealth plus in-state media (see VA-0001). Emitting the shared any_person/no_residency key here would misjoin Virginia with open-access states.
No statutory classification for multi-record, recurring, or subscription requests, and no distinct processing track for them. Each request runs the single § 2.2-3704 pipeline.

No VFOIA provision imposes a preservation/litigation hold triggered by the request or by an enforcement petition. Records retention runs under the separate Public Records Act (Title 42.1) on routine schedules, which are out of scope. No request-triggered hold rule found.

VFOIA prescribes no mandatory submission channel (no required form, portal, or writing). A request need not even cite the chapter (VA-0006); the statute is silent on medium, so no channel rule is emitted.

structural_branches.description: The § 2.2-3704(B) response is a four-way branch the engine must express within the 5-day clock: (1) provide records, (2) withhold entirely with citation, (3) provide/withhold in part with citation, (4) records not found/not practically possible. Each leg has its own required notice content (VA-0011/0012/0013) and the (4) leg opens the extension path.

§ 2.2-3704(C) court-petition-for-additional-time is a state-specific external fork (extraordinary volume / lengthy search) gated by a prior duty to attempt agreement with the requester; it produces no fixed day-count (VA-0010).
A request enters a terminal 'deemed withdrawn' state after 30 days of requester silence following a cost estimate (VA-0028) — a distinct end-state separate from denial or fulfillment.

The statutory clock pauses (tolls) in two payment-negotiation states: awaiting the requester's answer to a cost estimate (VA-0027) and awaiting the requester's answer to a >$200 advance-deposit determination (VA-0032). The request sits in a paused-for-payment state, resuming on requester response.

§ 2.2-3704.2 requires a designated, publicly-identified FOIA officer as the intake point of contact (VA-0035); routing anchors to that officer, and a not-found response must hand off to a known alternate custodian (VA-0013).

Virginia's only formal denial-review path is judicial — a mandamus/injunction petition (VA-0036) with a 7-day expedited hearing (VA-0037), burden on the public body (VA-0038), and docket precedence (VA-0039). There is no administrative-appeal stage to model.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect public records in the custody of any officer; the statute imposes no eligibility qualification (no residency, citizenship, standing, or purpose condition) on who may request.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of any person).
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key emitted as a rule per V2 symmetry mandate. 'Any person' is the affirmative basis for the no-residency rule (AZ-0003).

rules.legal_concept: Inspection available at all times during office hours
rules.atomic_rule: Custodian must make public records available for inspection at all times during regular office hours.
rules.trigger: Request to inspect during office hours.
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.notes: Split from the same sentence as AZ-0001: the availability window (office hours) is a distinct configurable concept from the eligibility fact.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship requirement
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency, citizenship, or in-state requirement to request public records; the right extends to 'any person.'
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared key (not a material negative) per V2 discovery discipline. Rests on the verbatim 'any person' language; the statute states no residency condition.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of reason/purpose required for non-commercial requests
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose for a non-commercial request; the only purpose-related duty is to affirm the record is not for a commercial purpose (or, if it is, to provide the commercial-purpose statement under § 39-121.03).
rules.trigger: Non-commercial request.
rules.source_language: At the time of the request, the requesting person shall affirm that the public record is not for a commercial purpose or, if the public record is for a commercial purpose, that the requesting person will provide a statement that explains the intended use pursuant to section 39-121.03, subsection A.
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per symmetry mandate. Arizona is distinctive: it requires a commercial/non-commercial affirmation (AZ-0010) but no statement of reason for non-commercial use. Source language is verbatim; the no-purpose conclusion is the reading of that clause.

rules.legal_concept: Manner of request: in-person examination, furnished copies, or mailed copy
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may (a) examine records in person during regular office hours, (b) be furnished copies/printouts/photographs, or (c) request that the custodian mail a copy of any public record not otherwise available on the public body's website.
rules.trigger: Request received.
rules.source_language: Any person may request to examine or be furnished copies, printouts or photographs of any public record during regular office hours or may request that the custodian mail a copy of any public record not otherwise available on the public body's website to the requesting person.
rules.notes: Mail-a-copy duty is limited to records 'not otherwise available on the public body's website.'

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment for copying and postage on mailed copies
rules.atomic_rule: For a request to mail a copy, the custodian may require the requester to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges.
rules.trigger: Requester asks that a copy be mailed.
rules.source_language: The custodian may require any person requesting that the custodian mail a copy of any public record to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges.
rules.notes: Prepayment is a permission ('may require'), applicable only to the mailed-copy channel.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to promptly furnish copies
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall promptly furnish the requested copies, printouts or photographs (subject to fee/facility conditions). 'Promptly' is an undefined standard; no fixed number of days is set by statute.
rules.trigger: Request received.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
rules.notes: Soft deadline: config_home=structural, do not invent a day-count. West Valley View Inc. v. Maricopa County Sheriff's Office (Ariz. App. 2007) interprets 'promptly' as without delay, allowing reasonable time for legitimate factors (redaction, volume) — flagged for manual verification against the official opinion. Failure to respond promptly triggers deemed denial (AZ-0013).

rules.legal_concept: Fee for copies of public records (non-commercial)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may charge a fee for copies if facilities are available; the statute sets no numeric per-page rate for ordinary (non-commercial) requests — the public body sets the amount.
rules.trigger: Copies furnished for a non-commercial request.
rules.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
rules.notes: No statutory numeric ceiling for ordinary copy fees; Arizona case law (Hanania; Judicial Watch) limits ordinary charges toward actual/reasonable cost. City supplies the operative rate under the soft standard. Distinct from the commercial-purpose fee basis (AZ-0016).

rules.legal_concept: No-charge furnishing for statutorily listed purposes
rules.atomic_rule: Records requested for the purposes listed in § 39-122 (federal benefit claims) or § 39-127 (crime-victim records) shall be furnished without charge.
rules.trigger: Request qualifies under § 39-122 or § 39-127.
rules.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
rules.notes: Cross-reference clause; the substantive waivers are AZ-0019 (§ 39-122) and AZ-0020 (§ 39-127).

rules.legal_concept: Requester affirmation of commercial vs non-commercial purpose
rules.atomic_rule: At the time of the request, the requester shall affirm the record is not for a commercial purpose, or, if it is, that they will provide the commercial-purpose statement under § 39-121.03(A).
rules.trigger: Any request, at time of submission.
rules.source_language: At the time of the request, the requesting person shall affirm that the public record is not for a commercial purpose or, if the public record is for a commercial purpose, that the requesting person will provide a statement that explains the intended use pursuant to section 39-121.03, subsection A.
rules.notes: Routing/classification input: the affirmation branches the request into the standard-fee or commercial-fee path (AZ-0015/AZ-0016), keyed to the commercial-purpose definition (AZ-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Index of withheld records and reasons (agencies)
rules.atomic_rule: If requested, the custodian of the records of an 'agency' shall furnish an index of the records or categories of records withheld and the reasons they were withheld, excluding information expressly made privileged/confidential by statute or court order.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for an index of withheld records; custodian is an 'agency.'
rules.source_language: If requested, the custodian of the records of an agency shall also furnish an index of records or categories of records that have been withheld and the reasons the records or categories of records have been withheld from the requesting person. The custodian shall not include in the index information that is expressly made privileged or confidential in statute or a court order.
rules.notes: Scope limit: 'agency' has the § 41-1001 meaning but EXCLUDES the Department of Public Safety, the DOT Motor Vehicle Division, the Department of Juvenile Corrections, and the State Department of Corrections. The statute expressly does not require (nor forbid a court ordering) an index from non-agency public bodies (e.g., cities). Material for municipal config — city custodians may not be statutorily compelled to index.

rules.legal_concept: Access to make copies when custodian lacks copying facilities
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian lacks facilities to copy a record the person has a right to inspect, the person shall be granted access to make copies, done while the record remains in the custodian's possession/custody/control and under the custodian's supervision.
rules.trigger: Custodian has no copying facilities for a record subject to a right of inspection.
rules.source_language: If the custodian of a public record does not have facilities for making copies, printouts or photographs of a public record that a person has a right to inspect, the person shall be granted access to the public record for the purpose of making copies, printouts or photographs. The copies, printouts or photographs shall be made while the public record is in the possession, custody and control of the custodian of the public record and shall be subject to the supervision of the custodian.
rules.notes: A production/inspection branch (requester-made copies under supervision).

rules.legal_concept: Deemed (constructive) denial of access
rules.atomic_rule: Access is deemed denied if the custodian fails to promptly respond to a production request, or fails to provide the requested index of withheld records/categories under § 39-121.01(D)(2).
rules.trigger: Custodian's failure to promptly respond, or failure to provide the requested withholding index.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: request moves to 'denied' state upon custodian's failure to promptly respond (or to furnish the requested index)
rules.source_language: Access to a public record is deemed denied if a custodian fails to promptly respond to a request for production of a public record or fails to provide to the requesting person an index of any record or categories of records that are withheld from production pursuant to subsection D, paragraph 2 of this section.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3 (deemed/constructive denial): the trigger is kept; the remedy amounts (attorney fees/damages) are excluded. The terminal event is tied to the soft 'promptly' standard (AZ-0007) and opens the judicial appeal (AZ-0014).

rules.legal_concept: Special action in superior court to appeal denial
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access to or the right to copy public records may appeal the denial through a special action in the superior court.
rules.trigger: Denial (actual or deemed) of access/copying.
rules.source_language: Any person who has requested to examine or copy public records pursuant to this article and who has been denied access to or the right to copy such records may appeal the denial through a special action in the superior court
rules.notes: Namespaced as appeal.judicial (court review), NOT an internal/administrative stage. Source language is the operative core; subsection A also lets a crime victim appeal a denial within the related criminal case. No statutory filing deadline stated. Arizona has no mandatory administrative/AG appeal stage (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Statement of commercial purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: When a person requests copies/printouts/photographs for a commercial purpose, they shall provide a statement setting forth the commercial purpose for which the reproductions will be used.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose.
rules.source_language: When a person requests copies, printouts or photographs of public records for a commercial purpose, the person shall provide a statement setting forth the commercial purpose for which the copies, printouts or photographs will be used.
rules.notes: Gates the commercial-fee basis (AZ-0016) and the governor-review path (AZ-0017).

rules.legal_concept: Fee basis for commercial-purpose reproductions
rules.atomic_rule: For commercial-purpose reproductions the custodian's charge may include: (1) a portion of the public body's cost of obtaining the original/copies; (2) a reasonable fee for time, materials, equipment and personnel in producing the reproduction; and (3) the value of the reproduction on the commercial market as best determined by the public body.
rules.trigger: Commercial-purpose statement provided; reproductions furnished.
rules.source_language: Upon being furnished the statement the custodian of such records may furnish reproductions, the charge for which shall include the following: 1. A portion of the cost to the public body for obtaining the original or copies of the documents, printouts or photographs. 2. A reasonable fee for the cost of time, materials, equipment and personnel in producing such reproduction. 3. The value of the reproduction on the commercial market as best determined by the public body.
rules.notes: Conjunctive fee formula kept in one row (not fragmented). Soft-standard: the state supplies the components; the public body determines the operative amounts (esp. 'reasonable fee' and 'commercial market value'). Distinct constraint_basis from AZ-0008 but the SAME fee-basis family — a commercial vs standard split of the copy-charge concept.

rules.legal_concept: Governor executive-order review of alleged commercial misuse
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian believes the stated commercial purpose is a misuse of public records, the custodian may apply to the governor for an executive order prohibiting furnishing the records; if no order issues within thirty days of the application, the custodian shall provide the reproductions upon being paid the fee.
rules.trigger: Custodian believes the commercial purpose constitutes misuse and applies to the governor.
rules.clock_spec: pauses production up to 30 calendar-days from the custodian's application to the governor; on expiry with no executive order, the custodian must provide upon payment
rules.source_language: If no order is issued within thirty days of the date of application, the custodian of public records shall provide such copies, printouts or photographs upon being paid the fee.
rules.notes: Arizona-specific structural fork (governor executive-order review). Source language is the verbatim 30-day/auto-release clause; the front half (custodian may apply to the governor for an order) is paraphrased in the atomic rule from § 39-121.03(B).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means using a public record for sale or resale, for producing a document containing the copy for sale, for obtaining names/addresses for solicitation, for selling names/addresses to another for solicitation, or for any purpose in which the purchaser can reasonably anticipate monetary gain from the record's direct or indirect use.
rules.trigger: Classifying a request as commercial vs non-commercial.
rules.source_language: For the purposes of this section, 'commercial purpose' means the use of a public record for the purpose of sale or resale or for the purpose of producing a document containing all or part of the copy, printout or photograph for sale or the obtaining of names and addresses from public records for the purpose of solicitation or the sale of names and addresses to another for the purpose of solicitation or for any purpose in which the purchaser can reasonably anticipate the receipt of monetary gain from the direct or indirect use of the public record.
rules.notes: Keeper: a definition the software branches on (drives the fee basis and the affirmation/classification path). The statute also excludes use as evidence/in anticipation of judicial/administrative proceedings from 'commercial purpose' (noted, not fully quoted here).

rules.legal_concept: Free search and certified copies for federal benefit claims
rules.atomic_rule: No state, county or city (or officer/board thereof) shall demand or receive a fee for certified copies of, or searches for, public records when they are to be used in connection with a claim for a pension, allotment, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefit to be presented to the United States or a federal bureau/department.
rules.trigger: Records are for use in a federal benefit/pension claim; requested by a U.S. official, the claimant, or the claimant's guardian or attorney.
rules.source_language: No state, county or city, or any officer or board thereof shall demand or receive a fee or compensation for issuing certified copies of public records or for making search for them, when they are to be used in connection with a claim for a pension, allotment, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefits which is to be presented to the United States or a bureau or department thereof.
rules.notes: Explicitly binds cities. Subsection C (services rendered on request of a U.S. official, claimant, guardian or attorney; official-bond liability for refusal) is the enforcement/remedy tail and is excluded.

rules.legal_concept: Free copy of police reports/recordings for crime victims
rules.atomic_rule: A crime victim (or the victim's attorney on the victim's behalf; and, for Part I crimes, immediate family if the victim is killed or incapacitated) has the right to receive one copy of the police report and audio/video recordings without charge from the investigating agency, plus specified court records.
rules.trigger: Requester is a qualifying crime victim (Part I crimes; domestic-violence or sexual offenses) or their attorney/immediate family.
rules.source_language: the victim or the victim's attorney on behalf of the victim has the right to receive one copy of the police report, audio recordings and video recordings
rules.notes: Source language is the verbatim operative phrase from subsection C; the eligibility scope (Part I crimes in (A), DV/sexual offenses in (C), immediate family, court minute entries) is summarized in the atomic rule. Definitions for victim/offense reference §§ 8-382 and related. Special-workflow record type (also see special-records table).

rules.legal_concept: Priority processing of crime-victim police report requests
rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency shall prioritize the processing and providing of each police report requested under § 39-127.
rules.trigger: Police report requested under § 39-127.
rules.source_language: A law enforcement agency shall prioritize the processing and providing of each police report that is requested pursuant to this section.
rules.notes: 'Prioritize' is a soft processing-order directive, not a numeric deadline (clock_effect=none). Affects queue ordering for the request rather than setting a date.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic records and embedded metadata are public records subject to disclosure in native format
rules.atomic_rule: When a public record is maintained in an electronic format, the electronic version — including embedded metadata — is a public record and, if requested in that form, is subject to disclosure in its native/electronic format.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a record maintained electronically in its native electronic form (including metadata).
rules.source_language: When a public entity maintains a public record in an electronic format, the electronic version of the record, including any embedded metadata, is subject to disclosure under the public records law. (paraphrase — official opinion not opened this pass)
rules.source_authority: Lake v. City of Phoenix, 222 Ariz. 547, 218 P.3d 1004 (2009)
rules.notes: Judicially established production/format rule not stated in statute. Only secondary sources (Ballotpedia, law firm summaries) were accessible this pass; the official Arizona Supreme Court opinion was not opened, so is_paraphrase=true and status flagged for manual verification. Included because it creates a distinct production-format obligation with strong cross-state relevance; verify the exact holding and any format-election limits before relying on it.

structural_branches.description: Commercial-purpose path (AZ-0015): a request classified commercial must carry a purpose statement and routes to the commercial-fee basis and the governor-review fork.

Governor executive-order review (AZ-0017): custodian may apply to the governor to block commercial-misuse requests; a 30-day timer auto-releases the records if no order issues. Arizona-bespoke review stage, not an internal appeal.

Withholding-index generation (AZ-0011): on request, an 'agency' custodian must produce an index of withheld records/categories and reasons; non-agency public bodies (cities) are outside the statutory compulsion.
Deemed-denial terminal state (AZ-0013): failure to promptly respond or to furnish the requested index moves the request into a 'denied' state, opening judicial review.
Judicial appeal path (AZ-0014): denial is contested by special action in superior court — the only statutory review stage; there is no mandatory administrative/AG stage.
Requester-copies branch (AZ-0012): when the custodian lacks copying facilities, the requester is granted supervised access to make copies while records remain in custody.
No-charge classification branches (AZ-0009/AZ-0019/AZ-0020): requests for federal benefit claims (§ 39-122) and crime-victim records (§ 39-127) are furnished free, bypassing the fee path.

material_negatives.note: Arizona sets NO fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline. The only response standard is 'promptly' (§ 39-121.01(D)(1)), captured as the soft-standard rule AZ-0007. Absence of a found numeric deadline is not proof none exists elsewhere, but none appears in the public-records article.

No statutory clarification/narrowing procedure or clock, and no statutory request-abandonment-for-nonresponse provision, was found in the public-records article. Clarification practice is unregulated by statute.

No statewide numeric per-page copy rate for ordinary (non-commercial) municipal requests. The statute permits 'a fee' (§ 39-121.01(D)(1)); the amount is set by each public body, constrained by case-law reasonableness/cost. Emitted as soft-standard parameter AZ-0008, not a negative — noted here for the missing numeric value.

No request-triggered or litigation-triggered preservation/legal-hold provision was found in the public-records article (§§ 39-121 to 39-128). General preservation duties exist (§ 39-121.01(C)) but are routine retention, excluded. Keeper-sliver #2 (a hold the request itself triggers) appears absent.

No mandatory administrative or Attorney General appeal stage before court review. The Ombudsman-Citizens' Aide (A.R.S. § 41-1376.01) provides non-binding assistance/mediation on public-records disputes but is not a required stage — deferred for a later pass; not opened this pass.

No statutory requester right to elect a specific production format. The native-format/metadata rule rests on case law (AZ-0022, Lake v. City of Phoenix), which was not verified against the official opinion this pass.

No explicit statutory segregability/redaction-and-release standard in the public-records article; redaction of exempt content is governed by case-law balancing (privacy, confidentiality, best interests of the state) — a human-legal-review balancing test unsuitable for automatic configuration, deferred.

rules.legal_concept: Availability to any person
rules.atomic_rule: Upon request for identifiable public records, the agency shall make them promptly available to any person.
rules.trigger: Any person submits a request for identifiable public records.
rules.source_language: Public records shall be available for inspection and copying, and agencies shall, upon request for identifiable public records, make them promptly available to any person including, if applicable, on a partial or installment basis as records that are part of a larger set of requested records are assembled or made ready for inspection or disclosure.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the shared eligibility key.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester shall not be required to provide the purpose of the request, except to establish whether disclosure would violate the commercial-purpose list prohibition or another statute restricting disclosure to certain persons.
rules.trigger: Any records request; purpose may be asked only to test a commercial-purpose or person-specific prohibition.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not distinguish among persons requesting records, and such persons shall not be required to provide information as to the purpose for the request except to establish whether inspection and copying would violate RCW 42.56.070(8) or 42.56.240(14), or other statute which exempts or prohibits disclosure of specific information or records to certain persons.
rules.notes: The purpose-inquiry exception is the branch that connects to the commercial-purpose list prohibition (WA-0030).

rules.legal_concept: No distinction among requesters
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not distinguish among persons requesting records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not distinguish among persons requesting records, and such persons shall not be required to provide information as to the purpose for the request except to establish whether inspection and copying would violate RCW 42.56.070(8) or 42.56.240(14), or other statute which exempts or prohibits disclosure of specific information or records to certain persons.
rules.notes: Same sentence as WA-0002; split as a distinct concept (equal treatment) from the no-purpose concept.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be made available to any person with no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: agencies shall, upon request for identifiable public records, make them promptly available to any person
rules.notes: Washington states 'any person' with no residency clause; residency-neutrality derives from that phrase and is confirmed by the AG model rules (WAC 44-14). Emitted as the shared eligibility key per universal-access symmetry rule.

rules.legal_concept: No official request format required
rules.atomic_rule: No official format is required to make a records request, though an agency may recommend a form or web page.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency provided form or web page.

rules.legal_concept: Accepted request channels
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall honor requests for identifiable public records received in person during normal office hours, or by mail or email, unless exempted by the chapter.
rules.trigger: Request received in person, by mail, or by email.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency's normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter.
rules.notes: RCW 42.56.100 separately confirms mail requests must be honored.

rules.legal_concept: Identifiable records requirement
rules.atomic_rule: A request must be for identifiable records; a request for all or substantially all of an agency's records is not valid, but a request for all records on a particular topic, keyword, or name is not treated as a request for all records.
rules.trigger: Request is evaluated for validity at intake.
rules.source_language: A public records request must be for identifiable records. A request for all or substantially all records prepared, owned, used, or retained by an agency is not a valid request for identifiable records under this chapter, provided that a request for all records regarding a particular topic or containing a particular keyword or name shall not be considered a request for all of an agency's records.
rules.notes: Gates whether a submission is a valid request the engine must process.

rules.legal_concept: Overbreadth not a sole basis for denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely because the request is overbroad.
rules.trigger: Request is identifiable but broad.
rules.source_language: Agencies shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely on the basis that the request is overbroad.

rules.legal_concept: Bot request denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny a bot request that is one of multiple requests from the same requester within a 24-hour period if it establishes that responding would cause excessive interference with other essential functions.
rules.trigger: Multiple computer-generated (bot) requests from one requester within a 24-hour period that would cause excessive interference.
rules.source_language: An agency may deny a bot request that is one of multiple requests from the requestor to the agency within a twenty-four hour period, if the agency establishes that responding to the multiple requests would cause excessive interference with other essential functions of the agency. For purposes of this subsection, "bot request" means a request for public records that an agency reasonably believes was automatically generated by a computer program or script.
rules.notes: The 24-hour aggregation window is fixed by statute; it is a condition, not a response deadline (clock effect none).

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response
rules.atomic_rule: Within five business days of receiving a request, the agency must respond in one of the five statutory ways.
rules.trigger: Agency receives a public record request.
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: Within five business days of receiving a public record request, an agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives must respond in one of the ways provided in this subsection (1):
rules.notes: Fixed statutory maximum for the initial response, not final production. City cannot extend it; the response itself may be an estimate (WA-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Five permitted response forms
rules.atomic_rule: The initial response must take one of five forms: provide the record; provide a website link to it; acknowledge and give a reasonable time estimate; acknowledge and request clarification with an estimate; or deny.
rules.trigger: Agency issues its initial response within five business days.
rules.source_language: (a) Providing the record; (b) Providing an internet address and link on the agency's website to the specific records requested, except that if the requester notifies the agency that he or she cannot access the records through the internet, then the agency must provide copies of the record or allow the requester to view copies using an agency computer; (c) Acknowledging that the agency ... has received the request and providing a reasonable estimate of the time the agency ... will require to respond to the request; (d) Acknowledging that the agency ... has received the request and asking the requestor to provide clarification for a request that is unclear, and providing, to the greatest extent possible, a reasonable estimate of the time ... to respond to the request if it is not clarified; or (e) Denying the public record request.
rules.notes: The five-way response fork the engine must be able to execute.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable estimate of response time
rules.atomic_rule: When acknowledging a request rather than fulfilling it, the agency must provide a reasonable estimate of the time it will require to respond.
rules.trigger: Agency acknowledges receipt instead of producing or denying within five business days.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable estimate of the time ... to respond" from acknowledgment
rules.source_language: Acknowledging that the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives has received the request and providing a reasonable estimate of the time the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives will require to respond to the request;
rules.notes: Soft standard: 'reasonable estimate' is not a fixed number; config home structural per soft-deadline rule.

rules.legal_concept: Promptness / most timely action
rules.atomic_rule: Responses to public records requests shall be made promptly.
rules.trigger: Request received.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Responses to requests for public records shall be made promptly by agencies, the office of the secretary of the senate, and the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives.
rules.notes: Reinforced by RCW 42.56.080(2) ('promptly available') and RCW 42.56.100 ('most timely possible action', WA-0041). Soft standard; do not convert to a day count.

rules.legal_concept: Grounds for additional response time
rules.atomic_rule: Additional time to respond may be based on the need to clarify the request, to locate and assemble records, to notify affected third persons or agencies, or to determine whether information is exempt.
rules.trigger: Agency needs more time and cites one of the enumerated grounds.
rules.source_language: Additional time required to respond to a request may be based upon the need to clarify the intent of the request, to locate and assemble the information requested, to notify third persons or agencies affected by the request, or to determine whether any of the information requested is exempt and that a denial should be made as to all or part of the request.
rules.notes: Defines the permissible bases for the reasonable estimate (WA-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Request for clarification
rules.atomic_rule: When acknowledging an unclear request, the agency may ask the requester to clarify what information is sought.
rules.trigger: Request is unclear.
rules.source_language: In acknowledging receipt of a public record request that is unclear, an agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives may ask the requestor to clarify what information the requestor is seeking.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to clarify ends duty
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to respond to a clarification request and the entire request is unclear, the agency need not respond to it.
rules.trigger: Requester does not respond to a clarification request and the entire request is unclear.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: agency need not respond; no statutory waiting period specified
rules.source_language: If the requestor fails to respond to an agency request to clarify the request, and the entire request is unclear, the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives need not respond to it. Otherwise, the agency must respond, pursuant to this section, to those portions of the request that are clear.
rules.notes: Constructive-abandonment terminal event; statute states no numeric deadline for the requester to reply.

rules.legal_concept: Partial response to clear portions
rules.atomic_rule: Where only part of a request is unclear, the agency must respond to the portions that are clear.
rules.trigger: Request is partly clear and partly unclear.
rules.source_language: Otherwise, the agency must respond, pursuant to this section, to those portions of the request that are clear.
rules.notes: Same sentence as WA-0016; split to isolate the affirmative partial-response duty from the abandonment trigger.

rules.legal_concept: Partial / installment production
rules.atomic_rule: Records may be provided on a partial or installment basis as records in a larger set are assembled or made ready.
rules.trigger: Requested records are part of a larger set assembled over time.
rules.source_language: agencies shall, upon request for identifiable public records, make them promptly available to any person including, if applicable, on a partial or installment basis as records that are part of a larger set of requested records are assembled or made ready for inspection or disclosure.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for inspecting public records or for locating documents and making them available for copying.
rules.trigger: Requester inspects records or agency locates records for copying.
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged for the inspection of public records or locating public documents and making them available for copying, except as provided in RCW 42.56.240(14) and subsection (3) of this section.
rules.notes: Fixed at zero; exceptions are the customized-service charge (WA-0029) and RCW 42.56.240(14).

rules.legal_concept: Copy charge limited to actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A reasonable charge may be imposed for copies and for use of agency copying equipment, not exceeding the amount necessary to reimburse the agency for its actual costs directly incident to copying.
rules.trigger: Agency provides copies of records.
rules.source_language: A reasonable charge may be imposed for providing copies of public records and for the use by any person of agency equipment or equipment of the office of the secretary of the senate or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives to copy public records, which charges shall not exceed the amount necessary to reimburse the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives for its actual costs directly incident to such copying.
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; city fills the operative rate under it. Also requires use of the most reasonable, cost-efficient method available.

rules.legal_concept: Default photocopy rate
rules.atomic_rule: Absent a published actual-cost calculation, the agency may charge up to fifteen cents per page for photocopies or printed copies of electronic records.
rules.trigger: Agency has not determined its actual per-copy costs under RCW 42.56.070(7).
rules.source_language: Fifteen cents per page for photocopies
rules.notes: Retrieval tool returned the amount verbatim in quotation marks but condensed the surrounding paragraph. Default schedule applies only if actual costs not determined; verify full clause text at RCW 42.56.120(2)(b)(i).

rules.legal_concept: Default scan rate
rules.atomic_rule: Absent a published actual-cost calculation, the agency may charge up to ten cents per page for public records scanned into an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Agency has not determined actual per-copy costs.
rules.source_language: Ten cents per page for public records scanned
rules.notes: Amount verbatim; surrounding clause condensed by retrieval tool.

rules.legal_concept: Default electronic-file rate
rules.atomic_rule: Absent a published actual-cost calculation, the agency may charge up to five cents per each four electronic files or attachments uploaded for electronic delivery.
rules.trigger: Agency has not determined actual per-copy costs.
rules.source_language: Five cents per each four electronic files
rules.notes: Amount verbatim; surrounding clause condensed by retrieval tool.

rules.legal_concept: Default electronic-transmission rate
rules.atomic_rule: Absent a published actual-cost calculation, the agency may charge up to ten cents per gigabyte for transmission of records in an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Agency has not determined actual per-copy costs.
rules.source_language: Ten cents per gigabyte for the transmission
rules.notes: Amount verbatim; surrounding clause condensed by retrieval tool. Storage media, containers, and postage chargeable at actual cost separately.

rules.legal_concept: Two-dollar flat fee
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a flat fee of up to two dollars for a request as payment for the costs of providing the copies, in lieu of itemized charges.
rules.trigger: Agency elects a flat fee instead of calculating itemized copy costs.
rules.source_language: An agency may charge a flat fee of up to two dollars for any request
rules.notes: Ceiling of $2 per request; no additional flat fee may be charged on subsequent installments of the same request. Clause condensed by retrieval tool.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for website-posted records
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not impose copying charges for access to or downloading of records it routinely posts on its public internet website.
rules.trigger: Requested records are routinely posted on the agency's public website.
rules.source_language: An agency shall not impose copying charges under this section for access to or downloading of records that the agency routinely posts on its public internet website.
rules.notes: Fixed at zero for routinely-posted records unless the requester specifically requests a copy in a different form.

rules.legal_concept: Published actual-cost statement
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge actual copying costs only in accordance with costs it has established and published; it may establish and make available a statement of the actual costs it charges for copies.
rules.trigger: Agency wishes to charge actual (rather than default-schedule) costs.
rules.source_language: Each agency may establish, maintain, and make available for public inspection and copying a statement of the actual costs that it charges for providing photocopies or electronically produced copies, of public records.
rules.notes: Precondition (structural step) to charging actual costs instead of the default statutory schedule.

rules.legal_concept: Costs excluded from copy fee
rules.atomic_rule: In determining actual copy costs, an agency may not include staff salaries, benefits, or general administrative or overhead charges unless directly related to the actual cost of copying.
rules.trigger: Agency calculates its actual copy costs.
rules.source_language: In determining the actual costs for providing copies of public records, an agency may not include staff salaries, benefits, or other general administrative or overhead charges, unless those costs are directly related to the actual cost of copying the public records.
rules.notes: Bounds the actual-cost calculation; a calculation-method constraint rather than a fillable value.

rules.legal_concept: Customized service charge
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose a customized service charge for a request that requires information-technology expertise to prepare data compilations or provide customized electronic access not used by the agency for other purposes, only after notifying the requester of the charge and the reason it applies.
rules.trigger: Request requires IT expertise for a data compilation or customized electronic access the agency does not use for other purposes.
rules.source_language: Agencies may charge for customized services (data compilations, custom electronic access) only when services aren't used internally, after notifying requestors of costs and reasons.
rules.notes: Retrieval tool returned only a summary of 120(3); verbatim operative clause needs confirmation at RCW 42.56.120(3), which also conditions the charge on advance notice, an explanation, and a cost estimate.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial-purpose list prohibition
rules.atomic_rule: The chapter does not authorize giving, selling, or providing access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes, and agencies shall not do so unless specifically authorized or directed by law.
rules.trigger: Request seeks a list of individuals and the purpose appears commercial.
rules.source_language: This chapter shall not be construed as giving authority to any agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives to give, sell or provide access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes, and agencies, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives shall not do so unless specifically authorized or directed by law.
rules.notes: 'Commercial purposes' is the definition the software branches on; it is also the sole basis on which purpose may be inquired (WA-0002).

rules.legal_concept: Deposit up to ten percent
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may require a deposit not exceeding ten percent of the estimated cost of providing copies for a request.
rules.trigger: Agency estimates the cost of providing copies.
rules.source_language: An agency may require a deposit in an amount not to exceed ten percent of the estimated cost of providing copies for a request.
rules.notes: Ceiling of 10%; city sets the operative deposit under it.

rules.legal_concept: Unclaimed installment ends duty
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to inspect, pay for, or claim an installment of a records request, the agency need not fulfill the balance of the request.
rules.trigger: An installment is not claimed, reviewed, or paid for.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: balance of request not fulfilled when an installment is unclaimed
rules.source_language: Agencies may charge for partial fulfillment installments and needn't complete requests if portions go unclaimed.
rules.notes: Retrieval tool summarized this portion of 120(4); confirm verbatim operative clause at RCW 42.56.120(4).
