rules.legal_concept: Segregability / deletion of exempt information
rules.atomic_rule: The chapter's exemptions are inapplicable to the extent that information whose disclosure would violate personal privacy or vital governmental interests can be deleted from the specific records sought; the non-exempt remainder must be disclosed.
rules.trigger: A record contains both exempt and non-exempt information.
rules.source_language: Except for information described in RCW 42.56.230(3)(a) and confidential income data exempted from public inspection pursuant to RCW 84.40.020, the exemptions of this chapter are inapplicable to the extent that information, the disclosure of which would violate personal privacy or vital governmental interests, can be deleted from the specific records sought. No exemption may be construed to permit the nondisclosure of statistical information not descriptive of any readily identifiable person or persons.
rules.notes: The redact-and-release duty; two enumerated exceptions carve out specific record types.

rules.legal_concept: Exemption citation and brief explanation
rules.atomic_rule: A response refusing inspection in whole or in part must include a statement of the specific exemption authorizing the withholding and a brief explanation of how the exemption applies to the record withheld.
rules.trigger: Agency withholds or redacts a record in whole or in part.
rules.source_language: Agency responses refusing, in whole or in part, inspection of any public record shall include a statement of the specific exemption authorizing the withholding of the record (or part) and a brief explanation of how the exemption applies to the record withheld.
rules.notes: Withholding-index / exemption-log requirement attached to any partial or full denial.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of reasons
rules.atomic_rule: Denials of requests must be accompanied by a written statement of the specific reasons for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies a request in whole or in part.
rules.source_language: Denials of requests must be accompanied by a written statement of the specific reasons therefor.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt internal review of denial
rules.atomic_rule: An agency must establish a mechanism for the most prompt possible review of a denial of inspection; the review is deemed completed at the end of the second business day following the denial and constitutes final agency action for purposes of judicial review.
rules.trigger: Agency denies inspection.
rules.clock_spec: internal review deemed complete at end of 2nd business day following denial
rules.source_language: Agencies, the office of the secretary of the senate, and the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives shall establish mechanisms for the most prompt possible review of decisions denying inspection, and such review shall be deemed completed at the end of the second business day following the denial of inspection and shall constitute final agency action or final action by the office of the secretary of the senate or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives for the purposes of judicial review.
rules.notes: Administrative-appeal stage with an automatic 2-business-day deeming that ripens the matter for judicial review.

rules.legal_concept: Superior court show-cause review
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied the opportunity to inspect or copy a record may move the superior court to require the agency to show cause why it refused; the agency bears the burden of proving the refusal is authorized by an exempting or prohibiting statute.
rules.trigger: A person is denied inspection or copying.
rules.source_language: the superior court ... may require the responsible agency to show cause why it has refused to allow inspection or copying of a specific public record or class of records. The burden of proof shall be on the agency to establish that refusal to permit public inspection and copying is in accordance with a statute that exempts or prohibits disclosure in whole or in part of specific information or records.
rules.notes: Judicial-review path (namespaced appeal.judicial). Retrieval tool condensed the opening clause; verbatim burden sentence captured.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial review of estimate or charge
rules.atomic_rule: A person may petition the superior court to challenge an agency's reasonable estimate of the time to respond or its copying charges; the agency must show the estimate or charge is reasonable.
rules.trigger: Requester disputes the agency's time estimate or copying charge.
rules.source_language: A person challenging an agency's time estimate or copying charges may petition superior court. The agency must demonstrate its estimate is reasonable.
rules.notes: Retrieval tool summarized 550(2); confirm verbatim operative clause. Distinct judicial path for estimate/charge disputes.

rules.legal_concept: One-year statute of limitations
rules.atomic_rule: An action under the judicial-review section must be filed within one year of the agency's claim of exemption or the last production of a record on a partial or installment basis.
rules.trigger: Agency claims an exemption or makes the last installment production.
rules.clock_spec: 1 year from the agency's claim of exemption or the last production on a partial/installment basis
rules.source_language: Actions under this section must be filed within one year of the agency's claim of exemption or the last production of a record on a partial or installment basis.
rules.notes: Fixed limitations period; the two alternative start events matter for close-out and records-retention on a request.

rules.legal_concept: Public records officer designation
rules.atomic_rule: Each state and local agency shall appoint and publicly identify a public records officer to serve as the point of contact for records requests and to oversee the agency's compliance with the chapter.
rules.trigger: Agency-level obligation; the officer is the routing target for incoming requests.
rules.source_language: Each state and local agency shall appoint and publicly identify a public records officer whose responsibility is to serve as a point of contact for members of the public in requesting disclosure of public records and to oversee the agency's compliance with the public records disclosure requirements of this chapter.
rules.notes: Custodian-designation keeper-sliver: drives routing/point-of-contact even though it sits in the officer-definition area.

rules.legal_concept: Fullest assistance / most timely action
rules.atomic_rule: Agency rules must provide for the fullest assistance to inquirers and the most timely possible action on requests for information.
rules.trigger: Any request for information.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "most timely possible action" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Such rules and regulations shall provide for the fullest assistance to inquirers and the most timely possible action on requests for information.
rules.notes: Soft timing standard reinforcing WA-0013 promptness; do not convert to a numeric deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Retention of record pending request
rules.atomic_rule: If a requested record exists but is scheduled for destruction, the agency must retain it and may not destroy or erase it until the request is resolved.
rules.trigger: A request is made while the responsive record is scheduled for destruction in the near future.
rules.clock_spec: destruction schedule held until the request is resolved
rules.source_language: If a public record request is made at a time when such record exists but is scheduled for destruction in the near future, the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives shall retain possession of the record, and may not destroy or erase the record until the request is resolved.
rules.notes: Preservation-hold keeper-sliver: a state the request enters that pauses the routine destruction schedule. Authority scope: Retention/Preservation.

rules.legal_concept: Notice to affected third parties
rules.atomic_rule: An agency has discretion to notify persons named in, or to whom a requested record specifically pertains, that release of the record has been requested, except where notice is required by law.
rules.trigger: A requested record names or specifically pertains to a third party.
rules.source_language: Agencies have discretion to notify persons named in or specifically pertained to by records when release is requested, except where law requires such notice.
rules.notes: Retrieval tool summarized 540; confirm verbatim notice clause. Third-party notice is the trigger for the injunction path (WA-0044).

rules.legal_concept: Injunction against disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: An agency, its representative, or a person named in or to whom a record specifically pertains may move the superior court by affidavit to enjoin inspection of a specific record, which the court may grant on finding that disclosure would clearly not be in the public interest and would substantially and irreparably damage any person or vital governmental functions.
rules.trigger: A named third party or the agency seeks to restrain disclosure before production.
rules.clock_spec: production held pending the court's ruling on the injunction motion
rules.source_language: would clearly not be in the public interest and would substantially and irreparably damage any person, or would substantially and irreparably damage vital governmental functions.
rules.notes: Judicial branch (namespaced appeal.judicial) that pauses production; the standard clause is verbatim, the standing/affidavit clause was condensed by the retrieval tool. Keep the conjunctive test intact (not-in-public-interest AND substantial irreparable damage).

material_negatives.note: Washington sets no fixed statutory deadline for FINAL production of records. The only hard deadline is the five-business-day initial response (WA-0010); the time to actually produce is governed by the agency's 'reasonable estimate' (WA-0012) and the soft 'promptly'/'most timely possible action' standards (WA-0013, WA-0041). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statutory numeric period within which a requester must answer a clarification request. RCW 42.56.520(3)(b) states only that if the requester fails to respond and the request is wholly unclear the agency need not respond (WA-0016) — no day-count is fixed.

No statutory deadline for a requester to REQUEST internal review of a denial. The internal-review mechanism (WA-0036) is agency-established and self-completes at the end of the second business day after denial; the statute imposes no filing window on the requester.

No statute requires municipalities to maintain a request tracking log or assign a tracking number. The AG model rules (WAC 44-14) recommend logging as a best practice, but that is advisory guidance, not a statutory requirement.

No provision authorizes charging for staff search/location time; RCW 42.56.120(1) bars any fee for locating records and RCW 42.56.070(7)(b) excludes staff salaries/overhead from copy costs. Recorded as the absence of a search-fee rule, consistent with WA-0019/WA-0028.

Washington has no acknowledgment step separate from the five-business-day response; acknowledgment is itself one of the five permitted first responses (RCW 42.56.520(1)(c)-(d)), so there is no distinct acknowledgment deadline to configure.

structural_branches.description: The five-way initial-response fork (provide / link / acknowledge+estimate / acknowledge+clarify / deny) the engine must be able to execute within five business days. RCW 42.56.520(1).

A terminal branch where a wholly-unclear request with no requester clarification lets the agency close it without responding, while partly-clear requests still require partial response. RCW 42.56.520(3)(b).
Washington-specific internal-review stage that auto-completes at the end of the second business day after a denial and ripens the matter for judicial review. RCW 42.56.520(4).
Superior-court show-cause path with the burden on the agency; distinct from any internal appeal. RCW 42.56.550(1).
Separate judicial path to challenge the reasonableness of a time estimate or copying charge. RCW 42.56.550(2).
Pre-production injunction branch: a named third party or the agency moves the superior court to restrain disclosure, pausing production pending the ruling. RCW 42.56.540.
Discretionary notice-to-affected-third-party step that feeds the injunction branch. RCW 42.56.540.
A preservation-hold state a request enters when responsive records are scheduled for destruction, pausing the destruction schedule until the request is resolved. RCW 42.56.100.
A conditional fee branch requiring an advance notice/explanation/estimate before an IT-intensive customized service charge may be imposed. RCW 42.56.120(3).
Mandatory routing target: each agency's publicly identified public records officer is the point of contact and compliance overseer. RCW 42.56.580(1).

rules.atomic_rule: Any person may request public records; upon such a request all responsive public records shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: A request for public records is made by any person.
rules.legal_concept: Public right of access — any person may inspect public records
rules.source_language: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per symmetry rule. 'Any person' establishes standing without qualification.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may not condition availability of records on the requester disclosing the intended use of the record; requiring intended-use disclosure constitutes a denial.
rules.trigger: Office would condition access on disclosure of intended use.
rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.source_language: Unless specifically required or authorized by state or federal law or in accordance with division (B) of this section, no public office or person responsible for public records may limit or condition the availability of public records by requiring disclosure of the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record. Any requirement that the requester disclose the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.notes: Same operative clause also supports OH-0003; split into two atomic rows for identity vs. purpose.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may not condition availability of records on the requester disclosing the requester's identity; requiring identity disclosure constitutes a denial.
rules.trigger: Office would condition access on disclosure of requester identity.
rules.legal_concept: No identification required to request
rules.source_language: Unless specifically required or authorized by state or federal law or in accordance with division (B) of this section, no public office or person responsible for public records may limit or condition the availability of public records by requiring disclosure of the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record. Any requirement that the requester disclose the requester's identity or the intended use of the requested public record constitutes a denial of the request.

rules.atomic_rule: Access is available to any person with no residency limitation; the statute extends the right to 'any person' without an Ohio-residency qualifier.
rules.trigger: A non-resident requests public records.
rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.source_language: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.notes: No-residency concept is derived from the unqualified 'any person' language (the verbatim clause quoted); the statute states no residency element. Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry rule rather than as a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: A written request is not mandatory; a requester may make an oral request and the office must honor it.
rules.trigger: A requester submits an oral (non-written) request.
rules.legal_concept: Written request not required
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may ask a requester to make the request in writing, may ask for the requester's identity, and may inquire about the intended use of the information requested, but may do so only after disclosing to the requester that a written request is not mandatory, that the requester may decline to reveal the requester's identity or the intended use, and when a written request or disclosure of the identity or intended use would benefit the requester by enhancing the ability of the public office or person responsible for public records to identify, locate, or deliver the public records sought by the requester.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may ask for a written request, identity, or intended use only after first disclosing to the requester that these are not mandatory and may be declined.
rules.trigger: Office wishes to ask the requester for writing, identity, or intended use.
rules.legal_concept: Precondition disclosure before inquiring into identity/use
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may ask a requester to make the request in writing, may ask for the requester's identity, and may inquire about the intended use of the information requested, but may do so only after disclosing to the requester that a written request is not mandatory, that the requester may decline to reveal the requester's identity or the intended use, and when a written request or disclosure of the identity or intended use would benefit the requester by enhancing the ability of the public office or person responsible for public records to identify, locate, or deliver the public records sought by the requester.
rules.notes: A required-notice step (structural), not a value. Engine must present the disclosure before any identity/purpose/writing inquiry.

rules.atomic_rule: Responsive public records shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: A request for inspection of public records is received.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.legal_concept: Prompt preparation and availability for inspection
rules.source_language: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
rules.notes: Undefined standard 'promptly' — do not convert to a fixed day count. Config Home structural because the engine applies a standard, not a city-filled value. Ohio has no fixed acknowledgment/response day count.

rules.atomic_rule: Copies of requested public records shall be made available at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for copies of public records.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable period of time" from request receipt
rules.legal_concept: Copies within a reasonable period of time
rules.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.notes: Two distinct soft standards in (B)(1): 'promptly' for inspection (OH-0007) and 'reasonable period of time' for copies (this rule). Kept as separate atomic deadlines.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office must organize and maintain its public records so that they can be made available for inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: None stated (ongoing obligation that conditions retrievability of records for any request).
rules.legal_concept: Duty to organize and maintain records for access
rules.source_language: To facilitate broader access to public records, a public office or the person responsible for public records shall organize and maintain public records in a manner that they can be made available for inspection or copying in accordance with division (B) of this section.
rules.notes: Kept (not routine retention governance) because it directly conditions per-request retrievability and is the basis the office uses when informing a requester how records are maintained (OH-0012).

rules.atomic_rule: A public office shall have available a copy of its current records retention schedule at a location readily available to the public.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing availability obligation).
rules.legal_concept: Records retention schedule kept publicly available
rules.source_language: A public office also shall have available a copy of its current records retention schedule at a location readily available to the public.
rules.notes: Kept because the schedule is the reference the office uses to inform a requester how records are maintained when giving the opportunity to revise (OH-0012). Routine retention/destruction scheduling itself is excluded.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may deny a request that is ambiguous or overly broad, or that does not reasonably identify what public records are being requested.
rules.trigger: A request is ambiguous, overly broad, or does not reasonably identify the records sought.
rules.legal_concept: Denial of ambiguous or overly broad requests
rules.source_language: If a requester makes an ambiguous or overly broad request or has difficulty in making a request for copies or inspection of public records under this section such that the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record cannot reasonably identify what public records are being requested, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record may deny the request.
rules.notes: The permission to deny is conditioned on the mandatory revise-opportunity in OH-0012; split into two atomic rows.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request is denied as ambiguous or overly broad, the office shall provide the requester an opportunity to revise the request by informing the requester of the manner in which records are maintained and accessed in the ordinary course of duties.
rules.trigger: The office denies a request as ambiguous or overly broad.
rules.legal_concept: Opportunity to revise an ambiguous/overly broad request
rules.source_language: If the request is denied because it is ambiguous or overly broad, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record shall provide the requester with an opportunity to revise the request by informing the requester of the manner in which records are maintained by the public office and accessed in the ordinary course of the public office's or person's duties.
rules.notes: No statutory clock attached to the revise opportunity — clock effect none.

rules.atomic_rule: The duty to prepare, make available, and copy public records falls on the public office or the 'person responsible for public records' who holds custody.
rules.trigger: A request reaches an office or the person responsible for the requested record.
rules.legal_concept: Person responsible for public records (custodian responsibility)
rules.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing — the request must reach the office or person responsible for public records. Ohio states no explicit wrong-department forwarding duty in statute; that gap is a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: If a request is ultimately denied in part or whole, the office shall provide the requester an explanation, including legal authority, setting forth why the request was denied.
rules.trigger: A request is ultimately denied in part or in whole.
rules.legal_concept: Denial explanation with legal authority
rules.source_language: If a request is ultimately denied, in part or in whole, the public office or the person responsible for the requested public record shall provide the requester with an explanation, including legal authority, setting forth why the request was denied.

rules.atomic_rule: If the initial request was provided in writing, the denial explanation shall also be provided to the requester in writing.
rules.trigger: A written request is denied in part or in whole.
rules.legal_concept: Written denial explanation for written requests
rules.source_language: If the initial request was provided in writing, the explanation also shall be provided to the requester in writing.
rules.notes: (B)(3) attaches no numeric deadline to the written explanation — clock effect none. The lack of a stated day count is a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: If a public record contains information exempt from disclosure, the office shall make available all of the information within the record that is not exempt.
rules.trigger: A responsive record contains a mix of exempt and non-exempt information.
rules.legal_concept: Segregation of exempt from non-exempt information
rules.source_language: If a public record contains information that is exempt from the duty to permit public inspection or to copy the public record, the public office or the person responsible for the public record shall make available all of the information within the public record that is not exempt.
rules.notes: Some codifications place this text at (B)(9); verify exact subsection label. Content confirmed verbatim from opened source.

rules.atomic_rule: When making a record available, the office shall notify the requester of any redaction or make the redaction plainly visible.
rules.trigger: The office redacts exempt information before producing a record.
rules.legal_concept: Notice of redaction
rules.source_language: When making that public record available for public inspection or copying that public record, the public office or the person responsible for the public record shall notify the requester of any redaction or make the redaction plainly visible.

rules.atomic_rule: Copies of public records shall be made available 'at cost' — the office may not charge more than its actual cost of making the copy.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for copies of a public record.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of the copy (no statutory per-page rate)
rules.legal_concept: Copies at cost
rules.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
rules.notes: Ohio sets no statutory per-page rate; 'at cost' is a ceiling of actual cost the city fills in. City must set the operative value under this ceiling.

rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office may charge the actual cost of preparing a video record, not to exceed $75 per hour of video produced and not to exceed $750 total.
rules.trigger: A request is for a video record held by a law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney's office.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $75.00 per hour of video produced; ceiling: $750.00 total
rules.legal_concept: Video record preparation charge
rules.source_language: a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester the actual cost associated with preparing a video record for inspection or production, not to exceed seventy-five dollars per hour of video produced, nor seven hundred fifty dollars total.
rules.notes: Two bounds in one conjunctive rule (per-hour ceiling AND total cap). Kept in one row per grain rule. Record-specific to video from law-enforcement/prosecutor offices.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may require the requester to pay in advance the cost of providing a copy, in accordance with the format the requester chose.
rules.trigger: A requester asks for a copy of a public record.
rules.legal_concept: Advance payment for copies
rules.source_language: If any person requests a copy of a public record in accordance with division (B) of this section, the public office or person responsible for the public record may require the requester to pay in advance the cost involved in providing the copy of the public record in accordance with the choice made by the requester under this division.
rules.notes: A payment gate/branch (require prepayment before producing), so structural. No statutory deposit percentage is set — that is a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: The office shall permit the requester to choose to have the record duplicated on paper, on the same medium the office keeps it, or on any other medium the office determines it can reasonably be duplicated on, and shall provide the copy in accordance with that choice.
rules.trigger: A requester requests a copy and selects a delivery/duplication medium.
rules.legal_concept: Requester's choice of copy format/medium
rules.source_language: The public office or the person responsible for the public record shall permit the requester to choose to have the public record duplicated upon paper, upon the same medium upon which the public office or person responsible for the public record keeps it, or upon any other medium upon which the public office or person responsible for the public record determines that it reasonably can be duplicated as an integral part of the normal operations of the public office or person responsible for the public record. When the requester makes a choice under this division, the public office or person responsible for the public record shall provide a copy of it in accordance with the choice made by the requester.

rules.atomic_rule: Nothing requires a public office to allow a requester to make the copies of a public record themselves.
rules.trigger: A requester proposes to make copies of the record personally.
rules.legal_concept: No duty to allow requester self-copying
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section requires a public office or person responsible for the public record to allow the requester of a copy of the public record to make the copies of the public record.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may transmit copies of public records to a requester by United States mail or by any other means of delivery or transmission the requester chooses, if the requester pays the postage/delivery cost in advance.
rules.trigger: A requester asks to have copies delivered rather than picked up.
rules.legal_concept: Transmission of copies by mail or other means
rules.source_language: A public office or person responsible for public records may transmit by United States mail or by any other means of delivery or transmission a copy of a public record requested under this division, upon the requester's payment in advance of the cost of postage or other delivery, and of the copying cost.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the opening permission of (B)(7) was rendered from the source rather than captured as a clean verbatim string this pass; the mail-volume-limit clause (OH-0024) was captured verbatim. Recommend verbatim verification of the (B)(7) opening sentence.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office may limit the number of records it will physically deliver by U.S. mail or another delivery service to ten per month, unless the requester certifies in writing non-commercial use.
rules.trigger: A requester seeks physical mail/delivery of more than ten records in a month without a non-commercial certification.
rules.clock_spec: floor: office may not cap physical-mail delivery below 10 records per month
rules.legal_concept: Ten-per-month mail delivery limit
rules.source_language: A public office may limit the number of records requested by a person that the office will physically deliver by United States mail or by another delivery service to ten per month, unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: constraint_basis floor: the statute permits a limit of ten/month, meaning the city may restrict but must allow at least ten. The commercial-use exception is split into OH-0025.

rules.atomic_rule: The ten-per-month delivery limit does not apply if the requester certifies in writing that they do not intend to use or forward the records, or the information in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.trigger: The requester provides a written non-commercial-use certification.
rules.legal_concept: Non-commercial-use certification (commercial purpose branch)
rules.source_language: unless the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: Keeper: a definition/branch the software acts on (commercial purpose) — it lifts the delivery cap. Kept per keeper-sliver guidance on branchable definitions.

rules.atomic_rule: A public office that makes records available online may limit the number of records it will transmit electronically (or otherwise) to a person to ten per month, unless the records are not available online or the requester certifies non-commercial use.
rules.trigger: A requester seeks electronic transmission of more than ten records in a month for records available online, without a non-commercial certification.
rules.clock_spec: floor: office may not cap electronic delivery below 10 records per month
rules.legal_concept: Ten-per-month electronic delivery limit
rules.source_language: A public office that makes available online at least ninety-five per cent of its public records may limit the number of records that the office will transmit to ten per month, unless the requested records are not available online or the person certifies to the office in writing that the person does not intend to use or forward the requested records, or the information contained in them, for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the online-availability threshold (reported by the fetch as web-accessible records) and exact subsection wording were rendered rather than confirmed verbatim; the 'ninety-five per cent' figure requires verbatim verification. Structure (ten/month with online-availability and non-commercial exceptions) is confirmed.

rules.atomic_rule: After a complaint alleging a failure to promptly prepare or make available records is served on the public office, the office has three business days to cure or otherwise address the failure before the requester may proceed.
rules.trigger: A requester serves a complaint alleging denial/failure on the public office.
rules.clock_spec: 3 business-days from service of the complaint on the public office
rules.legal_concept: Three-business-day pre-suit cure period
rules.source_language: the public office ... has three business days to cure or otherwise address the failure alleged in the complaint
rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification (verbatim wording of (C)(1) not cleanly captured)
rules.notes: Keeper (enforcement trigger with a clock): the 3-business-day cure window gates when a requester may file mandamus or a Court of Claims complaint. Damages/attorney-fee remedies in (C)(2) are excluded. Verbatim (C)(1) text should be confirmed.

rules.atomic_rule: A requester allegedly aggrieved by a public-records denial may file a complaint with the clerk of the court of claims; the court of claims is the sole and exclusive authority for adjudicating such complaints under this expedited alternative to mandamus.
rules.trigger: A requester elects the expedited alternative (rather than mandamus) after an alleged denial.
rules.legal_concept: Court of Claims public-records complaint (expedited alternative)
rules.source_language: the court of claims shall be the sole and exclusive authority in this state that adjudicates or resolves complaints based on alleged violations of that section
rules.notes: Namespaced appeal.administrative to distinguish from the judicial mandamus path (OH-0034). Technically adjudicated by the Court of Claims but functions as the low-cost, mediation-based review alternative rather than an ordinary court action.

rules.atomic_rule: A person filing a public-records complaint with the clerk of the court of claims shall pay a filing fee of twenty-five dollars.
rules.trigger: A requester files a Court of Claims public-records complaint.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: $25.00 filing fee
rules.legal_concept: Court of Claims complaint filing fee
rules.source_language: shall pay a filing fee of twenty-five dollars made payable to the clerk of the court
rules.notes: Fixed statutory amount (not a ceiling). Confirm exact subdivision letter (D)(1) vs (D)(2).

rules.atomic_rule: Upon assignment of a public-records complaint, the special master immediately refers the case to mediation.
rules.trigger: A Court of Claims public-records complaint is filed and assigned to a special master.
rules.legal_concept: Mandatory mediation referral
rules.source_language: immediately shall refer the case to mediation services
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: short quoted fragment from the fetch; confirm the full verbatim clause and exact subdivision. Distinct required stage in the Ohio review path.

rules.atomic_rule: Within ten business days after the termination of mediation (or notice that the case was not referred to mediation), the public office must file a response to the complaint.
rules.trigger: Mediation terminates unsuccessfully or the case is not referred to mediation.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from termination of mediation / notice of non-referral
rules.legal_concept: Public office response deadline in Court of Claims proceeding
rules.source_language: Within ten business days after the termination of the mediation or the notification to the court that the case was not referred to mediation
rules.notes: Config Home parameter with fixed 10-business-day count (statute fixes the number; city does not fill it). This is a hard statutory deadline within the administrative review path, distinct from the soft 'promptly' processing standard.

rules.atomic_rule: Not later than seven business days after receiving the response (or motion to dismiss), the special master shall submit a report and recommendation; the period may be extended by an additional seven business days for good cause.
rules.trigger: The special master receives the public office's response or motion to dismiss.
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from receipt of the response, extendable by 7 additional business-days
rules.legal_concept: Special master report and recommendation deadline
rules.source_language: Not later than seven business days after receiving the response, or motion to dismiss the complaint, if applicable ... may extend the seven-day period for the submission of the report and recommendation to the court of claims under this division by an additional seven business days

rules.atomic_rule: Either party may object to the special master's report and recommendation within seven business days after receiving it.
rules.trigger: A party receives the special master's report and recommendation.
rules.clock_spec: 7 business-days from receipt of the report and recommendation
rules.legal_concept: Objection period to special master report
rules.source_language: Either party may object to the report and recommendation within seven business days after receiving the report and recommendation

rules.atomic_rule: A person allegedly aggrieved by a failure to comply with the Public Records Act may commence a mandamus action to compel the public office to comply with its obligations.
rules.trigger: A requester elects to pursue a court remedy after an alleged denial/failure.
rules.legal_concept: Mandamus to compel compliance
rules.source_language: the person allegedly aggrieved may commence a mandamus action to obtain a judgment that orders the public office or the person responsible for the public record to comply with division (B) of this section
rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification (verbatim wording of (C)(1) not cleanly captured)
rules.notes: Namespaced appeal.judicial (court-review path) distinct from the Court of Claims administrative alternative (OH-0028). Only the trigger/path is kept; the statutory damages and attorney-fee remedies in (C)(2) are excluded per the Remove list. Confirm verbatim (C)(1).

rules.atomic_rule: A public office need not permit a person incarcerated pursuant to a criminal conviction to inspect or copy a record concerning a criminal investigation or prosecution unless the sentencing judge (or successor) finds the information is necessary to support what appears to be a justiciable claim of the person.
rules.trigger: An incarcerated person requests a record concerning a criminal investigation or prosecution.
rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated-requester screening for criminal records
rules.source_language: unless the request to inspect or to obtain a copy of the record is for the purpose of acquiring information that is subject to release as a public record under this section and the judge who imposed the sentence or made the adjudication with respect to the person, or the judge's successor in office, finds that the information sought in the public record is necessary to support what appears to be a justiciable claim of the person.
rules.notes: A distinct processing branch (requester status + record type gate requiring a judicial finding). Requires human legal review before automating the justiciable-claim determination.

structural_branches.description: Before asking a requester for a written request, identity, or intended use, the engine must present a disclosure that all three are optional and may be declined (R.C. 149.43(B)(5)).
On an ambiguous/overly-broad denial, the engine must branch into a revise-opportunity state that informs the requester how records are maintained and accessed (R.C. 149.43(B)(2)).
When exempt content is redacted, the engine must attach a redaction notice to the requester or render the redaction plainly visible (R.C. 149.43(B)(9)).
A written non-commercial-use certification is a branch that lifts the ten-per-month delivery cap (R.C. 149.43(B)(7)).
Service of a complaint opens a 3-business-day cure state before the requester may proceed to mandamus or the Court of Claims (R.C. 149.43(C)(1)).
Ohio-specific expedited review path: Court of Claims complaint -> mandatory mediation -> office response -> special master report -> objections, distinct from ordinary court action (R.C. 2743.75).
A mandatory mediation stage the special master must open immediately upon assignment, before any adjudication (R.C. 2743.75(E)).
The alternative court path — a mandamus action to compel compliance — that a requester may elect instead of the Court of Claims route (R.C. 149.43(C)(1)).
A status+record-type gate: incarcerated-person requests for criminal investigation/prosecution records route to a sentencing-judge justiciable-claim finding before release (R.C. 149.43(B)(8)).

material_negatives.note: Ohio sets NO fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline. The only processing timing standards are the soft 'promptly' (inspection) and 'within a reasonable period of time' (copies) in R.C. 149.43(B)(1), captured as soft-standard rules OH-0007 and OH-0008. No day-count for acknowledgment exists.
R.C. 149.43(B)(3) requires a written denial explanation for written requests but attaches NO numeric deadline to providing it. Absence of a found day-count is not proof none exists elsewhere.
The opportunity-to-revise duty (R.C. 149.43(B)(2)) carries no statutory clock — no deadline by which the office must offer revision or the requester must respond.

Ohio has no fixed 'silence for N days = denial' trigger. A failure to respond within a reasonable time may be treated as a denial for mandamus/Court-of-Claims purposes, but the statute states no numeric constructive-denial day count.

No statewide statutory per-page copy rate. R.C. 149.43(B)(1) sets only an 'at cost'/actual-cost ceiling (OH-0018); the city fills in the operative rate. (Older R.C. 149.43(B)(1) practice historically referenced actual cost; no fixed cents-per-page in statute.)
R.C. 149.43(B)(6) permits requiring advance payment of the full cost but sets no partial-deposit percentage or threshold above which prepayment may be demanded.

No explicit statutory duty to forward a misdirected request to the correct office/custodian. The duty is stated as resting on the office or 'person responsible for public records' (OH-0013); routing/forwarding is not statutorily prescribed.

No statutory requirement to log/track requests or assign tracking numbers for an individual request under R.C. 149.43. (A public-records policy is required at the office level but tracking of individual requests is not mandated.)

rules.legal_concept: Universal right of public inspection and copying
rules.atomic_rule: All public records are open for personal inspection and copying by any person, except records specifically exempted by court order or by law; no requester qualification is imposed for general access.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for personal inspection and copying, except those which by order of a court of this state or by law are specifically exempted from disclosure. Records shall be maintained by agencies to the extent and in the manner required by Article 5 of this chapter.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with shared key per prompt discipline #2. Reinforced by 50-18-71(b)(1)(B): 'any person may make photographic copies.' Verbatim from opened official State of Georgia PDF; core provision confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for general records access
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose to obtain general public records; a purpose/'need' showing is required only for enumerated special record types (e.g., motor vehicle accident reports).
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The general right in O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)-(b) imposes no purpose requirement; a 'need' showing is imposed only for specific record types (see O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(5), motor vehicle accident reports, which defines 'need' by enumerated categories).
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrase: the general no-purpose rule is stated by absence, and the enumerated 'need' requirement for accident reports is the exception that proves it. Emitted as a rule with shared key per discipline #2, never a negative. Manual verification of the general/no-purpose reading recommended.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no Georgia residency or citizenship condition on the right to request public records; the right runs to any person.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The Open Records Act conditions access on the record's public status, not the requester's residency; no residency or citizenship qualification appears in O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 or § 50-18-71.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Paraphrase (stated by absence). Emitted as a rule with shared key per discipline #2. Manual verification recommended.

rules.legal_concept: Request may be made orally or in writing
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be made to the custodian orally or in writing; an oral request is a valid intake path (though it does not unlock the statutory enforcement remedies — see GA-0007).
rules.trigger: Request submitted to custodian
rules.source_language: A request made pursuant to this article may be made to the custodian of a public record orally or in writing.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim from opened official PDF.

rules.legal_concept: Agency option to require written requests to a designated officer
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may (but is not obligated to) require that all written requests be directed to a designated official chosen from an enumerated list (director/chair/CEO, senior satellite official, designated records custodian clerk, or designated open records officer).
rules.trigger: Agency elects to require directed written requests
rules.source_language: An agency may, but shall not be obligated to, require that all written requests be made upon the responder's choice of one of the following: the agency's director, chairperson, or chief executive officer, however denominated; the senior official at any satellite office of an agency; a clerk specifically designated by an agency as the custodian of agency records; or a duly designated open records officer of an agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #1 (custodian designation / routing). Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Agency must accept written requests by e-mail or facsimile
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall permit receipt of written requests by e-mail or facsimile in addition to other approved methods, provided the agency uses e-mail or facsimile in the normal course of its business.
rules.trigger: Agency uses e-mail or facsimile in normal course of business
rules.source_language: An agency shall permit receipt of written requests by e-mail or facsimile transmission in addition to any other methods of transmission approved by the agency, provided such agency uses e-mail or facsimile in the normal course of its business.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Statutory enforcement/penalties available only for written requests
rules.atomic_rule: The enforcement and penalty provisions (§§ 50-18-73 and 50-18-74) are available only when the request was made in writing consistent with subsection (b); they are unavailable for oral requests. This classifies whether a request is enforcement-eligible.
rules.trigger: Request was made orally vs. in writing
rules.source_language: The enforcement provisions of Code Sections 50-18-73 and 50-18-74 shall be available only to enforce compliance and punish noncompliance when a written request is made consistent with this subsection and shall not be available when such request is made orally.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Included because it changes request classification (enforcement-eligible flag), not merely the remedy amount.

rules.legal_concept: Open records officer designation, notice, and website posting
rules.atomic_rule: An agency that designates one or more open records officers shall make the designation in writing, immediately provide notice of them to any person on request (orally or in writing), notify the county legal organ, and, if it has a website, prominently display the designation.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to designate an open records officer
rules.source_language: Any agency that designates one or more open records officers upon whom requests for inspection or copying of records may be delivered shall make such designation in writing and shall immediately provide notice to any person upon request, orally or in writing, of those open records officers. If the agency has elected to designate an open records officer, the agency shall so notify the legal organ of the county in which the agency's principal offices reside and, if the agency has a website, shall also prominently display such designation on the agency's website.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #1. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Absence of designated officer may not delay the response
rules.atomic_rule: The absence or unavailability of the designated agency officer or employee may not be permitted to delay the agency's response to a request.
rules.trigger: Designated officer/employee absent or unavailable
rules.source_language: provided, however, that the absence or unavailability of the designated agency officer or employee shall not be permitted to delay the agency's response.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Constrains routing so a single designee cannot toll the response clock.

rules.legal_concept: Three-day clock start when agency requires requests to a designee
rules.atomic_rule: Where an agency requires that requests be directed to designated individuals, the three-day response period does not begin to run until the request is made in writing upon such individuals.
rules.trigger: Agency has elected to require directed requests; request delivered to a required designee
rules.clock_spec: 3 business-day response clock does not start until written request is delivered to the required designated individual
rules.source_language: In the event an agency requires that requests be made upon the individuals identified in subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) of this subsection, the three-day period for response to a written request shall not begin to run until the request is made in writing upon such individuals.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Defines the start event for the GA-0011 clock; only applies when the agency has invoked GA-0005.

rules.legal_concept: Three business day production window
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall produce responsive records within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days of receipt of the request; the agency is not required to produce records that did not exist at the time of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request for existing records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Agencies shall produce for inspection all records responsive to a request within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days of receipt of a request; provided, however, that nothing in this chapter shall require agencies to produce records in response to a request if such records did not exist at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The window is a ceiling ('not to exceed'); the standard within it is 'a reasonable amount of time.' City sets its operative target under the 3-business-day ceiling. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Partial production of locatable records within the window
rules.atomic_rule: Where some but not all responsive records are available within three business days, the agency shall make available within that period those records that can be located and produced.
rules.trigger: Only some responsive records available within three business days
rules.clock_spec: 3 business-days from receipt of request (for the subset that can be located)
rules.source_language: In those instances where some, but not all, records are available within three business days, an agency shall make available within that period those records that can be located and produced.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Requires rolling/partial production rather than waiting for the full set.

rules.legal_concept: Description-and-timeline notice when records unavailable in three days
rules.atomic_rule: Where responsive records exist but are unavailable within three business days, the agency shall within that period provide the requester a description of the records and a timeline for when they will be available.
rules.trigger: Responsive records exist but cannot be produced within three business days
rules.clock_spec: notice due within 3 business-days of receipt of request
rules.source_language: In any instance where records are unavailable within three business days of receipt of the request, and responsive records exist, the agency shall, within such time period, provide the requester with a description of such records and a timeline for when the records will be available for inspection or copying and provide the responsive records or access thereto as soon as practicable.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. This row is the notice (description + timeline) due within 3 days; GA-0014 splits out the 'as soon as practicable' production duty that the same sentence carries.

rules.legal_concept: Soft-standard production deadline for delayed records
rules.atomic_rule: For records that could not be produced within three business days, the agency shall provide the responsive records or access to them as soon as practicable (a soft, undefined standard, not a fixed day count).
rules.trigger: Records described with a timeline under GA-0013
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as practicable" from receipt of request
rules.source_language: and provide the responsive records or access thereto as soon as practicable.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Soft-standard deadline per pilot #1: config_home structural, no invented day-count. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice citing specific exempting authority within three days
rules.atomic_rule: When an agency withholds all or part of a record, it shall notify the requester of the specific legal authority for the exemption by Code section, subsection, and paragraph within three business days (or, if search/retrieval is delayed, no later than three business days after retrieval).
rules.trigger: Agency withholds all or part of a requested record
rules.clock_spec: within 3 business-days of request, or within 3 business-days after retrieval where search/retrieval is delayed
rules.source_language: In any instance in which an agency is required to or has decided to withhold all or part of a requested record, the agency shall notify the requester of the specific legal authority exempting the requested record or records from disclosure by Code section, subsection, and paragraph within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days or in the event the search and retrieval of records is delayed pursuant to this subsection or pursuant to subparagraph (b)(1)(A) of this Code section, then no later than three business days after the records have been retrieved.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Required denial-notice content (section/subsection/paragraph cite) with an attached 3-business-day ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Hourly labor charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee's salary
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose a reasonable charge for search, retrieval, and redaction, but that charge shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Agency performs search, retrieval, or redaction
rules.source_language: In all other instances, the charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request; provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling basis: state caps the rate at the lowest-paid qualified employee's prorated salary; city supplies the actual dollar figure. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of labor is free
rules.atomic_rule: No labor charge may be made for the first quarter hour of search, retrieval, or redaction.
rules.trigger: Labor charge assessed
rules.source_language: provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Fixed statutory free increment of 15 minutes. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Copy charge capped at 10 cents per page
rules.atomic_rule: In addition to labor charges, an agency may charge for copying, not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents, or the actual cost of producing the copy for other document types.
rules.trigger: Agency produces paper copies
rules.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of $0.25... note: ceiling is $0.10/page for letter/legal; other sizes at actual cost. City supplies the operative per-page value under the cap. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic records charged at actual cost of media
rules.atomic_rule: For electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
rules.trigger: Agency produces records on electronic media
rules.source_language: In the case of electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Basis is actual cost of media (a fixed measured cost, not a discretionary rate). Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to use the most economical means of search and production
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall utilize the most economical means reasonably calculated to identify and produce responsive, nonexcluded documents.
rules.trigger: Agency conducts search and production
rules.source_language: An agency shall utilize the most economical means reasonably calculated to identify and produce responsive, nonexcluded documents.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Soft standard ('most economical means reasonably calculated') that constrains how labor charges accrue; structural, no numeric value. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Specific statutory fees supersede the general fee scheme
rules.atomic_rule: Where a specific fee for certified copies or other records is authorized or prescribed by law, that specific fee applies instead of the general search/retrieval/copy charges when such records are sought.
rules.trigger: Requested record is one for which a specific statutory fee is prescribed (e.g., certified copies)
rules.source_language: Where fees for certified copies or other copies or records are specifically authorized or otherwise prescribed by law, such specific fee shall apply when certified copies or other records to which a specific fee may apply are sought.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Routes certain record types to a different fee basis; branch, not a value. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate notice when costs will exceed $25
rules.atomic_rule: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.
rules.trigger: Estimated response costs will exceed $25.00
rules.clock_spec: estimate notice due within 3 business-days of receipt of request
rules.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $25.00 threshold is fixed by statute (city cannot change it), so it is a structural trigger, not a city-filled parameter. This row is the estimate-notice duty; GA-0023 splits out the deferral permission the same sentence carries. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Deferral of search/retrieval until requester agrees to pay estimate
rules.atomic_rule: The agency may defer search and retrieval until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs, unless the request already stated a willingness to pay an amount exceeding the search and retrieval costs.
rules.trigger: Cost estimate issued under GA-0022 and requester has not pre-committed to pay
rules.clock_spec: processing paused until requester agrees to pay the estimated costs
rules.source_language: and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A pause state pending cost agreement; the pre-commitment carve-out prevents the pause.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment may be required when estimate exceeds $500
rules.atomic_rule: Where the estimated production cost exceeds $500.00, the agency may insist on prepayment of the costs before beginning search, retrieval, review, or production.
rules.trigger: Estimated production cost exceeds $500.00
rules.clock_spec: processing paused pending prepayment when estimate exceeds $500.00
rules.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $500.00 threshold is fixed by statute; structural trigger. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment for future requests where prior costs unpaid
rules.atomic_rule: Where a requester has not paid costs lawfully incurred for a prior request, the agency may require prepayment for all future requests from that person until the prior costs are paid or the payment dispute is resolved.
rules.trigger: Requester has unpaid lawfully-incurred costs from a prior request
rules.clock_spec: future requests paused pending prepayment until prior costs paid or dispute resolved
rules.source_language: Whenever any person who has requested to inspect or copy a public record has not paid the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully incurred, an agency may require prepayment for compliance with all future requests for production of records from that person until the costs for the prior production of records have been paid or the dispute regarding payment resolved.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Requester-level state (delinquent) that gates future requests.

rules.legal_concept: Collection of agreed costs regardless of whether records are accepted
rules.atomic_rule: Where charges were lawfully estimated and agreed and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make records available, the agency may collect those charges (via tax/fee collection methods) regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts the records.
rules.trigger: Requester agreed to estimated costs, agency incurred them, and requester does not pay
rules.source_language: Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Affects billing/collection state of a request; included as a processing permission rather than a pure damages remedy.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may self-copy with portable devices at inspection
rules.atomic_rule: At the time of inspection, any person may make photographic copies or other electronic reproductions of the records using suitable portable devices brought to the place of inspection.
rules.trigger: Records made available for in-person inspection
rules.source_language: At the time of inspection, any person may make photographic copies or other electronic reproductions of the records using suitable portable devices brought to the place of inspection.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A no-fee self-copy path at inspection.

rules.legal_concept: Agency may provide copies in lieu of access when redaction needed
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may, in its discretion, provide copies of a record in lieu of providing access to the record when portions contain confidential information that must be redacted.
rules.trigger: Record contains confidential portions requiring redaction
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an agency may, in its discretion, provide copies of a record in lieu of providing access to the record when portions of the record contain confidential information that must be redacted.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A production-mode branch used to protect redacted originals.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create new reports, summaries, or compilations
rules.atomic_rule: No public officer or agency is required to prepare new reports, summaries, or compilations not in existence at the time of the request.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a record not in existence at time of request
rules.source_language: No public officer or agency shall be required to prepare new reports, summaries, or compilations not in existence at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Reinforced by the 'did not exist at the time of the request' clause in 50-18-71(b)(1)(A).

rules.legal_concept: Requester's choice of electronic/native/ASCII format
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may request that electronic records, data, or data fields be produced in the format in which the agency keeps them, or in a standard export format such as a flat-file ASCII format, if the agency's existing computer programs support such export; and the agency shall produce electronic copies or, if the requester prefers, printouts.
rules.trigger: Requester requests electronic records in a specified supported format
rules.source_language: A requester may request that electronic records, data, or data fields be produced in the format in which such data or electronic records are kept by the agency, or in a standard export format such as a flat file electronic American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) format, if the agency's existing computer programs support such an export format. In such instance, the data or electronic records shall be downloaded in such format onto suitable electronic media by the agency.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: No refusal because export/redaction requires query commands
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall not refuse to produce electronic records, data, or data fields on the ground that exporting or redacting requires inputting range, search, filter, or report commands, so long as those commands can be executed using existing programs the agency uses in the ordinary course of business.
rules.trigger: Production would require running query/filter/report commands in existing agency software
rules.source_language: An agency shall not refuse to produce such electronic records, data, or data fields on the grounds that exporting data or redaction of exempted information will require inputting range, search, filter, report parameters, or similar commands or instructions into an agency's computer system so long as such commands or instructions can be executed using existing computer programs that the agency uses in the ordinary course of business to access, support, or otherwise manage the records or data.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: Website access in lieu of copies; no refusal of data fields
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may provide access to records through a public website in lieu of separate printouts or copies, but if it receives a request for data fields it shall not refuse the responsive data on the ground that it is available through a website when the requester seeks the data in the electronic format in which it is kept.
rules.trigger: Records available through a public website; requester seeks data fields in native electronic format
rules.source_language: In lieu of providing separate printouts or copies of records or data, an agency may provide access to records through a website accessible by the public. However, if an agency receives a request for data fields, an agency shall not refuse to provide the responsive data on the grounds that the data is available in whole or in its constituent parts through a website if the requester seeks the data in the electronic format in which it is kept.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Bundles a permission (website in lieu) and a prohibition (no refusal of native data fields) from one provision.

rules.legal_concept: Private vendor arrangements must not limit public access
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency contracts with a private vendor to collect or maintain public records, the agency shall ensure the arrangement does not limit public access and that the vendor does not impede record access or the method of delivery established by the agency or by law.
rules.trigger: Agency uses a private vendor to collect or maintain public records
rules.source_language: if an agency contracts with a private vendor to collect or maintain public records, the agency shall ensure that the arrangement does not limit public access to those records and that the vendor does not impede public record access and method of delivery as established by the agency or as otherwise provided for in this Code section.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Relevant where a city routes records through a hosted/third-party system.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to redact narrowly and produce all nonexempt portions
rules.atomic_rule: Exemptions are interpreted narrowly to exclude only the portion of a record to which an exclusion is directly applicable, and the agency having custody has a duty to provide all other portions of the record for inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: A record contains both exempt and nonexempt portions
rules.source_language: This Code section shall be interpreted narrowly so as to exclude from disclosure only that portion of a public record to which an exclusion is directly applicable. It shall be the duty of the agency having custody of a record to provide all other portions of a record for public inspection or copying.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Reinforced by the narrow-construction mandate in 50-18-70(a).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory redaction of enumerated personal identifying information
rules.atomic_rule: Enumerated personal identifiers (e.g., social security number, financial/bank/credit-card/account data, personal e-mail or cell number, day and month of birth, medical/insurance information, and similar items) shall be redacted prior to disclosure of any requested record, subject to statutory exceptions.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains enumerated personal identifying information
rules.source_language: Records that reveal an individual's social security number, mother's birth name, credit card information, debit card information, bank account information, account number, utility account number, password used to access his or her account, financial data or information, insurance or medical information in all records, unlisted telephone number if so designated in a public record, personal e-mail address or cellular telephone number, day and month of birth ... Items exempted by this subparagraph shall be redacted prior to disclosure of any record requested pursuant to this article.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim (operative clause; full identifier list abridged with ellipsis, exceptions in (20)(B) not reproduced). A parallel public-employee PII redaction rule appears at 50-18-72(a)(21). Drives a default redaction pass on production.

rules.legal_concept: Superior court enforcement action
rules.atomic_rule: The superior courts have jurisdiction in law and equity to entertain actions to enforce the Open Records Act; such actions may be brought by any person, firm, corporation, or other entity.
rules.trigger: Noncompliance with the Open Records Act (written request)
rules.source_language: The superior courts of this state shall have jurisdiction in law and in equity to entertain actions against persons or agencies having custody of records open to the public under this article to enforce compliance with the provisions of this article. Such actions may be brought by any person, firm, corporation, or other entity.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Georgia's review path is judicial (superior court); there is no statutory administrative appeal (see material negatives). Namespaced appeal.judicial per pilot #1.

rules.legal_concept: Attorney General enforcement authority
rules.atomic_rule: The Attorney General has discretionary authority to bring enforcement actions to compel compliance with the Open Records Act and to seek civil or criminal penalties or both.
rules.trigger: Alleged noncompliance; AG discretion
rules.source_language: In addition, the Attorney General shall have authority to bring such actions in his or her discretion as may be appropriate to enforce compliance with this article and to seek either civil or criminal penalties or both.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. The AG's office also runs an informal (non-statutory) mediation program for open-records disputes; the statutory authority is enforcement litigation, not a requester administrative appeal.

rules.legal_concept: Prohibition on destroying records to prevent disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: Persons or entities that destroy records for the purpose of preventing their disclosure under the Open Records Act may be prosecuted under O.C.G.A. § 45-11-1.
rules.trigger: Records destroyed for the purpose of preventing disclosure under the Act
rules.source_language: In addition, persons or entities that destroy records for the purpose of preventing their disclosure under this article may be subject to prosecution under Code Section 45-11-1.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Keeper-sliver #2 (preservation tied to a request/disclosure). Included as a preservation prohibition triggered by the disclosure context; the penalty amount itself is excluded as a criminal remedy. Verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: 90 business day window for University System intercollegiate athletics records
rules.atomic_rule: For records (other than nonclerical staff salary information) of intercollegiate sports programs of any University System of Georgia unit, the period for any production, access, response, or notice is 90 business days from the date the agency received the request.
rules.trigger: Request is for intercollegiate sports program records of a University System of Georgia unit
