rules.clock_spec: fixed: 90 business-days from date agency received the request
rules.source_language: Any other provision of this Code section to the contrary notwithstanding, the period within which any production, access, response, or notice is required from an agency with respect to a request for records, other than salary information for nonclerical staff, of intercollegiate sports programs of any unit of the University System of Georgia, including athletic departments and related private athletic associations, shall be 90 business days from the date the agency received the request.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Applicability limit: University System of Georgia athletics only, NOT municipal agencies. Included for cross-state overlap value (record-type-specific extended deadline); a city platform would rarely hit it. Record-Specific authority scope.

rules.legal_concept: Civil litigant requests must be in writing and copied to agency counsel
rules.atomic_rule: Requests by civil litigants for records sought for use in ongoing civil or administrative litigation against the agency shall be made in writing and copied to the agency's counsel of record contemporaneously; the agency shall provide duplicate sets of produced records to that counsel at no cost unless counsel declines.
rules.trigger: Requester is a civil litigant seeking records for use in ongoing litigation against the agency
rules.source_language: Requests by civil litigants for records that are sought as part of or for use in any ongoing civil or administrative litigation against an agency shall be made in writing and copied to counsel of record for that agency contemporaneously with their submission to that agency. The agency shall provide, at no cost, duplicate sets of all records produced in response to the request to counsel of record for that agency unless the counsel of record for that agency elects not to receive the records.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A requester-type routing/notice branch (copy-to-counsel + duplicate-set delivery).

rules.legal_concept: Reverse-FOIA notice and hold for records claimed as trade secrets
rules.atomic_rule: Where a submitter has attached a trade-secret affidavit to records, the agency shall notify the submitter before producing them; if the agency determines the information is not a trade secret it shall notify the submitter of its intent to disclose within ten days unless barred by court order (the submitter may then sue to prevent disclosure).
rules.trigger: Records responsive to a request bear a submitter's trade-secret affidavit under Article 27 of Chapter 1 of Title 10
rules.clock_spec: 10 days notice of intent to disclose to the submitting entity before release
rules.source_language: If such entity attaches such an affidavit, before producing such records in response to a request under this article, the agency shall notify the entity of its intention to produce such records as set forth in this paragraph. If the agency makes a determination that the specifically identified information does not in fact constitute a trade secret, it shall notify the entity submitting the affidavit of its intent to disclose the information within ten days unless prohibited from doing so by an appropriate court order.
rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim (operative clauses). A distinct third-party-notice/hold workflow that can pause production pending the submitter's court action. Flag for human legal review on the trade-secret determination.

material_negatives.note: No separate statutory acknowledgment/receipt deadline distinct from substantive response. Georgia's three-business-day period (50-18-71(b)(1)(A)) is a production/response ceiling, not a mere acknowledgment obligation; there is no standalone 'acknowledge within N days' rule.

No statutory deemed/constructive-denial trigger (no 'silence for N days = denial'). Georgia enforcement is judicial and turns on noncompliance/no substantial justification (50-18-73), not an automatic terminal clock. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statutory administrative appeal to a state ombudsman or records authority. Review is judicial (superior court, 50-18-73) plus discretionary Attorney General enforcement; the AG's mediation program is informal and non-statutory.
No statutory clarification/narrowing clock and no requester-clarification-then-abandonment (nonresponse-abandonment) mechanism in the Open Records Act.
No statewide statutory requirement to maintain a public request log or assign tracking numbers for open records requests.

No statewide-mandated flat municipal copy or labor rate. The state supplies only ceilings (10 cents/page for letter/legal; lowest-paid qualified employee's prorated hourly salary for labor) and a fixed 15-minute free increment; the city fills in the operative values under those ceilings.

The Act counts in 'business days' for the core response window but does not codify a general holiday/weekend computation method or a rule for when receipt occurs (e.g., after-hours or weekend submissions); computation details are left unspecified. Manual verification / later AG-opinion pass recommended.

structural_branches.description: Optional open-records-officer regime: agency may designate officer(s) in writing, must publicize (county legal organ + website), and may require directed written requests (GA-0005/GA-0008).
Conditional clock-start fork: when the agency requires directed requests, the 3-business-day clock does not start until the written request reaches the required designee (GA-0010).
Delayed-records path: description + timeline notice within 3 business days, then production 'as soon as practicable' (soft standard) (GA-0013/GA-0014).

Cost-estimate/deferral branch at the fixed $25 threshold (estimate + optional deferral) and prepayment branch at the fixed $500 threshold, plus a delinquent-requester prepayment state (GA-0022/GA-0023/GA-0024/GA-0025).
Reverse-FOIA hold: third-party submitter notice, 10-day intent-to-disclose window, and potential submitter court action before release (GA-0041).
Civil-litigant routing: written request copied to agency counsel and duplicate record sets delivered to counsel at no cost (GA-0040).
Judicial enforcement path in superior court, available only for written requests, brought by any person or by the Attorney General (GA-0036/GA-0037).
Record-type fork: 90-business-day response window for University System of Georgia intercollegiate athletics records, overriding the general 3-day rule (GA-0039) (non-municipal).
